### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **291 — the decision, and a machine named. PAID.** Wednesday the fifth. **Six hundred and forty-nine pence in and nothing out, the first money into that yard since the eleventh of April, on a private person's account and for a private person's purpose.** A man of about fifty-five hires the party to look under his own boat and says why out loud before he is asked: whether the thing along her starboard side is his or was there before he bought her. **He gets his answer inside his own hire — a cut in the rock about nine feet long and about two inches across, with dressed sides and square at both ends, about four feet under her starboard side, counted twice and not the property of anybody, and the yard cannot tell him whose it is and puts it in the first column because a man can go and look at it with a pan and a line — and he pays the whole of it without arguing with a figure and does not ask what it meant.** A man of sixty-one is asked for his boat and for nothing else and sets one condition, and **NAMES THE CROWN SEAL IN A SHED, in his own mouth, because he has seen one: a round of glass in a collar with a wheel and a screw, in a bed cut in a sill, the mark of its name cut into the round — a machine and a seal at once, and a term and not a lock, and nobody in this country ever looks at one.** The yard does not enter the word in the first column. **The price of a descent is named out loud before anybody agrees to it at fourteen marks, three shillings and fourpence, and the yard cannot pay it, and the day goes off a book at Ternwatch because a man of sixty-one asked for it, and the holder of that writ says out loud that he has a rule about a man this yard has paid and none about a man this yard is being paid by.** And at four o'clock, before anybody has agreed to anything, **the letting is decided and its price is named: this yard will not read the chamber and will not take one piece out of it, and the only proof it will ever have of anything about a drowned city will be in a thing that closed.**
2. **292 — the working day. PAID.** Thursday the sixth, a rota day, **the forty-fourth charge, walked on none.** The book sends Amos Searle and the yard says no out loud, and the second name comes at the same figure. **The pot is down twenty past eight and up half past eleven at about seventy fathoms, and the gauge reads eighty-four pounds and the mark is not moved.** **A cut face of thirty feet with a doorway in it, a sill with a bed and, under the lip, a rebate; a plate of glass in the bed and not in the rebate; the bed empty; two hundred and nine marks in the sill, counted three times, and a day cut beside them, being the eleventh of May.** Nobody goes in. **He loses the afternoon and writes the day's entry himself, slowly.**
3. **293 — the round, and the storm. PAID.** Friday the seventh, **the far bench occupied from ten until four and not approached.** The reason for going again is said out loud at eight in the morning: **the plate goes into the rebate on the eleventh, and a plate the width of a doorway does not come down on a stone floor and stay off it.** **A round of glass comes up out of the bed with a chain of eleven stamped links on it and a date on every link, and a piece of worked glass bedded in it that will not come away.** It goes on the crown under a tarpaulin and **not into the shed, because the second clause of the notice of the thirty-first keeps recovered transparent mineral out of every shed.** Then the weather: **the skylight, the door light, a pane of plate, two boats' running glass, eleven windows and the lens of the mole-head light, and about a hundred people in the rain and nobody hurt, and no cause named for it in any volume.**
4. **294 — the injury, in three parts. PAID.** Saturday the eighth. **A pane of plate goes over on the crown of that mole across the RIGHT hand of a man of sixty-one, edge first, once.** A bonesetter of sixty who **does not say no** sets it, gives the figure and the date, and will not hear a word about who brought him: **a mark and four shillings, two hundred and eight pence.** **He is not on the water until the second of June and the north bar job is not going to happen, and his boat of about nineteen tons, which he built himself fifty years ago or near it, has taken a stove in the weather and is in eleven pieces on that mole.** He is not thanked and is not going to be.
5. **295 — the accounting, and a figure that comes back. PAID.** Sunday the ninth. **Four marks and a shilling to a glazier for two lights and a skylight, which is the whole of the glass this yard owns in that harbor.** **A man of sixty-one brings his own account of the weather up the steps unasked, in his own book, four streets off, on a page that is not on top of this yard's.** And **the figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks, which has had no subject since the seventh of April, comes back at forty-three pence on a bag of five hundred and ninety-seven, and the chapter says it came back and not that anybody is going to pay it.**
6. **296 — the concealment, in a room with two people in it. PAID.** Monday the tenth, **the wall comes down bare for the fifty-third time and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the forty-fifth.** **The Oren mark is told once and once only, in her room, to her, and told twice because she sets that as the price, and the first time it was told it was nine seconds in a shed in a voice he could not have repeated.** Four things she will not do, and will not forgive him, and cannot do again. **Neither of them calls it a reunion.**
7. **297 — the letting. PAID.** Tuesday the eleventh, **the wage Tuesday: the column does not move and twenty-nine weeks have fallen due; the far bench occupied from ten until four.** **The round is carried down the mole steps in the open air in front of about nine people, stands in two hands on the stone, and is not put back, and the sentence is: the chamber closes whether it is read or not, and we are letting it close.** And: **that is not a surrender and it is not a proof, and nobody in that boat is going to say this yard was right about it, because it does not know.** At a quarter past two **the plate goes down into the rebate and is not coming up and nothing is holding it up**, and nobody in the boat saw the beginning of it and a man in a boat could see the end of it, **and that is what a figure cut in a sill is for.**
8. **298 — a consequence, a lead, a seal and a loss. PAID.** Wednesday the twelfth. **A lead of about fourteen pounds marked at every fathom and a slate with no name on it, and the whole of that sill entered in the first column in about nine minutes by anybody with a lead.** Then alone on the crown, **the eleven stamped links, and a seal line on the last of them read through a flat piece of glass so as not to scratch at it: *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, senior Registry examiner* — dated in the chain and older than the collar of the same office, and a difference in two made things says nothing about which is right.** **HE IS IN NO ROOM.** And at half past two **he cannot say one of the nine lines of the order, and she reads them off the sheet in the drawer in ninety seconds and he has them again, and a thing relearned is not a thing remembered, and the record outlives the man.**
9. **299 — the two marks, a name, and three true things. PAID.** Thursday the thirteenth, **the cistern charged and walked on none, being the forty-sixth; the far bench occupied from ten until four.** **The two marks four hundred yards apart: this yard's own, fouled about a foot and a half where it was four inches in March, and one with a shackle of a make nobody in that harbor makes, whose season of nine marks is not paid and is not going to be asked for.** A man of sixty-one looks at it from ten feet off the bottom for four minutes and refuses to say either of the two things he could say. **The name at the head of the third column is said out loud once in that boat and it is Mara Venn, and it is said once and not again.** Then three statements about **the sill, the round and the room**, all three true, all three different, and none of them Chapter 290's words, marks and house.
10. **300 — the close. PAID.** Friday the fourteenth. **The read-back: thirty-two entries in the first column at the hour of it and thirty-three at the close; a hundred and twelve lines in the second at the hour of it and a hundred and fifteen at the close; none in the third, with the boy's hand at the head of it; twenty-four in the fourth at the read-back and twenty-five at the close, the last of them the last thing in that book.** **The thirteen things**, read out in the flat voice she uses for a column and entered without addition, of which **the fourth is the seal line and the fact that no such person is in a room, and the thirteenth is the poverty**: a working harbor poorer on the fourteenth of May than on the twenty-third of February, the four returns four and no fifth, five drawers five drawers, the plate in eleven feet with its note open, the forty marks twice, the wage column standing, and two hundred and sixty-one pence in a drawer on a mole. And then **a round of glass going up that coast in a drawer in a woman's hand on the eighteenth** — the round that came out of the bed beside the plate, and not a piece of the plate, the two having been separate objects from the seventh of May onward — and her forty marks not reduced and not paid.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 300

- **Calder and Mara Venn.** **She is the one who named the word on the twenty-fifth of April, and the one who said the third of the three true things on the fourth of May, and the one the name in the third column belongs to, and she was not in the room for the reading on the twenty-ninth and was not asked to be. On the tenth of May he told her the Oren mark, once, in a room with nobody else in it, and he said it twice because she made the price of it, and she said four things she would not do and one thing she cannot do again, and neither of them called it a reunion. On the fourteenth the round of glass went into a drawer in her hand and it did not buy a shilling of her forty marks. He does not get to be thanked and she is not going to forgive him and she is not going to be able to do it again.**
- **Calder and Nessa Pike.** **She is the one who made him say the letting out loud so that it would be a record, and who made him say the thirteen, and who read the nine lines back to him off a sheet in ninety seconds and told him what the loss was. She has four stitches in a right hand and writes in her left. She said the first of the three true things in Chapter 299 about the sill, and she has still not said one word about the cost to the yard of anything in these ten days, and the ledger is in her hand and the ledger is what the ten days are.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **He was asked for a boat and not for knowledge, he set one condition, he did not want to be thanked, he named the Crown Seal because he has seen one, he was not asked one question about the stair, he paid for the day's plant and air in his own name, he kept his own account of the storm in his own book and brought it up unasked, he is hurt in the right hand and a boat he built himself is in eleven pieces on that mole, and he did useful work afterwards by looking at a shackle from ten feet off the bottom and refusing to say either of the two things he could say about it.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on three of the ten days, being the seventh, the eleventh and the thirteenth, and not at any hour on the other seven; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story; **the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** Nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift.
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it with a name set beside it that is not his and not the holder's, **and that name was said out loud once on the thirteenth of May, in a boat, and it is not going to be said again.** He was not put on anything and was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and no name of his is in any column of that book.
- **Calder and Elias Voke.** **Untouched and unasked, for the fifth time.** The six fathoms of his gear are still flat on a course of cut stone at forty fathoms under a lead, and the season of his mark is nine marks and is not paid, and he was not in the boat on the sixth and he was not in the boat on the thirteenth.
- **Calder and the four people of that coast.** **Untouched and unasked, for the fifth time, with a fifth reason written out loud: that this yard has now read the sill of a chamber of that kind at seventy fathoms in its own ground is not a reason to ask them. The complaint was not raised. The limit they wrote and signed stands and the holder did not ask to have it lifted once in these ten days.**

### The power state

**LINE DIVER. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN VOLUME 06 AND NONE IN THIS BATCH. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, NOT IMPROVED AND NOT RENAMED. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED, AND ITS SEASON OF NINE MARKS IS NOT PAID.** What this batch paid is the cost of the perception in ordinary work, once, on the sixth, in the second column with a reason and no name in it: **an afternoon on the crown of that mole, and the day's own entry written by him in his own right hand, slowly, in about twenty minutes, with nobody helping him.** **And what it also paid, separately, and NOT to the condition, is a permanent loss of a portion of that man's own recall on the twelfth of May, in the second column with a date against it and a reason against the line and no name in it, and there is no figure for it because there is no figure for it.** A strike on a link and a strike on a collar are both differences and neither is a truth.

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** One afternoon lost to it, being the sixth of May, in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure. **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, still nameless, not struck out, and in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is one mark, eight shillings and fivepence, being two hundred and sixty-one pence**, and it was five marks, one shilling and fourpence, being eight hundred and sixteen pence, on the fourth. The whole of what came in in the ten days is **six hundred and forty-nine pence on the fifth of May only**, and **the whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past is now two thousand four hundred and nine pence, and the figure of one thousand seven hundred and sixty the four state files carried is withdrawn and named as withdrawn here.** The whole of what went out in the ten days is **one thousand two hundred and four pence, being two hundred and eight to a bonesetter, six hundred and sixty to a glazier, and a mark and eightpence twice for a boat and a man in her**, and **not one penny of the twenty-eight marks, six shillings and eightpence of plant and air on the sixth and the seventh went out of this yard at all.** The whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December past is **thirteen thousand nine hundred and five pence in twenty-seven transactions at ten counters.**
- **The figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks came back on the ninth of May at forty-three pence, being three shillings and sevenpence, with a subject, and the page says it came back and not that it was paid, and it is not paid. It stands at three hundred and seventy-nine pence at the close, being two marks, four shillings and eleven pence.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-NINE weeks have fallen due with no envelope, the last of them being the twenty-ninth, which fell due on Tuesday the eleventh of May; the next is Tuesday the eighteenth for the thirtieth week and the column will not move on it.** There was one wage Tuesday in these ten days and the column did not move on it.
- **The slate wall came down bare once, the fifty-third, on Monday the tenth, the counter not restarting, the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting held in that room on any day of this yard's life.** The cistern was charged on three rota days and walked on none of them, being the forty-fourth, the forty-fifth and the forty-sixth, and no figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the seventh, the eleventh and the thirteenth, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of them.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for the hundred and third night. The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and thirty-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved.**
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY, AND A FORM OF AN OFFICE THAT YARD DOES NOT BELONG TO IS ON A STEP TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, AND A PAPER WITH A SEAL ON IT IS UNDER A BED IN THIS HARBOR, AND A COPY OF A DROWNED CITY IS IN A DRAWER IN THAT SHED, AND A ROUND OF GLASS IS GOING UP THAT COAST IN A DRAWER IN A HAND THAT IS NOT THAT YARD'S. NONE OF THE FOUR IS A KEEPER AND ALL FOUR ARE, AND THERE IS NO HANDLE ON THE INSIDE OF ANY OF THEM.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April past. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved, nobody sent. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, he not asked anything, the chest not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed. **Nine feet of chain on a nail in that shed wall and a bar of square iron in the drawer, neither sold nor given away, and nobody has asked whose either is.**
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IS NOT A REGISTRY AND IS NOT A COURT AND IS NOT A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH PAST AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS BATCH, AND ITS FOUR LINES ARE ABOUT A RECORD AND NOT ABOUT A HOUSE, AND THIS YARD DID NOT LOOK IN ONE OF THE FOUR DRAWERS IT CANNOT LOOK IN AND WROTE TO NOBODY. THE OLD EVIDENCE CHAIN IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT AND THE TWO ARE NOT FUSED ON ANY PAGE.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch, all thirteen of them, and the list of thirteen is in `state/chapter-summaries.md` § *Volume 06, Batch 0005*, Chapter 300:** a chamber that closes with a figure and a day a man can look at before it happens; a letting decided in advance with its price named first; a glass storm with no cause named; a working day's plant and air bought off a real book at the same figure and paid for by a man rather than by a yard; an injury in three parts with a real bill, a real absence and a real consequence; a permanent loss out of a man's own recall with no figure for it; the Crown Seal named as a machine and as a term and not a lock; a seal of a Registry examiner on the old evidence chain, dated in the chain and older than the office that made it, on a line, in no room; **the Crown's history exposed as incomplete and not as false**; a proof that is physical and labor-based and about half unreadable; the concealment told once, in a room, at a price, with nobody calling it a reunion; a name said out loud once that is neither the boy's nor the holder's; and a harbor poorer on the last page than on the first.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY ANY LATER CHAPTER:** the plate at the fifth seam and its open note; the case of five bells and the limit four people of that coast wrote; the delayed note at eleven and two; the lead plug and the chest and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the certificate of method, whose standing in a market was spent on the twenty-second of April and is not restored; **the form on a step two days down that coast, which no later chapter may say was withdrawn or unserved**; **the Quietening, named once, in Chapter 281, and not named again in any of the fifty chapters**; **and the new-volume question, asked on the third of May and not answered in eleven days, which no chapter of this volume may answer and which no later volume may answer out of this one's material.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: THE ANSWER ABOUT A DROWNED CITY TURNED OUT TO BE AT SEVENTY FATHOOMS UNDER THIS MOLE, AND IT WAS FOUND BY PEOPLE WHO WERE NOT LOOKING FOR IT, AND IT WAS NOT READ, AND A GLASS STORM WENT THROUGH A HARBOR IN ABOUT SIX HOURS, AND A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE HAS TWO STITCHES IN A RIGHT HAND AND ELEVEN PIECES OF A BOAT ON A MOLE, AND A MAN OF THIRTY-TWO CANNOT SAY NINE LINES HE CARRIED IN HIS OWN HEAD, AND A WARD OF TWO AND A HALF HAS TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE PENCE IN A DRAWER, AND A HARBOR IS POORER.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0005 summary (Chapters 291–300) — the story state at the end of Chapter 300

**MOVEMENT 5 IS WRITTEN AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX, AND IT IS A CHOICE AND NOT A VICTORY.** In ten days a yard that had five marks and one shilling in a drawer earned six hundred and forty-nine pence from a stranger, bought two days of plant and air off a book four hundred miles off on a man's name and not on its own, went down to about seventy fathoms twice off the south end of its own mole, found a doorway in a cut face with a sill carrying a bed, a rebate, two hundred and nine marks and a day, took a round of glass with a chain of eleven stamped links out of the floor of the room behind a plate that had nothing behind it, caused six hours of weather it will never name, cost a man of sixty-one his right hand and his boat, decided in advance and out loud that it would not read the chamber, let the plate go into the rebate on the eleventh, could not say nine lines it had carried in its own head, told a woman of no office the thing it had kept since the middle of November, said a name out loud once, and closed its own book on a leaf with thirty-three entries, a hundred and fifteen lines, an empty column and twenty-five lines, and a bag with two hundred and sixty-one pence in it.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT IS CHAPTER 296 AND ITS CLIMAX IS CHAPTERS 297 AND 298, WHICH ARE ONE EVENT: THE LETTING AND WHAT IT COST.** The chapters before 296 are the decision, the working day, the round, the hand and the accounting. Chapter 296 is the concealment. Chapters 297 and 298 are the letting, the closing, the lead and the slate, the seal on the chain, and the loss. Chapter 299 is the two marks, the name and the three true things. Chapter 300 is the read-back, the thirteen, the whole standing inventory and the final chapter image.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY-NINE PENCE IN AND ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE OUT, so a net loss of five hundred and fifty-five pence; **twenty-eight marks, six shillings and eightpence, being four thousand five hundred and sixty pence, of plant and air that went on somebody else's book;** a wage column that did not move on the one wage Tuesday in the ten days and twenty-nine weeks fallen due; an afternoon lost to the body with no figure; a right hand, a bill of a mark and four shillings, an absence until the second of June and a boat in eleven pieces; a permanent loss of a portion of the holder's own recall with no figure; a glass storm with no cause named in it; a chamber closed and unread; and a round of glass going up a coast in a drawer in a hand that is not that yard's.**

**CONFLICTS FOUND AND HOW THEY WERE RESOLVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN DEFENDED:**

1. **THE HAND-OFF THAT DISPATCHED THIS BATCH COUNTED ALL THREE OF THE STANDING FIGURES WRONG AND SAID SO ON ITS OWN FACE, AND THE CHAPTERS FOLLOWED THE ANCHOR.** It counted three Mondays in a span that has one, four rota days in a span that has three, and two wage Tuesdays in a span that has one. **THERE IS ONE WALL WIPE, BEING THE FIFTY-THIRD ON MONDAY THE TENTH; THREE CISTERN CHARGES WALKED ON NONE, BEING THE FORTY-FOURTH, FORTY-FIFTH AND FORTY-SIXTH; AND ONE WAGE TUESDAY, BEING THE ELEVENTH, ON WHICH THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE, SO THE FIGURE THAT GOES FORWARD IS TWENTY-NINE WEEKS FALLEN DUE.** This is the second batch in a row whose hand-off mis-counted and it is recorded at `state/continuity.md` § *Batch 0005 as written*, item 1.3.
2. **THE WORD *QUIETENING* IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE WORDS *CROWN SEAL* ARE NAMED FIRST IN CHAPTER 291.** A scan of the ten chapters returns nothing for *quieten*, *orison*, *returning memory* and *panel*.
3. **THE MONEY RECONCILES IN ONE LINE: 816 + 649 − 1,204 = 261.** In: six hundred and forty-nine pence on the fifth of May, being three marks for a day's work at the standing rate, a mark and eightpence for a boat and a man in her, and a penny of line, on a private person's account and for a private person's purpose. Out: two hundred and eight to a bonesetter, six hundred and sixty to a glazier, and a mark and eightpence twice for a boat. **The whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past is two thousand four hundred and nine pence and not the one thousand seven hundred and sixty the four state files carried, and the withdrawn figure is named as withdrawn in all four.**
4. **THE DESCENT IS BOUGHT AND IT IS NOT PAID FOR BY THIS YARD, AND THAT IS THE BATCH'S OWN ARGUMENT APPLIED TO ITSELF.** The day is fourteen marks, three shillings and fourpence, the identical figure of the eighth, ninth, tenth and twenty-eighth of April, component for component, and the figure *dearer* remains withdrawn. **It went off a book at a pressure house at Ternwatch because a man of sixty-one asked for it, and the holder of that writ said out loud, before agreeing to it, that a man this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about and that he does not know what a man this yard is being paid by is.**
5. **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS CAME BACK WITH A SUBJECT ON THE NINTH OF MAY, AT FORTY-THREE PENCE, AND THE PAGE SAYS IT CAME BACK AND NOT THAT IT WAS PAID.** It is not paid and it stands at three hundred and seventy-nine pence at the close.
6. **THE GLASS STORM IS ON THE PAGE AND NO CAUSE IS NAMED FOR IT IN ANY VOLUME, AND IT IS IN TWO HANDS ON TWO PAGES THAT ARE NOT ON TOP OF EACHING.** No character's action in this batch is caused by it.
7. **THE LETTING IS A DECISION TAKEN IN ADVANCE WITH ITS PRICE NAMED IN THE SAME BREATH, AND IT IS CARRIED OUT ON THE ELEVENTH WITH NOBODY ASKED IN BETWEEN, AND THE SECOND HALF OF IT IS SAID OUT LOUD: it is not a surrender and it is not a proof, and nobody in that boat said this yard was right about it because it does not know.**
8. **THE CONCEALMENT IS TOLD ONCE, IN A ROOM, AT A PRICE SHE NAMED, AND NEITHER OF THEM CALLS IT A REUNION, AND HER FORTY MARKS ARE NOT REDUCED AND HER CERTIFICATE'S STANDING IN A MARKET IS NOT RESTORED AND HE IS NOT FORGIVEN AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE ABLE TO DO IT AGAIN.**
9. **NO OFFICE ANSWERS IN A ROOM, NO SENIOR EXAMINER IS A FACE, HALVEN ROOK IS NOWHERE, AND MAGISTER ILYA SERR IS A SEAL LINE ON TWO PAGES AND IN NO ROOM, ON NO MOLE, IN NO MARKET AND NOT IN THIS HARBOR.**
10. **NO ONE OF THE FOUR PEOPLE OF THAT COAST WAS ASKED FOR ANYTHING, THE COMPLAINT WAS NOT RAISED, AND THE FACT THAT THIS YARD HAS NOW READ THE SILL OF A CHAMBER OF THAT KIND AT SEVENTY FATHOOMS IN ITS OWN GROUND IS NOT A REASON TO ASK THEM AND WAS NOT USED AS ONE.**
11. **THE BOY AND THE THIRD COLUMN DID NOT MOVE, EXCEPT THAT THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF IT WAS SAID OUT LOUD ONCE ON THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY, AND IT IS NEITHER THE BOY'S NOR THE HOLDER'S, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO BE SAID AGAIN.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 280

**MOVEMENT 3 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. A FORM WITH A NAME AND AN ADDRESS ON IT HAS BEEN PUT IN THE ORDINARY POST AND SERVED BY BEING LEFT, AND THE PRICE OF THAT IS A MAN'S AFTERNOON AND A MAN'S DAY AND A SEASON'S PEACE, AND NONE OF THAT PRICE BELONGS TO THIS YARD. AND A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE SAID A THING OUT LOUD IN A FISH MARKET IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING AND IT COST HER THE STANDING OF A CERTIFICATE OF METHOD IN A MARKET, AND THE CERTIFICATE CANNOT BE WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OFFICE TO TAKE IT FROM. AND THE PRICE OF THE VOLUME'S OWN SOLUTION IS NOW SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM, AND THE SOMEBODY IS AT THE END OF A STALL IN THIS HARBOR, AND IS NOT FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST UNDER SEVENTY FATHOMS.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **271 — the undertaking broken, and four lines. PAID.** Thursday the fifteenth of April. The thirty-eighth charge, walked on none. **Calder Marr breaks the three things he said on Wednesday the fourteenth out loud in that shed before nine and gives one reason, which is that a form exists and that a yard which does not answer a letter is an address that answers nothing, and an address is an address.** Four unsigned lines go into the post at a penny, and **the fourth line is five words: *I am asking you. Not the yard***, and she reads that line eleven times and the three above it not once.
2. **272 — the person of no office, and the line of the fourth of April. PAID.** Friday the sixteenth. **MARA VENN IS A PERSON OF NO OFFICE, THIRTY, OF THIS HARBOR, AND HAS BEEN SINCE THE FOURTH OF JANUARY PAST, AND THE GEOGRAPHY CONFLICT IS SETTLED ON THE PAGE AND NOT BY INVENTION: the second column's line of the fourth of April which said her letter came four days up that coast IS WRONG, IS NOT STRUCK OUT, and has the correction written against it, and the reason she gives is that a yard which strikes out its own line because it was wrong is a yard which has decided that a wrong line is not a record.** She puts **a form** on the bench — particulars of material held as unsettled, five ruled lines, one filled in with a name and a house in a town two days down that coast, a foot that says served and has nothing after it, and **a seal line with Halven Rook's name on it, entered in the first column because a name on a piece of paper is a thing a man can go and look at.** She **refuses to name the young man who filled in the first line**, and it is entered as refused and not as not-asked. **She has had the sheet eleven weeks, since the fourth of January, and cannot put it in a drawer, cannot burn it, cannot post it and cannot hand it to a yard, and those are four things and she has tried three.**
3. **273 — the four lines, and the mark. PAID.** Saturday the seventeenth. The mark, thirty-six days on it, a foot and three-quarters and two inches, the shackle found with a thumb. Four hundred and eighty pence out. **THE DISCOVERY: the four lines made on the sixth of March past are about a RECORD and not about a HOUSE. There is not one address in them and the word house is not in them at all. A record may be asked who has read it, which is why the second line is written the way it is — a no can be asked about, so a no is not written. A house may be asked nothing. A form cannot be served on a record because a record has no address, and a record is given one by writing down where the drawer is.** And Calder Marr says the turn out loud, once: **this yard did it on the third of April in a good cause, and a page in a drawer in a house is custody an office can reach, and the only reason a form has not been at somebody's door in eleven days is that nobody here has held one, and that is not a protection, it is a fortnight of luck.** **Nessa Pike refuses to copy the four lines into the fourth column**, and a yard does not add a sixth page to anything.
4. **274 — five doors, and a penny. PAID.** Sunday the eighteenth. **Four doors shut on the sheet inside two hours, in this order: not the drawer, not the tin because a tin shuts, not a wall because a sheet on a wall in that harbor goes out of that harbor, and not a fire — and the woman of no office says the last of those out loud for the two of them, that a person who burns a paper with unsettled material on it has handled it, and a person who has kept it is the thing the paper is about, so the burning is the keeping and it is the same door.** Three addresses are ruled out — this shed, the boy, and the man of about thirty who cannot read, which is the only one in that book which is not that yard's. **The reason is not that he is a keeper; a form cannot tell the difference and neither can the holder of that writ. The form goes in the post at half past four at a penny, and the undertaking of the fourteenth is entered in the first column as broken and not as kept.**
5. **275 — the fiftieth wipe, and the outer marks. PAID.** Monday the nineteenth. The fiftieth wipe, the thirty-ninth charge walked on none. **They wait, and there is no figure for waiting. The shipwright says out loud that this yard has now put three things into the world it cannot go and look at, and that the third of them is going to arrive on a step and not in a drawer.** They stand on the crown for twenty minutes, **see the outer marks for the first time from that ground and take no figure and enter nothing**, because the bar has not been narrowed and this party is not going to ask to have it narrowed, in advance or in a boat. And **a boat of this yard may not go to the outer marks either.** And it is decided that **no letter is to be written to the man of about thirty**, because a form on a step and a letter behind it in one week is two things from this yard at one door.
6. **276 — the twenty-sixth week, a lost morning, and three doors. PAID.** Tuesday the twentieth. The wage Tuesday; the column does not move; twenty-six weeks. **He loses the morning to the body and says the only sentence anybody in that harbor has used for it.** In the afternoon the chain and the bar go down the front street and are refused at three doors: a chandler who would not take it at nothing or at four shillings; a boat's owner of about fifty-five who asks whose it is and then says out loud on his own step that the next man who comes down that street with a thing off a wreck will be able to say that this yard asks; and a man of about sixty-one behind a counter who **offers a shilling for the chain and is refused, and asks for the reason and is told that a nail is a thing that cannot be a sale.** What the afternoon cost is not a money figure: about nine people now know.
7. **277 — the outer marks, and a bar that is only a change in the water. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-first. **The price is named on the Tuesday evening. The bar is read out loud at the boat. Nobody is in the water.** The outer marks are two baulks of green timber with a ring of stone and a can on a stake, and three bearings agree with a chart of about thirty years standing to within a cable's length. **And then the man of the second lay stands up and shows them the bar: it is not a fence and there is no post in it, it is a line of about a mile and a half on which the water darkens and stands up in a low sea, and any man in a boat can see it and any man on a mole cannot.** **The three hundred and fifty-two pence bought the fact that nothing on that ground has changed, and that is a fact and it is in the first column.**
8. **278 — the fortieth charge, and a fish market. PAID.** Thursday the twenty-second. The fortieth charge, walked on none. **No person of that yard is in that market and nobody is sent.** A woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall asks one question in about forty people's hearing — **is a person allowed to burn a thing like that** — and is answered in the words of a method, about a thing that is not glass, in a place with no glass and no bench and no oath in it. **What it cost is a certificate of method and the standing of a certificate in a market: a method's words said in a market are a story told by a woman who used to be certified, and the certificate is not withdrawn and cannot be, because she is of no office and the office that keeps the copy is a building with a door on it and no person behind the counter, and the copy is in a drawer in a town four days up this coast. And what she said was true, and nobody in that market was able to tell whether it was true or not, and that is the whole of the price.**
9. **279 — three dates, and three marks. PAID.** Friday the twenty-third. A letter of one page, in a young hand, signed **Wend Brace, thirty, and Ilse Brace, nineteen**, at the address of the third of April. It asks for nothing and **its three dates are kept apart**: the twentieth, the twenty-first, the twenty-second. **A hand hired by the day at three marks was out of a day's work on the Wednesday because he stood in his own doorway for about ten minutes and did not pick up a sheet off his step; the daughter read it out to him on the Thursday and he had it read twice and he cannot read and the letter says so in those words. The three marks is the boat's man's figure and not this yard's and the boat's man is not named, and it is in the second column because the day after that somebody is going to say to an office that this yard has taken a man's wage off him.** And the refusal: **nobody sent, no money sent, and the three marks are not going to be, and the reason is not that the yard has not got them — the day this yard pays that man three marks he is a man this yard has paid, and this yard put a page in his daughter's mouth in the autumn without asking him and has an arrangement with nothing.**
10. **280 — the close. PAID.** Saturday the twenty-fourth. The far bench is occupied from ten until about four and is not approached. **The leaf is read back in full: twelve entries in the first column at the read-back, being three on the fourteenth of April past and nine since, one for every day from the fifteenth to the twenty-third and no day in two of them, and thirteen at the close with that day's own entry in it; forty-eight lines in the second being seven plus thirty-two plus nine, none in the third, and eleven in the fourth.** **The shipwright says that five of the forty-eight are refusals and that in about four years a man in a city will read that book and say that this yard never did anything, and that it will be the wrong shape of right, and that there is no column in that book for the saying of it.** And then the turn, once: **a house is not a place a thing is safe in; it is a place a person cannot refuse anybody anything about; a drawer is a house, a yard is a house, this shed is a house; and the price of that is a man of thirty who cannot read, a woman of about fifty-eight with a drawer under her bed, and a girl of nineteen — and both of those are ours, and neither of them is money, and we are not going to see either of them again unless we write, and we are not going to write.** And then, for Monday: **a woman in this harbor has told forty people in a market that a keeper is a function, and about sixty boats on this coast have a sheet in them that says where every other copy is, and in about two months those two things are going to meet in a place where neither of them is us.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** a form with a name and an address on it, read on a bench and squared with both hands; **a keeper in a town two days down that coast, who is not an officer and did not attend a service because there was no service to attend;** the serving of it by being left; a person of no office asked by a person and not by a yard; a market scene in about forty people's hearing; four refusals, each with a reason against the line; **and the turn, which is that a page in a drawer in a house is custody an office can reach, and that the four lines four people wrote in March are about a record and are not about a house, and that the price of the volume's own solution is now somebody else's problem.**

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 281:** the volume's question, four hundred miles west under seventy fathoms, and the method for reading it, which this yard has and cannot use; **THE WORD *QUIETENING*, WHICH IS NAMED IN CHAPTER 281 AND NOWHERE EARLIER IN THIS VOLUME, IN A CHARACTER'S MOUTH, AND THE WORD *CROWN SEAL*, WHICH IS NOT NAMED IN MOVEMENT 4 AT ALL AND MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291;** the man of about thirty-one of the third lay and his Crown chart; the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in; the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, **THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, FOR A THIRD VOLUME**; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND WAS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE THIRTY CHAPTERS;** the certificate of method whose standing was spent on the twenty-second of April past and which no later chapter may say was restored; **THE FORM ON A STEP IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, WHICH NO LATER CHAPTER MAY SAY WAS WITHDRAWN OR UNSERVED;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume, **and the fact that this batch found a made floor four hundred miles from where they keep their page was not used as a reason to ask them**; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name; the certificate, which cannot be restored and is not going to be asked about; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE THIRTY CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, A MAN OF TWENTY-EIGHT IS IN A BED AT ASHTIDE FOR FIVE WEEKS, A MAN OF FIFTY-ONE HAS LOST ABOUT A HALF OF A SEASON'S GEAR AND HIS GROUND IS STILL SHUT, A YARD HAS SPENT FIVE MARKS, TWO SHILLINGS AND TENPENCE IN TEN DAYS AND EARNED NOTHING, AND IS CARRYING A CHAIN ON A NAIL IT CANNOT SELL AND A BAR IN A DRAWER IT CANNOT GIVE AWAY AND A FORM IN A POST BAG IT CANNOT GET BACK, AND HAS AN ADDRESS IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST IT DID NOT WANT, AND A DRAWER UNDER A BED IN THIS HARBOR IT CANNOT HELP, AND THE ANSWER IS FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST, AND IN ABOUT TWO MONTHS A WORD SAID IN A FISH MARKET AND A SHEET IN ABOUT SIXTY BOATS ARE GOING TO MEET IN A PLACE WHERE NEITHER OF THEM IS THAT YARD.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0003 summary (Chapters 271–280) — the story state at the end of Chapter 280

**Movement 3 is written. A form was served by being put in the post at a penny, a keeper in a town two days down that coast lost an afternoon and a day of three marks and a season's peace, a woman of no office said a thing in a fish market that cost her the standing of a certificate, and the batch's turn is the volume's turn: a page in a drawer in a house is custody an office can reach, the four lines of the sixth of March are about a record and not about a house, and the price of the volume's own solution is now somebody else's problem.** In ten days a man broke his own undertaking out loud in a shed and asked a woman by his own name and not by the yard's; she came up the hill with a sheet she had carried for eleven weeks and put it on a bench; the yard's own sheet-head of that form says *house* and the four lines four other people wrote in March say *record* and neither cancels the other; four doors shut on the sheet and a fifth one is a box on a corner; a chain and a bar went down a front street and were refused three times and a shilling was refused with them; a boat went to the outer marks and a mile and a quarter out and found that nothing had changed since a man dead thirty years drew it, and that the bar is a line of white water and not a fence; a man of thirty who cannot read stood in his own doorway for ten minutes and did not pick up a sheet off his step; a girl of nineteen read a sheet to him twice; a woman of fifty-eight asked in a market whether a person was allowed to burn a thing like that and was told no, in the words of a method, by a woman who used to hold a certificate and cannot have it taken off her because there is no office to take it from; and a boy of twenty-two was not on the stone on any of the ten days and nobody asked him one word.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT IS CHAPTER 275 AND ITS CLIMAX IS CHAPTER 280.** The chapters before 275 are the form and the discovery and the decision to post it. Chapter 275 is where the yard stands on its own ground and cannot look at anything, and where it decides not to write. Chapter 280 is where the turn is paid, once, and the whole standing inventory is carried once.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: NOTHING IN AND EIGHT HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FOUR PENCE OUT, so a net loss of five marks, two shillings and tenpence; a wage column that did not move on the one wage Tuesday in the ten days; twenty-six weeks fallen due; a morning lost to the body on the twentieth; a man's afternoon, a man's day at three marks, and a season's peace in a town this yard cannot see; a certificate of method and the standing of a certificate in a market; a shilling refused; a chain and a bar that cannot be sold and cannot be given away; and a form on a step that cannot be got back.**

**CONFLICTS FOUND AND HOW THEY WERE RESOLVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN DEFENDED:**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 270

**MOVEMENT 2 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. THE VOLUME'S QUESTION HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE ANSWERABLE AND THIS PARTY HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE THE WRONG PARTY FOR IT. A DESCENT WAS BOUGHT AND NOT FOUND, IT WENT TO FORTY FATHOOMS IN A TRENCH OFF THE SOUTH END, IT COST A POT, THREE DAYS OF A CROWN HOUSE'S AIR AND A MAN'S SEASON, AND IT BROUGHT UP A THING THAT IS NOT A RECORD AND A PERSON WHO IS NOT A WITNESS. THREE DAYS ON WHICH A PERSON OF THAT YARD WENT INTO THE WATER WERE ENTERED IN THAT YARD'S OWN FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND THE PRICE NAMED BEFOREHAND, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OTHER BOOK TO ENTER THEM IN, AND THAT IS THE VOLUME'S PROBLEM AND IT WAS PAID AND NOT RENAMED.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **261 — the rate, and the cut. PAID.** Monday the fifth of April. The forty-eighth wipe, the thirty-fifth charge walked on none, and nothing in or out. **GARROW FISK NAMES THE CROWN HOUSE RATE OUT LOUD ON THE MOLE STEPS IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING: nine marks a day for the compressor, the housing, the pipe, the gauges and one man off a Crown house book; two marks and eightpence a day for his own time; a mark and two shillings a day for a hand on the hose, the rate the 28 September 2026 review corrected on the page and which this file had not taken up; thirty-six marks and eight shillings for three days. NOBODY IN THAT HEARING SAID IT WAS SMALL.** His condition is not caution and it is not about what is under a diver's feet; it is about a line, and the cut is therefore a cut in a line made above the water — a bight rove through a shackle, the two ends on the crown, the bight cut on the surface. **NESSA PIKE MAKES THE THREE TURNS ON THE WATER SIDE, AGAINST THAT YARD'S OWN PRACTICE, BECAUSE A SHACKLE ON THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM HAS THREE TURNS ON THE WATER SIDE, AND THE FOURTH COLUMN GETS ITS SECOND LINE.** And **ELIAS VOKE, FIFTY-ONE, OF THE *ANNA RAY* OF THE SECOND LAY, COMES UP WITH HIS NET HUNG AT FORTY FATHOOMS AND A MILE AND A HALF OF GROUND SHUT AGAINST SIX BOATS, AND OFFERS ELEVEN MARKS BEFORE ANY PRICE HAS BEEN SPOKEN OF.**
2. **262 — the first money in twenty-three days. PAID.** Tuesday the sixth of April. The twenty-fourth week falls due and the column does not move, and the holder of that writ **corrects his own sentence of the thirtieth of March in the open and asks that the old one not be struck out.** Voke pays eleven marks, counted twice and read back and counted back. The set is engaged for the eighth, ninth and tenth, **Fisk says out loud that he wrote the yard's name on a sheet and not in the Crown house book, and that a Crown house book has a column for a depth and no column for a year, a name or a reason, and enters that himself, unsigned.** And the form for unsettled material enters as legal pressure: **this yard became an address on the third of April, and an address is a thing that can be given to a man who is going somewhere.**
3. **263 — the cut, and the book that is not there. PAID.** Wednesday the seventh of April. A shackle of that yard's own iron, three turns on the water side, **a serving half a turn out of true, entered in the fourth column and not the first because a thing which is not is not a thing a man did.** A man of twenty-six hired at a mark and two shillings a day. **THE SIX CONDITIONS READ ALOUD AT THE BOAT, NO FIRST ENTRY AND NOTHING TO ENTER, AND THEN THE SENTENCE THAT LANDS L22: THERE IS NO HARBOR AUTHORITY'S BOOK TO GO IN, AND THAT YARD'S OWN BOOK IS NOT THAT BOOK AND IS NOT THE SAME THING.** **AND THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY ASKS HOW FAR OFF THE GROUND IS AND FISK ANSWERS IT BEFORE HE HAS FINISHED ASKING: THE OUTER MARKS ARE A MILE AND A QUARTER OFF THE HEAD OF THAT MOLE, THE BAR IS FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF THE OUTER MARKS, THE BAR BEGINS ABOUT A MILE AND A HALF OUT ON THAT LINE, AND THE CUT IS OFF THE SOUTH END AND ROUND THE CORNER FROM ALL OF IT, AND NOBODY HAS NARROWED THAT BAR AND THIS PARTY IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND HE ASKS FOR IT TO BE SAID AGAIN IN THE BOAT AND BEFORE THE TWO MEN GO DOWN.** The pot is charged to **eighty-four pounds on a face of a hundred and fifty**, and a pencil mark is left on the face where the needle stood, and eighty-four is not near the end of it. **AND THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS CEASES TO EXIST, AND NOBODY SAID A WORD ABOUT IT.**
4. **264 — the forty fathoms. PAID.** Thursday the eighth of April. The thirty-sixth charge walked on none. A day of work done and not booked, because there is no paper to book it against. **The two ends of the bight are cut on the surface at about eleven with a man at forty fathoms and nothing on the surface of the earth holding anything.** And the bottom is not a quarry: **it is a laid floor in courses with a figure cut at the near end of every course, running from one to forty-one without a break, and a socket in the top course with a bar of iron in it and a chain made to the bar, and a net hung across thirty feet of it.** He comes up with a figure he cannot get out of his hand, and nobody asks him what he means.
5. **265 — the net. PAID.** Friday the ninth of April. The warp comes off the bar, the bar comes out of the socket, **and the net comes up, slow and wide and all at once, and takes Amos Searle up about eleven feet into the edge of a course of squared stone.** He says one thing and asks for it in his own words: a net that has been hung eleven days comes up slow, and if he had known it he would have gone under it and not beside it. **Fisk says on the crown of the mole in about a hundred people's hearing that the shoulder is not out and is gone, and that the book carries the man as unfit for five weeks and then as fit for light work, and that the word light is his house's word and he has never been able to make a man light.** The day is a waste and everybody says so.
6. **266 — the third day, and the bill. PAID.** Saturday the tenth of April. **A Crown house sent a man, Hesk Ottrim, thirty-one, up on the Friday night in a coach that took fourteen hours, at the book's own figure, and he says out loud that he asked for the job.** Two hundred and eight fathoms of net come up out of four hundred and eleven, with eleven of eleven floats and the head rope entire, **and the belly is still down and the middle was the money.** **The Crown house book came up the road on the Friday night in the same coach that brought the second man, and at about seven on the Saturday morning, with the door open and about four people in the street and the market not up, FISK READS THE ENTRY OUT, and the word light is his house's word and there is no light work in a holder's trade, and the ship's hand enters the four lines in the second column in his words and the figure in no column.** Fisk names his travel at one mark and fourpence a day for six days and counts it out on the front step in front of about eleven people, and says the fortnight before was his own and is not going on that book, **and then goes in that boat to Ashtide and is away from the eleventh to the fifteenth, as he said out loud on the step.** **The bill goes out as three separate figures — a boat to a hospital at Ashtide, a man's fee, a week's keep of a bed — and Fisk goes in that boat on his own account and says so, and there is no figure for it and there is not going to be one.** Nine feet of chain and a two-foot bar are in that shed.
7. **267 — the chain, the boy, and the lost day. PAID.** Sunday the eleventh of April. **The chain is hung on a nail and lies on the floor, and a man of the second lay says it is not chain that came off a boat and that he would not take it if he could.** The boy comes down on his own account, is put on nothing, and says one thing: **the second column is getting full, and it was not getting full in the spring.** **The man of the second lay asks the ship's hand for the figure in the bag, is given it out loud, is told that it is not a third of what the job cost, asks for it to be written on the front of the shed, is refused and is given the reason against the refusal, and says that is fair, and does not ask again.** **The holder of that writ loses the day to the body** and says the only sentence anybody in that harbor has ever used for it, **and the fourth line of the fourth column is dictated at the bench and written by the ship's hand in her own left hand.**
8. **268 — the bearing, and the mole's foot. PAID.** Monday the twelfth of April. The forty-ninth wipe, the thirty-seventh charge walked on none. **He cannot hold a slate and can hold a compass, and a bearing of north-west by west, about two hundred and seventy, taken four times off the crown of the mole and once in a boat along the courses on the floor, IS THE SAME LINE AS THE BEARING OF THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE ON A SHEET ROLLED BEHIND THE TIDE TABLE IN THAT SHED. THE MOLE HAS A FOOT AT FORTY FATHOOMS AND THE FOOT IS NOT RUBBLE ON A SLOPE.** And then nothing is done about it: nobody is sent for, nothing is written, nothing goes on a wall, and the reason is that a refusal is better than a sheet. Fisk does the arithmetic of seventy fathoms and says the third part of it is not a number and is who owns a machine.
9. **269 — the turn, argued twice and badly. PAID.** Tuesday the thirteenth of April. The twenty-fifth week falls due and the column does not move. **Voke says out loud that he will not pay the difference and why.** And the four sentences: **the floor is not about the fleet, the floor is not the answer, the floor is the method, and this party is the wrong party for it** — said twice, both attempts left standing in the first column. The two depths and the one bearing go in the first column, where a man can check them, and the rest goes in the second.
10. **270 — the close. PAID.** Wednesday the fourteenth of April. The leaf read back in full: **three entries in the first column, seven lines in the second, none in the third, and six in the fourth, being the lines of the fourteenth of May and of the fifth, the seventh, the eleventh, the thirteenth and the fourteenth of April.** The third column is empty, nobody is appointed to it, the boy's hand is at the head of it. The turn in four sentences and no more, and the form for unsettled material at the end of it: **a form is served by being left at an address, the price of that is a person's afternoon and their fear, and this yard is not going to be the reason.** The whole standing inventory, once.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 270

- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair changed most again and neither says so, and the change is that he has now lost an argument to the method twice: he wanted the made floor to be about the fleet and would not have it, and he wanted the whole of what he found in the first column where a man can check it and was given the two figures and the bearing and not the rest.** She put the two depths and the one bearing in the first column and the rest in the second, and the reason she gave is that a man on a mole can take a bearing on the crown of that mole and get the same figure she got. She made the cut wrong on purpose and defended it in front of a man of a pressure house. Nothing in this batch is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, **occupied on three of the ten days, being the tenth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of April, and not occupied at any hour on the other seven**; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and **Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the ten days and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** **NOBODY NAMED HIM AS THE ANSWER TO ANYTHING IN THIS BATCH, AND THE NOT-NAMING CARRIES THE REASON OF THE SECOND OF APRIL FORWARD UNCHANGED AND UNIMPROVED: A MAN ASKED ON A MOLE WHETHER HE CUTS ANSWERS IT WITH A PRICE, AND A PRICE ANSWERED TO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A PRESSURE HOUSE IS A THING THIS YARD WOULD THEN HAVE TO PAY, AND IT HAS NOT GOT, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO ASK A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE WHAT HE WILL TAKE. NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT. AND TOBIAS WREN IS NOT ON A PAGE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT SENT FOR.**
- **Calder and Mara.** **A letter, once, on the second of April, and nothing since. She is a letter and nothing else in these ten days, and nothing was asked of her, nothing was written back, and nobody went up that coast road to a doorstep, and all three of those are in the second column and not the first. Her forty marks stand first after food and were not paid and were not reduced and were not mentioned. The form she described was not served on anybody in these ten days, and Halven Rook is not named in them.**
- **Calder and Garrow Fisk.** **Three days of a Crown house's air and a man who named every figure before he was asked and would not be argued off any of them, and who would not be thanked and was not.** He wrote the yard's name on a sheet and not in the book and said so out loud. He read a five-week entry in a street and said the word light is his house's word. He counted his travel out on a front step in front of about eleven people and said the fortnight before was his own. He went into a boat to a hospital at Ashtide on his own account and said there is no figure for it. **He is not a friend of that party and no chapter of this batch made him one, and nothing in it was a rescue.**
- **Calder and Elias Voke.** **One scene that began on a mole with a figure and ended on a Tuesday with a refusal to pay a difference, and neither man thanked the other and the second asked for that to be a fixed arrangement.** He named his price before one was asked for and would not be argued up; the yard took a job at a loss and put the why in the first column with the date on it. **He is owed nothing and is owed no thanks and has lost about a half of a season's gear and has got back about a half of it, two hundred and eight fathoms out of four hundred and eleven, and the ground is still shut.**
- **Calder and Amos Searle.** **Three days, one of them in the water, and then a net.** He asked for the gas to be called twice and it was. He said one true thing about a net and asked for it in his own words. **He is a man of twenty-eight in a bed and not a witness, and this batch did not make him one and a later volume may not either, and the yard's own second column records that there is nobody to ask and that it is not because a man was hurt.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, the boy's hand at the head of it. **He came down once on the eleventh on his own account, was put on nothing, was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and said that the second column is getting full.**
- **Calder and Ors Kest.** **Not in a room and not on a page in this batch, and the slate wall came down bare twice with the clerk keeping his own page.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-one of the third lay.** **Not on a page in this batch. He was not asked anything and asked nothing, and the batch's nearest temptation — using a bearing or a floor as a reason to go and find the man with the Crown chart — was refused on the page on the twelfth.**

### The power state

**LINE DIVER. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN VOLUME 06 AND NONE IN THIS BATCH. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, IMPROVED OR RENAMED. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED, AND ITS SEASON OF NINE MARKS IS NOT PAID.** What this batch paid is the cost of the perception in ordinary work, and it paid it twice and named it neither time: **he came up out of forty fathoms with a figure he could not get out of his hand, and he lost a day to the body on the eleventh, and on the twelfth he could hold a compass and could not hold a slate, and a compass is a needle and a card and a bit of looking and is not a join.** The standing fact is unchanged: **a seam identifies difference and not truth, and nothing in these ten chapters settled an argument, proved a motive or told anybody what happened; the figures cut at the end of a course on a floor at forty fathoms are a working mark and not a name, and this yard is not going to call them anything else.** The bell is a mark, a frame, a line and a shackle and is not an instrument. No buoy and no bell and no mark went into the water, no finding of worked glass was made, and no return of any kind was made out of any of the ten days.

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** The body is charged: **one day lost on the eleventh of April, entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure, because there is no figure for a day, and the reason is the reason that has been against that line on every lost day since the sixth of October past.** **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, still nameless, not struck out, and in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is twenty-four marks, seven shillings and sevenpence, being three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one pence, and it was sixty-five marks and threepence, being ten thousand four hundred and three pence, on the morning of the fifth of April.** The whole of what came into that yard in the ten days is **eleven marks**, and that is also the whole of what has come into it since the sixth of December, because nothing came in at all after the fourteenth of March. The whole of what went out in the ten days is **fifty-one marks and six shillings**, being 8,232 pence, and the whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December is **fifty-nine marks, twelve shillings and twopence in seventeen transactions at six counters**, which is the figure every chapter from the tenth to the fourteenth now carries, **and eleven marks is one thousand seven hundred and sixty pence and has been printed as one thousand seven hundred and seventy-six in four chapters and is now right in all of them.** **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS DOES NOT EXIST AND HAS NOT SINCE THE SEVENTH OF APRIL, and nobody in that shed said one word about it at the time.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-FIVE weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them.** Two wages of four marks were not paid in these ten days, on the sixth and the thirteenth of April, and the column did not move on either and the envelopes did not move.
- **The slate wall came down bare twice, being the forty-eighth and the forty-ninth Mondays since the first of May, on the fifth and the twelfth of April, the counter not restarting and the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting was held in that room on any day of this book.**
- **The cistern was charged at no figure on three rota days and this party walked none of them, being the thirty-fifth, thirty-sixth and thirty-seventh of the charges walked on none since the third of August past. The walk is nil and it stays nil. No figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.**
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the tenth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of April, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for a seventy-fourth night, counting from the Sunday of the thirty-first of January, and it is the only bare thing in that shed.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the ten days.**
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, and he was not asked anything in these ten days and the chest was not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure, and that is in no sentence with the bed at Ashtide. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, and nothing was asked of her and nothing was written back. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed with the boy's hand at the head of it, and he was not on the stone on any of the ten days. NINE FEET OF CHAIN ON A NAIL IN THAT SHED AND A BAR OF SQUARE IRON TWO FEET LONG IN THE DRAWER, AND NOBODY CAN USE THE CHAIN AND NOBODY WOULD TAKE IT, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED WHOSE EITHER IS.**
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IS NOT A REGISTRY, A COURT OR A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS BATCH.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** the air, and its Crown house rate, said out loud; a cut made above the water on a bench; a descent to forty fathoms bought and not found; a pot, three days and a body; a mole with a foot at the bottom of it; a chain that is not a record; a man in a bed at Ashtide; **and the turn, which is that the volume's question is answerable and this party is the wrong party for it.**

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 271:** the volume's question, which is now known to be answerable and is four hundred miles west under seventy fathoms; **the form for unsettled material, which is a form and not a favour, has never been served on anybody, and is now attached to an address, because this yard wrote a letter to a man who cannot read and became an address on the third of April;** the man of about thirty-one of the third lay and his Crown chart; the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in; the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, for a third volume; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND WAS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume, and the batch found the method of laying stone four hundred miles from where those four people are and used it as no reason to ask them; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, A MAN OF TWENTY-EIGHT IS IN A BED AT ASHTIDE FOR FIVE WEEKS BECAUSE A NET CAME UP ON HIM, A MAN OF FIFTY-ONE HAS LOST ABOUT A HALF OF A SEASON'S GEAR AND HIS GROUND IS STILL SHUT, AND A YARD HAS BOUGHT THREE DAYS OF A CROWN HOUSE'S AIR AND LOST FORTY MARKS AND SIX SHILLINGS DOING IT, AND IS CARRYING A CHAIN ON A NAIL THAT IT CANNOT SELL AND CANNOT GIVE AWAY, AND THE ANSWER IS FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST.**

The air has a price, the cut is made on a bench above the water, the descent went to forty fathoms and cost a pot, three days and a body, and the batch's turn is the volume's turn: the question is answerable and this party is the wrong party for it.** In ten days a fireman of a pressure house named a Crown house rate out loud in front of nine people and would not pretend it was small; a shipwright made a shackle wrong on purpose and wrote down why; a skipper of fifty-one lost the middle of his net, offered eleven marks before anybody had mentioned a price, refused to be argued up, and said out loud that he would not pay the difference; a descent went to forty fathoms in a trench off the south end on a line that was cut on the surface with a man at the bottom; a net came up on a man of twenty-eight and put him into a stone course and into a bed at Ashtide for five weeks; a bearing of north-west by west about two hundred and seventy was taken off a crown of a mole and found to be the same line as the bearing of the crown of that mole, which means the mole has a laid and numbered foot at forty fathoms a mile and a half out; and a boy of twenty-two stood in a shed door and said that the second column is getting full.
