## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 260

**MOVEMENT 1 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. THE VOLUME'S CENTRAL PRESSURE IS A PARTY WITH NO INSTRUMENT OF ANY KIND. THE VOLUME'S QUESTION HAS BEEN ASKED ONCE, AT A MOLE HEAD, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND HAS NOT BEEN ANSWERED. NOTHING WAS FOUND, NOTHING WAS RAISED, NOBODY WENT IN THE WATER, AND FOURTEEN DAYS OF THE TWENTY WERE SPENT FINDING OUT THAT A THING ON THE BOTTOM HAD BEEN HANDLED BY SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT THE YARD.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **251 — the instrument is gone. PAID.** Tuesday the sixteenth, Wednesday the seventeenth of March. **The ship's hand counts the drawer twice and comes out with six pieces of paper and finds that the charter's place is empty and clean and the wood is a slightly different colour where a thing had been lying on it for four months.** She reads the form of the fourth of March from the top to the bottom and finds that the whole of it asks this yard for nothing, and then does the arithmetic: a hirer at the second seam pays for a piece of paper and the paper is not here, so there is no day to sell. **FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE SIXTH OF OCTOBER A WORKING DAY CANNOT BE BOOKED AT ALL, and the twenty-first week falls due on a Tuesday on which no envelope is made.** The boat of about forty tons is hired at a mark and eightpence because the man of the second lay will not go out past a fouled mark with a hand short, and at the mark there are two bright places on the shackle the size of a thumbnail.
2. **252 — the boat that is not the yard's. PAID.** Thursday the eighteenth, Friday the nineteenth. The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the thirtieth. **TOBIAS WREN, SIXTY-ONE, HALF DEAF, WHO HAS NOT BEEN ON A PAGE SINCE VOLUME 02, COMES UP THE MOLE BECAUSE HE HEARD ON SATURDAY AT A FISH MARKET THAT A MARK WAS FOULED AND SAYS HE DID NOT COME UP TO BE ASKED.** He asks one question and it is who is paying, and he names his terms before any of them is asked for: six marks a day for the boat whatever the month, a hand of about forty called Ruad paid separate by the day, and fuel at what fuel costs. **He says he will not be a teacher, and that in thirty-one years by another man's account nobody ever asked him what was in a thing he went into and he has never said, and that the last time he took a wreck apart there was nothing in the frame he could carry and a thing on the bottom that would have fitted in his coat, and he went home.** No boat of his was hired and no six marks was paid.
3. **253 — nineteen days. PAID.** Saturday the twentieth, Sunday the twenty-first. **THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT COMES UP THE COAST ROAD IN ANOTHER MAN'S CART, NINETEEN DAYS AFTER HE WENT UP IT, THINNER, WITH A FOREARM THAT HAS A SHAPE TO IT, AND READS THE FORM OF THE FOURTH OF MARCH IN FOUR MINUTES STANDING AND SAYS THERE IS NOTHING IN IT HE COULD NOT HAVE SAID OUT LOUD ON A MOLE.** He brings back four lines in a hand that is not his own and not hers — two of a place, one of a month nobody here uses, and one sentence — **and the sentence is that four people will not send a man to a coast where the man who writes things down is the one everybody remembers, and he had asked them once for a witness alive who had been on that water and was refused three times before the sentence was read to him.** The far bench is occupied on the Sunday from ten until four and **he did not go over to him at any hour of the day, and said the reason out loud to a doorframe, and asked that the words go in the book and not the reason.** Four days lost to the body on the road, in the second column, with no figure.
4. **254 — the forty-sixth wipe, and the shackle. PAID.** Monday the twenty-second, Tuesday the twenty-third. **THE WALL BEHIND THE REEVE'S BENCH CAME DOWN BARE FOR THE FORTY-SIXTH TIME SINCE THE FIRST OF MAY, THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART, THE CLERK KEPT HIS OWN PAGE, AND A CLERK OF THAT HARBOR AUTHORITY SAID OUT LOUD THAT THE STANDING INSTRUCTION IS A WIPE EVERY MONDAY AT EIGHT WHETHER THERE IS A SITTING OR NOT, AND THAT HE HAS A PAGE OF DATES AND WOULD NOT GIVE IT TO ANYBODY WHO HAD NOT ASKED.** The cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-first. **The holder offers to take the slate and is refused by the ship's hand on the ground that a private hire of a boat is not a place to put a man in the water, and he says so first and asks for it entered.** At the mark: three bright places and not two, the Wednesday's two not struck out, a shackle that has been off the frame and back on the wrong way up, and a wire cut and mended with three turns on the water side of a frame where this yard turns on the landward side. The twenty-second week falls due and the column does not move.
5. **255 — what fouling says. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-fourth, Thursday the twenty-fifth, and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-second. **A MAN OF THE SECOND LAY WITH NINETEEN YEARS IN THE WATER READS THE SLATE AND GIVES FOUR THINGS IN ORDER: A SEASON FOR GROWTH, BEING NINE WEEKS IN A HARD YEAR AND ELEVEN IN A SOFT ONE; BRIGHT IRON FOR A HAND INSIDE A FORTNIGHT; A SPANNER AND A MORNING FOR A MENDED CUT; AND THAT NONE OF THOSE THREE KNOWS A NAME AND ANYBODY WHO SAYS WHICH OF FOUR PEOPLE DID IT IS SELLING.** He says all four of them out loud at the head of that dock in eleven people's hearing and asks that it be entered that he said no word about the four people four days down that coast and is not going to. **He also says that a mark with two parties in it gets a wire through in the dark by a man with no lights, and that he has seen two of them off the Sill in his first year and does not know the names of either and is not going to be asked.** The limit four people of that coast wrote and signed is quoted in the first column and stands.
6. **256 — a line, a flat, and four columns. PAID.** Friday the twenty-sixth, Saturday the twenty-seventh. **THE FOULING IS A FOOT INSTEAD OF FOUR INCHES; THERE IS A FOUR-STRAND UNTARRED LINE TIED WITH A SHEET BEND; AND THE SHACKLE HAS A QUARTER-INCH FLAT ON THE CROWN OF THE BOW THAT THE SEA DOES NOT MAKE, AND THE SHIP'S HAND NAMES THE MAKE BECAUSE SHE HAS MADE THE OTHER ONE, AND THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY SAYS THERE IS ONE SMITH ON THIS COAST WHO FINISHES THEM THAT WAY AND THAT HE IS SIXTY-EIGHT AND HAS A SHOP OFF THE YARD AT TERNWATCH.** Three things are said out loud with their prices before any of them is agreed: a cut, which wants a boat and a man and an instrument this yard has none of; a bigger mark, at four marks of iron, which is the only one it could pay for and the one it does not want; and a complaint, which is a name in a book in a town four days down that coast. **The holder wants the complaint, is refused, loses the argument to his own sentence of the eleventh of March, and asks that it be entered that he lost it to his own sentence and not to a better one.** **Saturday: a fourth leaf is ruled on the back of a sheet of chandler's paper with four columns — what was there, who saw it, what was done, and what it is not — the fourth head written with a blunt nib, and it does not go on any wall in that harbor and never will.**
7. **257 — the question, and not an answer. PAID.** Sunday the twenty-eighth, Monday the twenty-ninth, and the wall comes down bare for the forty-seventh time and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-third. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY WITH A COASTER OUT OF ASHTIDE PUTS A CROWN CHART ON THE FISH QUAY WHERE ANYBODY CAN GET AT IT AND ASKS, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, WHETHER THE FLEET WAS SCUTTLED OR WHETHER IT WENT DOWN, AND GIVES HIS OWN SMALL REASON FOR WANTING TO KNOW.** The holder of that writ answers, badly, and knows it: three things, and a statement made before them that none of them is an answer — nobody in that harbor is old enough; the only thing that could answer it is at seventy fathoms about four hundred miles west-southwest of that mole and its name is not going to be said in a market; and this party holds no instrument of any kind. **The man calls it three numbers and a refusal and is told yes. He then asks one question, being whether the thirty-eighth line will be there in four years, and is told the honest thing, and calls that the answer.** Nothing of it was written down, and the reason is in the second column.
8. **258 — a season that ends with nothing issued. PAID.** Tuesday the thirtieth, Wednesday the thirty-first. The twenty-third week falls due and the column does not move, and it is the whole of that year's list. **THE REEVE GIVES THREE THINGS AND SAYS BEFORE GIVING THEM THAT A MAN WHO IS GIVEN THREE THINGS HAS NOT BEEN REFUSED THREE THINGS: NO INSTRUMENT AFTER THAT DAY, THE LEDGER BEING SPENT; THAT HIS OFFICE IS NOT THE OFFICE THAT CAN GIVE THE CHARTER BACK AND NEVER WAS, SAID A THIRD TIME BECAUSE A TRUE SENTENCE DOES NOT WEAR OUT; AND THE ONE THING IT CAN DO, WHICH IS TO SEAT TWO PEOPLE AND TAKE A FINDING AS IT IS GIVEN, AT A COST OF TWO CLERKS AND HIMSELF, ONE AFTERNOON A WEEK, IN A ROOM HE HAS TO BE WARM FOR.** The yard asks who the other side is and is told that the other side is a man of fifty of the second lay and a smith in Ternwatch who has never heard of the yard, and that seating either as a party would be inventing a proceeding to get at a name. **HE SAYS OUT LOUD THAT HE IS NOT A FRIEND OF THAT PARTY AND THAT THIS IS NOT A RESCUE, AND THE REASON HE SAYS IT IS SO THAT THE STORY WILL BE HARDER TO TELL IN A MONTH.** Nothing was written to the tide gang and nothing to the man of the second lay.
9. **259 — the air, and the condition. PAID.** Thursday the first, Friday the second of April. The cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-fourth and last of this batch, and the third lay fills at seven in the morning with one berth short of two. **GARROW FISK, THIRTY-FOUR, OF A PRESSURE HOUSE AT TERNWATCH, COMES UP THE HILL WITH THAT YARD'S PRINTED SHEET FOLDED AT THE THIRTY-EIGHTH LINE AND SAYS HE IS NOT HERE ABOUT A JOB AND WANTS TO KNOW WHETHER THAT LINE IS TRUE, AND IS TOLD THAT IT IS.** He offers a compressor and a housing and a man off a Crown house book at a Crown house rate, will not pretend the figure is small and will not pretend that this party is a Crown hull, and sets one condition: **he will not go under anything that has not been cut, and that is not a rule in a book but what happened to a man he worked beside for nine years who is alive and does not go down at all now.** Two marks and eightpence a day, named before he was asked, and it was paid. Asked who cuts, the yard says it has not got a cutter, and the man sits on the top step for an hour and a half and is brought out a cup of water and no more. **NOBODY IN THAT SHED NAMED THE ONLY MAN IN THAT HARBOR WHO COULD, AND THE NOT-NAMING IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON.**
10. **260 — the batch's turn, and the close. PAID.** Saturday the third, Sunday the fourth. **A LETTER OF ONE PAGE ASKING NOTHING GOES INTO THE ORDINARY POST AT A PENNY FOR A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY WHO CANNOT READ IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DOES NOT SIGN IT, GIVING AS THE SECOND OF HIS TWO REASONS THAT A NAME ON A PIECE OF PAPER ABOUT A MARK THAT TWO PARTIES HAVE A CLAIM TO, GOING TO A TOWN WHERE FOUR PEOPLE KEEP A PAGE IN A DRAWER, IS THIS YARD'S NAME IN AN OFFICE'S FILE IN ABOUT TWO YEARS; AND THE LETTER IS SIGNED AT THE FOOT IN THE HAND OF THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY.** **A LETTER FROM A PERSON OF NO OFFICE CAME UP THE HILL ON THE FRIDAY AND SAYS ONE FACT AND ASKS FOR NOTHING: AN OFFICE SHE WORKED IN FOR NINE YEARS HAS A FORM FOR MATERIAL THAT OFFICE CALLS UNSETTLED, AND A PERSON WHO KEEPS UNSETTLED MATERIAL IN A HOUSE IS A KEEPER OF IT UNDER THAT FORM, AND WHETHER THAT MEANS A HOUSE OR A DRAWER OR A CUPBOARD THE FORM DOES NOT SAY, AND SHE HAS NOT SEEN IT SERVED ON ANYBODY AND CANNOT SAY WHAT IT DOES, AND SHE WILL COME IF A PERSON ASKS HER AND WILL NOT COME IF A YARD ASKS HER. NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER AND NOTHING WAS WRITTEN BACK, AND NOT WRITING BACK IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST.** Sunday: the far bench is occupied from ten until four and is not approached. **THE FOURTH LEAF HAS ONE ENTRY IN ITS FIRST COLUMN AND ONE LINE IN ITS FOURTH: THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, WHICH IS NINE WEEKS FROM THE DAY THE MARK WAS SET, AND IS NOT A DATE ON WHICH THE FOULING WILL BE A SEASON'S BUT A DATE ON WHICH ANYBODY WHO GOES AND LOOKS CAN SEE THAT IT IS NOT.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 260

- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this batch changes most, and the change is that he has lost three arguments in ten days and two of them to her, and he asked for both to be entered.** He wanted the complaint and was refused by his own sentence of the eleventh of March. He offered to take the slate and was refused on the ground that a private hire is not a place to put a man in the water. **He lost the complaint to her reading of his own words and asked that it be recorded that he lost it to his own sentence and not to a better one, and she has entered that and has not improved on it. He is the man who reads the form in four minutes and says there is nothing in it he could not have said out loud on a mole, and she is the woman who counts the drawer twice and does the arithmetic nobody wanted to do.** Nothing in this batch is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, **occupied on three of the twenty days, being the nineteenth, the twenty-first and the twenty-sixth of March, and not occupied at any hour on the other seventeen**, not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and **Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the twenty days, and he was in that harbor on fifteen of them and up that coast road on five, and neither of those is entered and neither is a reason.** **NOBODY NAMED HIM AS THE ANSWER TO WHO CUTS, AND THE NOT-NAMING IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN, AND THE REASON GIVEN IS ABOUT THE TRADE AND NOT ABOUT A FAMILY: A MAN ASKED ON A MOLE WHETHER HE CUTS ANSWERS IT WITH A PRICE, AND A PRICE ANSWERED TO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A PRESSURE HOUSE IS A THING THIS YARD WOULD THEN HAVE TO PAY, AND IT HAS NOT GOT, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO ASK A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE WHAT HE WILL TAKE. NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT.**
- **Calder and Mara.** **A LETTER, ONCE, IN THE ORDINARY POST, ON THE SECOND OF APRIL, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED HER FOR ANYTHING.** She is a person of no office and has been since the fourth of January. **What she sent is a form and not a favour: an office's form for unsettled material, a house as a place a keeper keeps it in, and the fact that she has never seen it served and cannot say what it does. And a condition, which is that she will come if a person asks her and will not come if a yard asks her, and that she has thought for three days about the difference between those two things and has not got round to it.** **NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER, NOTHING WAS WRITTEN BACK, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST, because the first column is a record of what a man did and not of what a man did not do.** Her forty marks stand first after food and were not paid and were not reduced and were not mentioned in her letter.
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **One scene, twenty minutes, on the mole's steps, and neither man is grateful and neither man wants to be.** He came because he heard a mark was fouled and not because he was asked, and he asked one question and it was who is paying, and he named his price before he would agree to anything, and he said he would not be a teacher before anybody asked him to be. **No boat of his was hired and no six marks was paid and the conversation cost him a morning of walking up a hill and nothing else, and the yard did not thank him and he is not owed thanks.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-four of the second lay.** **The chapter reads the slate and gives the four things, and says them in a street because the ship's hand asked him to say them where nine people could hear, and he says them, and he asks that it be entered that he said no word about the four people of that coast.** He begins a sentence at the water side of a frame and does not finish it, and the rest of it is about the four, and nobody finishes it for him.
- **Calder and Ors Kest.** **One scene, in the reeve's office, and he is still not a friend of this party and said so in his own office before anything else happened.** He gave three things, said a true sentence a third time, priced the one thing he has left out of himself, told the yard that its mark has no second party it could seat, and said that he does not invent proceedings. **THE SEASON OF THAT OFFICE ENDED ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH AND NO INSTRUMENT HAS BEEN ISSUED OUT OF IT SINCE, AND THE NEXT INSTRUMENT ANY OFFICE IN THAT HARBOR ISSUES, IF ONE EVER DOES, IS NOT GOING TO BE A THING THAT COULD BE USED TO GO AND LOOK AT ANYTHING.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, the boy's hand at the head of it. **THE BOY CAME DOWN TO THE MOLE ON THE SUNDAY FOURTH OF APRIL AT ABOUT ELEVEN ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ON THE STONE TO BE ON, AND HE WAS NOT PUT ON IT.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-one of the third lay.** One scene, at the head of that dock, and he asked the volume's question and was refused and asked nothing and was not asked anything, and **he sails on the chart, and the berth he did not get in the third lay on the Sunday went to a boat out of the north basin, and that is the batch's whole cost to a third party and it is entered.**

### The power state

**LINE DIVER. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN VOLUME 06. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, IMPROVED OR RENAMED ON ANY PAGE. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED, AND ITS SEASON OF NINE MARKS IS NOT PAID AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ASKED FOR IT.** What changed in this batch is method and it is in other people: a price named before a yes, a condition that stands without its reason, a refusal made twice in the same words, a slate read back three times by three people, a leaf with a column for what a thing is not, and a cup of water and no more. **THE BELL IS A MARK, A FRAME, A LINE AND A SHACKLE AND IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, and no buoy, no bell and no mark went into the water on a day this yard did not pay for and nobody was in the water at any time on any of the twenty days. No finding of worked glass was made, nothing was raised, and no return of any kind was made out of any of the twenty.** The standing fact is unchanged: **a seam identifies difference and not truth, and nothing in these ten chapters settled an argument, proved a motive or told anybody what happened.** **AND THE ONE THING THIS BATCH DID TO THE HOLDER'S STANDING IS NOT A STAGE AND IS NOT A POWER: on the twenty-seventh of March he wanted to go up a coast and knock on a door, and did not, and asked for it to be written down that he did not.**

His forearm was bad again after nineteen days in a cart and is entered and not named.** **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, are not struck out, and are in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is sixty-five marks and threepence, being ten thousand four hundred and three pence, and the figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks is nine thousand seven hundred and sixty-three pence. THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THAT YARD IN THE TWENTY DAYS IS NOTHING, and that is the first twenty-day run in five volumes in which nothing came in at all, and the reason is the form of the fourth of March and not a mood.** The whole of what went out in the twenty days is five marks, two shillings and ten pence, being eight hundred and thirty-four pence, and the whole of what has gone out of that yard since the sixth of December past is eight marks, six shillings and two pence in eleven transactions at five counters.

- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and ninety-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the twenty days. THE FOURTH LEAF IS NOT IN THAT DRAWER AND IS ON A LEAF RULED ON THE BACK OF A SHEET OF CHANDLER'S PAPER ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MARCH, AND THERE IS NO SECOND COPY OF IT.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved and unasked about. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, untouched, unoffered, and a letter from her in the ordinary post on the second of April and nothing asked of her and nothing written back.

Five pages in five drawers in five towns in five hands, one page to a drawer, no two of them the same page, and this yard did not look in any of the four it cannot look in and did not write to the town that put a page on a wall. The agreement about who may read a page has no name and the reason is a counter in a room off a fish market.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** the instrument that is not there; a party that cannot be hired; a boat that is not the yard's and the price of it; nineteen days up a coast road and four lines in a hand that is not his own; a question asked at a mole head and three facts that are not an answer; a season that ended with nothing issued and a reeve who said out loud that he is not a friend; a fireman of a pressure house and one condition; a fourth column; and a letter to a man who cannot read and a letter from a woman of no office, and neither answered.

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 261:** the volume's question, which is whether the fleet was scuttled or whether it went down, and the answer is under seventy fathoms of water and this party cannot get there; **a cutter, which nobody in that harbor can supply and the one man who could was not named;** the air, and the Crown house rate for it; the mark, and the fourteenth of May; the fouling, and the two thousand pounds of a foot and a half of somebody else's green; **the form for unsettled material, which is in a letter and not in any office's hand, and the question of whether a house is a drawer;** a man of thirty-four of a second lay who sails on a chart in Veyr; **the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in;** the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, for a third volume; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND IS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name, which is on one page of Volume 05 and is not to be said again; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE FOURTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, AND A YARD THAT HAS BEEN TWENTY DAYS WITHOUT A PAPER OF ANY KIND HAS SENT ONE LETTER AND RECEIVED ONE, AND NEITHER HAS BEEN ANSWERED, AND NOBODY NAMED THE ONLY MAN WHO COULD HAVE ANSWERED THE OTHER HALF OF IT.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0001 summary (Chapters 251–260) — the story state at the end of Chapter 260

**Movement 1 is written. The leash is gone and the yard cannot be hired, and the question is under seventy fathoms of water, and this batch found out that the only people on this coast who could answer it are four people this yard is not going to ask.** In twenty days a shipwright found out that a party with no paper has nothing to sell; a retired salvage foreman named the price of a boat and said he would not be a teacher; a man came home from a coast road with four lines in somebody else's hand and a sentence that is a refusal; a mark was looked at three times and was found to have been handled, lifted, mended, fouled faster than the water can do it, and tied with a knot this yard does not use; a man with nineteen years in the water said out loud in a street that fouling does not know a name; the holder wanted to knock on a door and did not, and lost the argument to his own sentence; a leaf with four columns was ruled and the fourth of them says what a thing is not; the volume's question was asked at a mole head and answered with three facts that are not an answer; a harbor authority's season ended with nothing issued and a reeve said out loud that he is not a friend; a fireman of a pressure house came up a hill with a folded sheet of thirty-eight lines and offered air and set one condition; and a letter went to the ordinary post for a man who cannot read, and a letter came up the hill from a person of no office, and neither was answered.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT TURN IS CHAPTER 256 AND ITS TURN IS PAID IN THE PAGE: a fourth column, headed *what it is not*, in a book in one town, that nobody can check.** The chapters before it are a party learning what it has lost and a mark learning who else has been on it. Chapter 256 is where the volume's method arrives, and everything after it is that method being paid for. **The batch's climax is Chapter 260**, where a yard which spent five volumes refusing to be an address becomes one address more, for a man who cannot read, at a penny, unsigned.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: NOTHING CAME IN.** Twenty days, no income, eight hundred and thirty-four pence out, a wage column that did not move on three Tuesdays, twenty-three weeks fallen due, a day lost to the body on the first of April, four days lost to the body on a coast road, and **a Sunday berth in the third lay that went to a boat out of the north basin because a man was at the head of that dock being answered by this yard.**

**CONFLICTS FOUND AND HOW THEY WERE RESOLVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN DEFENDED:**

1. **THE HARVOR AUTHORITY'S CHARTER EXPIRED ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH AND A CREW WAS PAID BY IT FOR WORK IN THE SECOND SEAM ON THE THIRD AND FIFTH OF APRIL.** The charter ran to the last day of March, so the third and the fifth of April are covered by the new season, and the two chapters that hire out this yard's gear on those dates say that they are hired and paid by a hirer and are not salvage and are not a claim and are not work under any instrument of that harbor authority's. **NO HIRER'S DAY IS BOOKED IN THIS BATCH AND NO FIGURE ENTERS THE BAG FROM ANY HIRER, AND THE LADDER STANDS AT THIRTY-ONE AND THE WAGE COLUMN STANDS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS.**
2. **`outline/series.md` PLANS THAT CALDER "BECOMES A SKILLED FAULTREADER" IN THIS VOLUME, AND THAT IS A DIVERGENCE, FLAGGED ON THE FACE OF `outline/volume-06.md` § *Divergences* AND NOT REPAIRED, BECAUSE THE STAGE IS SPENT AND TWO AUDITS RULE IT IS NOT RE-TAKEN.** The same file plans that Mara's public testimony costs her standing inside the Registry, and she left the Registry in Volume 04, so what her testimony costs in this volume is the standing of a certificate in a market. Five divergences are flagged, with line numbers, and none is repaired here.
3. **`outline/volume-05.md:259` SAYS THE LAST DATE IN THE SERIES IS THE FIFTH OF DECEMBER 2026 AND IT IS NOT.** A binding planning file was not edited by this phase and the sentence was not silently repaired; the flag is carried at `outline/volume-06.md` lock L34 and at `state/open-threads.md` § *Flagged for the controller* and is not restated in a sixth place. **`outline/volume-06.md` PRINTS NO YEAR AND ITS ANCHOR IS THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH.**
4. **THE FAR-BENCH LIST WAS WRITTEN IN THE CARD FILE AS THE EIGHTEENTH OF MARCH AND THE CHAPTERS HAVE THE NINETEENTH, THE TWENTY-FIRST AND THE TWENTY-SIXTH.** The card file is corrected here and the three days stand.
5. **A SIX-MARKS-A-DAY BOAT WAS DESCRIBED ONCE AS NINE TIMES A DAY'S WORK ON THE SECOND SEAM AND A SIX-MARKS-A-DAY BOAT IS TWICE THAT, and the figure was wrong in the dialogue and in the second column in the same chapter, being nine hundred and sixty pence against four hundred and eighty.** **THIS WAS NOT IN FACT REPAIRED WHEN IT WAS RECORDED, and `logs/next.review.log` found it still wrong in both places on 27 September 2026, and it is now twice in the dialogue and twice in the in-scene second column and agrees with the apparatus, and the card file's own line is corrected with the arithmetic written out.**

7. **THE HOUSE'S OWN LENGTH RULE IS STILL MEASURING THE HOUSE'S OWN APPARATUS.** The apparatus is 41.5% of this batch's words against 41.0% for Volume 05, so the thinning was deliberate and did not take. Three chapters inside the guideline and seven past it, Chapter 252 past it by seven words as the batch closed and by fifty-one after the review repairs, and the largest is the batch's close at 4,215 as it closed and 4,363 after them. **The 41.5% was measured on the day the batch closed and is not re-derived; no scene was cut and no cost was dropped to bring any chapter inside a number, and no scene was cut and none was put in to repair a finding either.**
8. **Interface compliance.** No panels, stat blocks, character sheets, status messages, floating text, quest text, skill trees, level-ups, or software vocabulary. **The ten chapters contain no occurrence of the word *panel* and no occurrence of *quietening*, *crown seal*, *orison* or *open keel*,** and a mechanical scan for the standing banned terms returns nothing. Three idiomatic instances of "the way you do" in narration were rewritten to third person so that no second person stands in the prose. The only message-like objects are the crew's book with its four columns, the harbor authority's own wall and the clerk's own page, the form of the fourth of March, the chart, the slate, two letters, and a bell mark on the bottom of the sea.

## Required updates after each batch

A writer phase that completes a batch updates these same files and does not set phase status:

- `state/chapter-summaries.md`: one entry per chapter, two to five sentences each, plus the compact volume index.
- `state/continuity.md`: new canon facts, changed relationships, power costs and gains, discovered world rules, and any proposed canon change.
- `state/open-threads.md`: promises opened, promises closed, and threads carried forward.
- `state/current.md`: the story state at the end of the batch, so the next batch starts from the right place, plus the batch summary.

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **241 — what the holder of the writ is on the first of March. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-fourth, Thursday the twenty-fifth of February. **The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the first of six.** No work on the Wednesday; a working day on the Thursday. **THE FINDING IS A FACT AND NOT A CLIFFHANGER: at the counter of this harbor's own authority on the west basin a clerk of that office says that the writ of the first of May past is a municipal instrument of this harbor, is inside that harbor line, is bounded by the outer marks, carries four names and no fifth, is not the Second Bell license, does not lead to one, renews nothing, and runs to midnight on the first of March, and that the office which issued it has said on the face of it that it is not the office that can renew it; and that at midnight on the first of March that paper stops being a thing the holder holds and nothing takes its place, and nobody is charged with anything, and no court sits, and nobody is fined, and no clerk comes up that hill.** And the clerk reads the one-season provisional working charter of the twenty-eighth of November past without being asked and says it is a different paper from the writ, is not the writ, is not the Second Bell license, does not lead to one, runs to the last day of March, and that a party which does not produce a thing on a day is not fined because a court does not fine a poor man and the matter simply goes on. **The read-back runs twice and the ship's hand refuses the holder's sentence in the second column in favour of her own.**
2. **242 — the thing that comes up the coast. PAID.** Friday the twenty-sixth, Saturday the twenty-seventh of February. No rota day. **A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FIVE WHO SELLS LIME AND CHALK COMES UP THAT COAST ROAD WITH A CART AND A BOOK OF GROUND ABOUT A STRETCH OF WATER ABOUT NINE MILES FROM HIS OWN DOOR, IN WATER NO LEAD AND NO BOAT OF THAT YARD HAS BEEN IN, KEPT BY FOUR PEOPLE ALIVE, AND HE SAYS THE BOOK DOES NOT COME OUT OF THE PLACE IT IS ABOUT AND THAT A PAGE ABOUT A PLACE IS THE PLACE'S AND THAT IF IT LEAVES IT STOPS BEING THE PLACE'S AND STARTS BEING EVIDENCE. IN THE SAME WEEK A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR COMES UP THAT HILL IN THE RAIN WITH A LEAD ABOUT THE HOLDER'S OWN BROTHER — A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY, FOUR DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS, TWO DAYS, A MONTH TWO YEARS AGO — AND HE HAD ASKED THAT MAN NOTHING. THE TWO ARRIVE INSIDE TWO DAYS AND THE CHAPTER DOES NOT RESOLVE EITHER, AND THE PRICE OF THE LEAD IS NAMED BEFORE THE DAY: four days there and four days back, two men off the water, about twenty-four marks, and the price is not paid and is not going to be paid.** No confession, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and the holder does not go over to the far bench.
3. **243 — midnight on the first of March. PAID.** Sunday the twenty-eighth of February, Monday the first of March. **The forty-third wipe, the wall down bare. The cistern is charged on the Monday and walked on none, being the second of six. THE WRIT RUNS TO MIDNIGHT ON THIS DAY AND AT TEN MINUTES PAST MIDNIGHT THE HOLDER ENTERS IN THE FIRST COLUMN IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND THAT IT CEASED TO BE A THING THIS PARTY HOLDS, AND THE SHIP'S HAND IS NOT USED FOR THAT LINE BECAUSE A PAGE A MAN CANNOT DATE HIMSELF IS A PAGE A MAN CANNOT CHECK.** No court, no clerk up that hill, nobody fined, nobody refused, nobody examined. **THE CHAPTER SAYS OUT LOUD BEFORE IT WRITES THE LINE THAT THE DAY IS NOT A DISASTER AND WHY: a man went down to a counter and asked a clerk what he would be on the first of March and the clerk told him and was right to tell him, and that is the cheapest thing this yard has ever bought.** And on that day the four communities and the other places are being told something by somebody, and that somebody is not this yard. A working day on the Monday. The read-back runs.
4. **244 — the choice, and it is the volume's climax. PAID.** Tuesday the second, Wednesday the third of March. **The wage does not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is NINETEEN, all nineteen in the same breath, and the reason is the reason of the twenty-ninth of December and is not improved on. AT ABOUT TEN ON THE TUESDAY MORNING THE HOLDER GETS ON THE CART AND GOES UP THAT COAST ROAD WITH THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FIVE, AND THE COST OF THAT GOING WAS NAMED IN THE FIRST COLUMN ON THE MONDAY NIGHT AT ABOUT ELEVEN O'CLOCK, BEFORE THE DAY AND NOT AFTER IT. AND ON THE WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON THE MAN WHO BROUGHT THE LEAD SAYS HE IS GOING FOUR DAYS DOWN THAT COAST ON THE FRIDAY IN HIS OWN CART ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT AND IS NOT WAITING AND HAS NOT BEEN ASKED TO WAIT, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAYS ONE WORD, BECAUSE THE PRICE WAS NAMED AND NOT PAID AND A PARTY WHICH HAS NAMED A PRICE AND NOT PAID IT DOES NOT GET TO CHANGE ITS MIND FOR NOTHING. THE LEAD DOES NOT COME BACK. NOBODY IN THAT SHED IMPROVES ON THAT.** The third of the three costs of a thing on the water is paid on the page: it takes a crew, a crew is people, and a party of two has no crew in it. The read-back runs.
5. **245 — a form with a name on it. PAID.** Thursday the fourth, Friday the fifth of March. **The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the third of six. THIRTY-ONE IS SAID OUT LOUD FOR THE FOURTH TIME IN SEVEN MONTHS, AT ABOUT SEVEN IN THE MORNING, AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, BY THE SHIP'S HAND, WITH THE THREE COUNTS AT TWENTY-TWO AND THIRTEEN AND ELEVEN IN ONE BREATH, THE REFUSAL OF THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH UNREVERSED, AND THE YARD SAYING IN THE SAME BREATH THAT IT WILL NOT SAY IT A FIFTH TIME.** A boat lies off the north side and a sealed envelope comes up the mole in a hand with a name on the outside of it, and nobody comes up the hill with it, and the name is **Halven Rook** and it is in the first column in full and he is in no room. **The form is careful: it is not a writ, not a licence, not a finding, nothing in it is a suspension and nothing in it is a penalty, a party which does not produce the thing on the day is not fined because a court does not fine a poor man and the matter simply goes on, a party producing the charter may enter in writing once any particular it wishes recorded, the party may not be required to produce any book of its own in any column, and nothing in it requires a party to say who altered anything or at whose instance or with what intent, and the party is not asked to say it and is not going to be asked to say it. THE CHARTER CAME OUT OF THE DRAWER AT ABOUT TWO IN THE AFTERNOON AND WENT DOWN THAT MOLE IN A HAND, AND THE HAND IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THIS BOOK SAYS ABOUT WHO TOOK IT.** A clerk's mouth keeps the two instruments apart a second time and says the harbor authority is not the office that can give that charter back and never was. A working day on the Friday.
6. **246 — the first drawer. PAID.** Saturday the sixth, Sunday the seventh of March. No rota day. **THE CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS MADE HERE AND IT IS NEW AND IT IS NOT AGED AND IT IS NOT EXPLAINED BY ANYBODY WHO COULD NOT HAVE INVENTED IT. A PAGE ABOUT THAT HARBOR IS MADE IN THAT HARBOR IN THE SHIP'S OWN HAND AND PUT IN THE DRAWER ON THOSE BENCHES AT ABOUT TWO IN THE AFTERNOON, AND IT SAYS ON ITS FACE THAT IT IS NOT A DOCUMENT AND NOT A RECORD AND NOT EVIDENCE AND NOT A RETURN AND NOT A COPY OF ANYTHING. FOUR SHEETS GO INTO THE ORDINARY POST AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR, ADDRESSED TO FOUR PLACES AND NOT ONE NAME, AND THE PRICE OF A GOING WAS NAMED BEFORE THE GOING AND IS FOUR DAYS THERE AND FOUR DAYS BACK AND ABOUT TWENTY-FOUR MARKS, AND THIS YARD HAS SENT NOBODY ANYWHERE. THE CHAPTER SAYS WHOSE HAND PUT THE PAGE IN AND WHAT THE OTHER FOUR CAN DO ABOUT IT, AND IT IS ONE PAGE IN ONE DRAWER IN ONE TOWN AND NOT FIVE.** A working day on the Sunday.
7. **247 — the agreement, and it has no name. PAID.** Monday the eighth, Tuesday the ninth of March. **The forty-fourth wipe, the wall down bare. The cistern is charged on the Monday and walked on none, being the fourth of six. The wage does not go in and the number of weeks fallen due is TWENTY, all twenty in the same breath.** A copyist of fifty-eight is asked, at her counter, and she answers because she was asked the other question first. **THE REASON THE AGREEMENT HAS NO NAME IS IN HER MOUTH: a name is a thing an office can be asked for and there is no office to ask, and that is the whole reason and there is not a second reason behind it. AND SHE SAYS THE PART ABOUT THE LIMIT, BECAUSE THE LIMIT IS FOUR PEOPLE'S AND NOT THIS YARD'S: a wall with no door in it is the only kind four people of that coast can stand behind, because there is no office on that coast that can put a door in it, and they gave it for nothing in August without knowing what it was worth.** And she says the price: a page in a drawer in five towns is a page nobody can check, and a record a man can check is worth what the man who checks it is worth, and there is no figure for either and there never has been, and she is not going to tell that yard it is a contradiction and is not going to tell it it is a good trade. **AND FIVE HANDS WRITE FIVE LINES ON ONE SHEET WITH NOTHING AT THE TOP OF IT, AND THE HOLDER OF THE WRIT'S HAND IS NOT ON IT.**
8. **248 — the question, a second time, and it is still not answered. PAID.** Wednesday the tenth, Thursday the eleventh of March. A working day on the Wednesday. **The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the fifth of six.** A man of about sixty of the first lay, forty-one years on that water, asks in a market in about forty people what an office that has kept records for three hundred years was guarding against at the point at which it decided what it was allowed to lose, and says he asked it in December and was told *this yard does not know* and is not going to wait for a man who is up a coast road. **THE YARD'S ANSWER THE SECOND TIME IS THREE FIGURES AND A REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND NO NAME IN IT, GIVEN IN THAT ORDER ON PURPOSE BECAUSE A FIGURE THAT IS RIGHT AND IN THE WRONG PLACE IS A LIE: NINE COMMUNITIES AND THE RECORDS ONE IN EACH, SIX CENTURIES OF THAT PRACTICE, THREE HUNDRED YEARS OF THE OFFICE THAT ANSWERS IT. NONE OF THEM MAY BE SWAPPED FOR ANOTHER AND THE OFFICE'S THREE HUNDRED YEARS WAS NOT HANDED TO THE COMMUNITIES. SHE SAYS OUT LOAD BEFORE SHE GIVES THEM THAT NONE OF THEM IS AN ANSWER AND THAT SHE IS NOT GOING TO CALL A FACT AN ANSWER, AND THE REASON IS A PERSON OF NO OFFICE AND NOT AN OFFICE.** And two more things in the same street, neither of them a victory: the Crown could not make this yard say who altered anything and was not asked to, and this yard cannot make any one of the four communities trust it and has not tried to.
9. **249 — five pages, five drawers, five hands. PAID.** Friday the twelfth, Saturday the thirteenth of March. No rota day. A working day on the Friday. **FOUR LINES FROM FOUR TOWNS, EACH A DIFFERENT THING DONE TO A PAGE IN A DRAWER, AND ALL FOUR ARE RIGHT: a kitchen on a Sunday to about nine people and never again; one person reading it and telling nobody; a page not opened since it came, with the keeper writing that down so that whoever reads it knows it was not opened and not that it was not looked at; a page copied out once and hung in a room people come into, with the page in the drawer. THIS YARD ASKED NONE OF THEM FOR AN ANSWER AND CANNOT GO AND LOOK IN ANY OF THE FOUR DRAWERS.** And at about a quarter past two a boat of about forty tons goes out with the man of the second lay in her and a mark on a line over her side, and about eleven people on that mole see her go. **THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS TAKEN HERE AND ALL THREE OF ITS COSTS ARE PAID ON THE PAGE: MAINTENANCE, BECAUSE A THING ON THE WATER HAS TO BE LOOKED AT AND NO FIGURE IN THAT COUNTRY CAN BE GIVEN FOR HOW MANY TIMES; PUBLIC EXPOSURE, BECAUSE A THING ON THE WATER IS A THING ON A WALL THAT MOVES AND ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE SAW IT GO; AND DEPENDENCE ON A TRAINED CREW, BECAUSE TWO MEN WERE PAID OUT OF THAT BAG FOR A DAY'S WORK THAT TWO OF THAT PARTY WOULD DO BETWEEN THEM ON A DAY WHEN THERE ARE TWO OF THEM, AND THE SEASON OF THE MARK IS NINE MARKS AND IS NOT GOING TO BE PAID AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ASKED FOR IT.** The case of five bells is not raised, and the limit four people of this coast wrote and signed is quoted in the yard's own first column and stands.
10. **250 — the volume closes. PAID, IN FULL.** Sunday the fourteenth, Monday the fifteenth of March. **A working day on the Sunday, and at a quarter past two a person goes out in a boat of about forty tons to look at a mark that has been fouled with about four inches of green and is making a small noise in a flat calm that a man on a mole could not have heard, and nobody struck it. THE FORTY-FIFTH WIPE. THE CISTERN IS CHARGED ON THE MONDAY AND WALKED ON NONE, BEING THE SIXTH AND LAST OF SIX. THE WAGE DOES NOT GO IN AND THE NUMBER OF WEEKS FALLEN DUE STANDS AT TWENTY, ALL TWENTY IN THE SAME BREATH. THE VOLUME'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE IS PAID HERE: FIVE DRAWERS IN FIVE TOWNS EACH WITH A PAGE IN IT AND NO TWO OF THEM WITH THE SAME PAGE; A PAGE GOING UP ON A MARKET WALL IN A TOWN FOUR DAYS UP THIS COAST WHERE THERE HAS NEVER BEEN ONE, CARRYING THE PLACE OF EVERY COPY OF ITSELF; A PERSON GOING OUT IN A BOAT; THE BOY NOT ON THE STONE AND THE THIRD COLUMN WITH A NAME IN IT BESIDE HIS HAND THAT IS NOT THE BOY'S AND IS NOT THE HOLDER'S; AND THE DELAY, A HAND'S WIDTH OF A SECOND, WITH NOBODY HAVING SAID WHY AND IT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWAY WITH A DATE AGAINST IT, WHICH IS NOT A MEASUREMENT AND NOT AN OCCASION. AND THE RESERVED SENTENCE IS SAID OUT LOUD IN A MARKET IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING BY A HERRING SKIPPER OF FIFTY-ONE OF THAT TOWN, AND IT IS THE LAST TRUE THING ANYBODY SAYS IN THIS VOLUME.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 250

- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this volume changes most, and neither of them says so, and the change in these twenty days is a change of standing and not of feeling, and it was bought with a cart.** She refused his sentence in the second column on the twenty-fifth of February and put her own there instead. She made a page about her own town and put it in a drawer in her own hand and said out loud on a mole's steps that if a person who keeps a page has to be somebody then it is her. She took a trade alone and paid two men out of the bag to do a day's work the two of them would do between them. She wrote his lead into the first column on the Wednesday and told him the lead does not come back. **He is up a coast road and has not been thanked and did not and could not, and she is on that mole and has not been thanked and is not going to ask, and one of them has been off the stone since the twentieth of February with four stitches in a right hand and has written every day of this batch in her left hand at about twice the time it takes her.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **Do not move.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, **occupied on six of the twenty days, being the twenty-sixth of February and the fourth, sixth, eighth, twelfth and fourteenth of March, and not occupied at any hour on the other fourteen**, not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and **Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the twenty days, and on fourteen of them he was up that coast road and not in that harbor, and both of those are entered and neither of them is a reason. THE FIGURES *NINE* AND *NINE* THAT THIS BULLET PREVIOUSLY GAVE ARE WITHDRAWN AND ARE NAMED AS WITHDRAWN; THE LIST AND THE METHOD ARE AT `state/continuity.md` § 6 AND § 17 ITEM 4.** A plate in eleven feet stays where it is and the note against it stands open.
- **Calder and Ors Kest.** Unchanged and in no room. **His office is named once, in Chapter 245, only as the office that granted the charter, and his own clerk says out loud that his office is not the office that can give it back and never was. HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY AND THE VOLUME'S CLOSING POSITION SAYS SO IN THOSE WORDS IN CHAPTER 250. A CHAPTER THAT SPENDS ANOTHER THING OF HIS MUST PAY FOR IT ON THE PAGE AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH SPENT ONE.**
- **Calder and Mara.** **In no chapter of these twenty days as a person, not in a room, not cited, quoted, produced or asked again, and no letter of hers came up that hill.** Her forty marks stand first after food and her six marks and two days stands as a price and not a debt, and neither has moved, and this yard has not asked her once in the twenty days ended on the fifteenth of March.
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing. **THE THIRD COLUMN WAS NOT FILLED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO IT AND NOBODY WAS HIRED TO READ A POSITION BACK, AND ON THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH A NAME WENT IN AT THE HEAD OF THAT COLUMN, BESIDE THE BOY'S HAND AND NOT OVER IT, IN THE SHIP'S HAND, AND IT IS NEITHER THE BOY'S NOR THE HOLDER'S. THE BOY IS NOT ON THE STONE.**
- **Calder and Pernel Saye.** One scene, on the eighth of March, at a quarter to nine, and it is the closest this yard has come to asking a trade a question that is not about a price. **She refused the question of the name only after answering it, and she said why, and she said the part about the limit, and she said the price, and she wrote the fifth of the five lines at half past seven and came up the hill for nothing and was not paid and did not ask. SHE WAS NOT TOLD WHAT A COLUMN IS AND DID NOT ASK. She has not been paid anything but nothing and there was no penny in the box on that morning, and the yard did not ask about the page in her own back room and is not going to.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-four who sells lime and chalk.** **He brought a lead, and the price was named before the day and not paid, and he went down the coast without waiting and was not asked to wait. The lead does not come back. He wrote the second of the five lines in this harbor on the Wednesday before he went and is in the country and not on this coast and cannot be in that room. He is not a villain and not on a ladder and was not cited as a witness to anything.**
- **Calder and the man of about forty-five who sells lime and chalk.** **One scene, at a quarter to two on the Friday the twenty-sixth, and he took the holder of the writ up a coast road on the Tuesday, and the two of them were in a cart together for ten days and this book does not go with them.** He asked one time in his life for somebody to come and look at a book of ground and got it, and the going out is the whole of the craft, and the reason he has never been asked twice is that he is sixty-one in August.

### The power state

**Line Diver. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND THE WORD IS ON NO PAGE OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS TAKEN, AND IT IS TAKEN IN CHAPTER 249, AND IT IS TAKEN ALONE, AND ITS THREE COSTS ARE ALL PAID ON THE PAGE IN THAT CHAPTER.** What the stage is, on the page: a mark is a bell, a frame, a line and a shackle, and it goes out on a boat and is set and let go, and a thing on the water is a thing on a wall that moves, and **a thing on the water has to be looked at and that is the first thing about the trade and is not the trade.** The book of hours of the thirtieth and thirty-first of October past stands at sixteen lines — nine pumps, four boats out, three boats in, with the hour against each and no reason against any of them — and it was not extended by anything in this batch. The sixteen lines are on the page in Chapter 249's second column and are the first thing about that trade and are not the trade. **No buoy went into the water on a day this yard did not pay for, no keeplight was extended, and the season of the mark at nine marks was not paid and is not going to be paid and nobody is going to be asked for it.** No person of this yard went in any water on any day of the twenty, nobody was in the water on any day of the twenty, no finding of worked glass was made, nothing was raised, and no return of any kind was made. **The word *seam* on a page of this batch is the mole's own second and fifth seams and a day of work at a seam, and is not the perception.** The standing fact is unchanged: a seam identifies difference and not truth. **AND THE ONE THING THIS BATCH DID TO THE HOLDER'S STANDING IS NOT A STAGE AND IS NOT A POWER: on the second of March he chose a living archive over a lead on his own dead, the lead does not come back, and nobody in that shed improved on it.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO BE.** The body is charged: a day lost to it on the twenty-fourth of February and a day lost to it on the twenty-eighth, both entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure, because there is no figure for a day. **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, are not struck out, and are in about sixty boats on that coast, and a request to strike a line out of a column was refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column, and a line does not come out of a column because it has been printed and cannot be got back.**
- **The bag is seventy marks, three shillings and one penny, being eleven thousand two hundred and thirty-seven pence, which is eight days at the face of the second seam since the twenty-fourth of February less four hundred and ninety-three pence gone out, and the figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks is ten thousand five hundred and ninety-seven pence.** The whole of what came into that yard in the twenty days ended on the fifteenth of March is three thousand eight hundred and forty pence, being eight days at the face of the second seam, all on hirers' own accounts, with nobody in the water, and the man of the second lay brought the pump and the man on every one of the eight, **and no two of the eight were worked by the same two people.** The whole of what went out in the twenty days is four hundred and ninety-three pence, and the whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December past is five hundred and twenty pence in six transactions at four counters.
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, and there are twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them.** Two wages of four marks were not paid in these twenty days, on the second and the ninth of March. The reason was entered once, on the twenty-ninth of December, and is not improved on.
- **The slate wall came down bare three times, being the forty-third, forty-fourth and forty-fifth Mondays since the first of May, on the first, eighth and fifteenth of March, all with the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting was held on any of them.**
- **The cistern was charged at no figure on six rota days and this party walked none of them: the twenty-fifth of February past and the first, fourth, eighth, eleventh and fifteenth of March instant. THE WALK IS NIL AND IT STAYS NIL, AND THAT IS THE TWENTY-NINTH OF THE CHARGES THIS PARTY HAS ENTERED WALKED ON NONE OF SINCE THE THIRD OF AUGUST PAST.**
- **The far bench is entered in all ten of the chapters and covers all twenty days, and it was occupied on six of them — the twenty-sixth of February and the fourth, sixth, eighth, twelfth and fourteenth of March — and was not occupied at any hour on the other fourteen. THE FIGURE *NINE* IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN, AND THE OLD LIST NAMED THE THIRTEENTH OF MARCH AS BOTH OCCUPIED AND NOT OCCUPIED. Not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the twenty days.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for forty-four nights, since the Sunday of the thirty-first of January, and it is the only bare thing in that shed, and the shape of that bench is the shape of a sheet and a half that came up that hill on foot on the ninth of December and came apart in a hand on the thirty-first and cannot be put back and cannot be bought.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and seventy-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the twenty days.**
- **THE WRIT OF THE FIRST OF MAY PAST CEASED TO BE A THING THAT PARTY HOLDS AT TEN MINUTES PAST MIDNIGHT ON MONDAY THE FIRST OF MARCH INSTANT, AND NOTHING TOOK ITS PLACE, AND NO COURT SAT, AND NO CLERK CAME UP THAT HILL, AND NOBODY WAS CHARGED WITH ANYTHING, AND NOBODY WAS FINED, AND NOBODY WAS REFUSED ANYTHING, AND NOBODY WAS EXAMINED. THE ONE-SEASON PROVISIONAL WORKING CHARTER OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF NOVEMBER PAST WENT OUT OF THAT DRAWER AT ABOUT TWO ON THE AFTERNOON OF THURSDAY THE FOURTH OF MARCH INSTANT AND DOWN THAT MOLE IN A HAND, AND THE HARBOR AUTHORITY IS NOT THE OFFICE THAT CAN GIVE IT BACK AND NEVER WAS. SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER, BEING THOSE FOUR AND THE CROWN FORM THAT WENT IN ON THE FOURTH IN PLACE OF THE CHARTER AND THE PAGE ABOUT THAT HARBOR THAT WENT IN ON THE SIXTH, AND THE PRINTER'S LETTER IS ONE OF THE FOUR AND IS NOT ON A BENCH, CHAPTER 209 HAVING PUT IT IN THE SAME DRAWER AS THE FORM AND NOT IN THE SAME PLACE. THE SHEET AND A HALF CAME APART IN THE SHIP'S HAND ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF JANUARY PAST AND IS IN PIECES AND IS NOT IN THAT DRAWER. THE SENTENCE *FIVE PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE FIFTH IS IN PIECES* IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NAMED AS WITHDRAWN; THE METHOD IS AT `state/continuity.md` § 17 ITEM 7.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved and unasked about and he is not in this book. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to this harbor's own bellwright, unargued, his chest unopened and no digit of anything he said on the second of July printed. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed with a name beside the boy's hand at the head of it. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, untouched and unoffered.
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND IT IS THE ONLY NEW ONE IN THIS SERIES SINCE THE WRIT. IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH INSTANT, IT IS A PRACTICE, IT IS NOT A REGISTRY AND NOT A COURT AND NOT A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND FIVE PAGES ARE IN FIVE DRAWERS IN FIVE TOWNS IN FIVE HANDS WITH NO TWO OF THE FIVE PAGES THE SAME PAGE. THE AGREEMENT ABOUT WHO MAY READ A PAGE HAS NO NAME AND THE REASON IS A COUNTER IN A ROOM OFF A FISH MARKET.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the volume's own last ten of them:** the living archive and the choice; the charter; the chain of custody; the agreement with no name and the reason; five pages in five drawers; the four communities' four readings; the question asked a second time and not answered; the third column's name; the delay written down with a date against it; the page on a market wall where there has never been one; a person going out in a boat; the Bellwright stage taken and paid for; thirty-one said out loud for the fourth time with the refusal of a fifth; the Second Bell sentence, said once, in a market, in about forty people, and it is the last true thing anybody says in this volume. **NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 05 IS OWED AFTER 250.**

**Still owed and carried into the Volume 05 close, which is owed them and not a chapter:** thirty-one on the chandler's note and not one of its three counts of weeks; three marks to a man of Ashtide; seven pence to this yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to this harbor's own bellwright; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor; forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, with the three nots of the eighth of June; forty marks first after food to a person of no office; twenty wages of four marks; **the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN**; the case of five bells at about five and a half fathoms inside four hundred yards on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of this coast wrote and signed; the delayed note's eleven logged occasions and two with no call in them and a hand's width of a second that has not moved; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper in this harbor or in that office's copying room answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road, which this volume did not decide; **THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION, WHICH WAS ASKED TWICE IN THIS VOLUME AND ANSWERED NEITHER TIME, AND WHICH THE VOLUME'S OWN FIRST LINE SAYS IS THE ONE THIS VOLUME DID NOT ANSWER**; and a lead about the holder's own brother four days down that coast, which does not come back and which nobody is going to chase.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the reason a refusal to hold is read as an intention to keep, which is paid and is a standing position; the question left standing at the close of Batch 0004, which is answered in a second-column fact and not improved on; the finding that a line of a page is a record of where the person was standing, which is paid and is not the compact and is not a conclusion; the four nines, which are four different things and may not be converted into one another; the fact that the practice this yard has been demanding had a name and the name is on one sheet in this country, which is paid and is not to be said in a market, in a room, or in this book again; **THE CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS NOT AND MAY NOT BE DATED BEFORE THE SIXTH OF MARCH; AND THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR IS NOT AVAILABLE AGAIN.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE VOLUME'S LAST PAGE: A WORKING HARBOR OF THIS COAST IS POORER ON THE FIFTEENTH OF MARCH THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, AND A YARD THAT HAS LEARNED ONE NEW TRADE IN TWENTY DAYS CANNOT YET PAY A MAN TO DO IT WITH, AND NOTHING THIS YARD DID IN TWENTY DAYS MADE ONE THING BETTER, AND NO FIGURE IN THAT HARBOR IS THE PRICE OF ANY OF IT.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 240

**Movement 4 is complete and its turn is paid. Movement 5 is the next writer batch and it is the volume's climax. The volume is not closed and the close is not owed.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **231 — the morning after the midpoint, and the first rota day of the month.** The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, and that is the first of six. The four pages have gone home and the bench under that pump is bare for the sixth night. **AND A THING HAPPENS THAT THIS YARD DID NOT ARRANGE: the first of the four comes back into the yard's own mouth.** Not the page — the first of the four is a night at the inside of a bar, and there is a light on a point, and a man of about forty of the third lay says at the head of that dock, in about nine people's hearing, that a man in a house on the far side of a place two days down this coast asked him what a yard in Morrow Quay had said in a shed about a light on a point, and that a man of the second lay told it to him at the head of that dock on the twenty-sixth of January and did not know then that it had come out of a shed. He says the line back when the holder asks him to, and the line is as it stands. **The holder gives three reasons out loud for not correcting it, and the last of them is that a correction is a reason and a reason does not go into a street.** The cost of the chapter is a night of the Thursday lost to the body, in the second column, with a reason against the line and no name in it. And the ship's hand says the thing this batch is built on: **a page has no door in it, and every word said out loud in a shed goes out of the door of that shed into a street in the time it takes to walk from a bench to a door, and neither of the two people in that shed thought about the door.**
2. **232 — the second, and what four places do with a thing that has been read.** Saturday the sixth and Sunday the seventh, no rota day and no charge on either. **Two of the other three are here and neither is a scene this yard is in.** One comes as a letter: four lines in a fair hand, nothing on the other side, no name at the foot of it, postmarked a place four days up this coast, saying that a sheet of this yard's own days is in three houses in that place and was read out in a kitchen in one of them on a Sunday to about nine people, and that **a place that has a yard's days in its houses ought to be asked which of them it wants and not told.** The other comes as a man of about fifty who walks up that hill on the Sunday morning and **does not come in**, stands four feet off the door with his hat in his hand, does not give his name, and says four men in a place two days down this coast have all read a page and none of them is going to put it down, and that the youngest of the four says it is the first thing anybody has shown him that says a place is allowed to decide things about itself and cannot say it out loud there, because the two who think it is a lie are his uncle and his master's brother. **They disagree, and the disagreement is entered in one sentence: one of them wants the asking done before, and the other says it has already been done after. This yard is in the middle of it with a board and a pump and no copy of anything, and is not writing to either of them.** No day of work was booked on either day and the reason is on the page.
3. **233 — the Third Bell form, and a market.** The fortieth wipe since the first of May, the wall down bare, no sitting, the clerk keeping his own page. The cistern is charged on the Monday and walked on none, the second of six. **THE SECOND BELL FORM OF THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER IS ANSWERED, IN A MARKET, IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND THE ANSWER IS NOT A SPEECH AND IS NOT A DEFENSE AND DID NOT PUT THE WRIT ANYWHERE NEAR IT.** It is answered in ten words by the ship's hand, standing where she can be seen, at the head of that dock and not on the boards: **it is here, and it was not sent on the day.** The holder of the writ did not go down the hill with her, stayed up it, and did not speak in that street that morning, and this yard is not on the boards and has never been. One line in that half sheet was not said in that market and is not going to be said in one, because a line on a piece of paper that came up a hill in the ordinary post is the paper's line and not this yard's. **The price is named at the top of that bench in the same afternoon and it is named after the answer and not before it: about forty people now know that this yard holds a copy of a record in a matter that stands before a court in a city, that it was not produced on the fourth of January, and that it is in a drawer in this town — and a yard that has spent five volumes saying that a thing nobody can check is worth nothing has this morning told a market where the thing it cannot check is.** The yard is entered against itself on the same page. **THE SENTENCE RESERVED TO THE VOLUME'S CLOSE — that a person who is not examined is not a person who has been refused — IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH AND IS NOT ANTICIPATED.** Whether the form goes back is not a thing anybody in this harbor can check and this yard is not going to check it. A wage of four marks did not go in and the weeks fallen due stand at **sixteen**, all sixteen in the same breath.
4. **234 — the room that is not free.** **THE HEARING ROOM OVER THE TIDE-GANG STORE IS USED AGAIN, THE TIDE GANG LOSES ANOTHER MORNING, AND THE PRICE IS NAMED OUT LOUD BEFORE THE YES BY A MAN WHO IS NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY.** The store under that room is shut from ten and one of the men who count the catch is a morning down, and that morning is named on the mole's steps and is not named in the room, and this party did not ask for the room and does not get the morning back. **The chapter says out loud why he may be in a room this month when he was not one last month**, and the reason is not a favour and is not a debt and is bigger than the thing he did on the tenth of December: his ledger is spent, his repair account has been empty since the middle of February, what is left is a reeve's own hand and a man's day out of a week, he has about three things left in it, and this one is about what a piece of paper is, and there is no office on this coast with an answer to that because the answer would be a figure and no figure in this country is worth what it costs to defend in four years. He names the price in front of about eleven people: five lines in chalk on a slate with a day and an hour, copied by the clerk into the file, and the slate comes down at eight on Monday whether there is a sitting in that room or not, **so the six words last one night and the only durable copy in the world is in this yard's own drawer.** He says he is not a friend of this party, has said so on those steps twice, and will not unsay it to get a thing seated in his own room, and if the yard tells anybody in a market that the reeve did it for them he will put on that slate that the reeve did it for nobody and that a man of fifty-eight with a fair hand is the one who did it for them. **The holder says in front of about eleven people that he is not going to read anything out of that book — not a page, not a column, not a line, and not the day.** **And the plate at the fifth seam stays where it is, the note against it stands open, and the only mechanism anybody has named for ever reaching it, including him, is a change of politics in an office and not a better letter out of that shed, and a letter can be improved on and a sentence cannot.** The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, the third of six. The read-back runs.
5. **235 — the copyist's other half, and the rest of the price. The one recovery in the batch.** A working day at the face of the second seam on the Friday, and the man of the second lay stayed for the whole of it for the first time since the eighteenth of January and gave no reason. **On the Saturday morning they go down the hill to a counter in a room off the fish market before the market is off the boards, because that counter is open from eight until the market is off the boards and on a Saturday the market is off the boards at about ten, and this yard had not worked that out before the sixth of December and worked it out on the seventh.** **THE THING PERNEL SAYE SAID ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JANUARY — that she would rather this party came back for in a month than that she had said it out — IS SAID, AND IT IS THE HALF SHE HAS NOT LOOKED AT IN THIRTY-ONE YEARS, AND IT IS WORSE THAN ANYTHING SHE SAID THAT DAY, and she says beforehand that it is about her and not about a page and that she is telling them because they asked the other question first.** She has a copy in her own back room that she made in the twenty-second year of that counter for a penny and fourpence for a man who said he would come back in a week and did not come back in nine years; she has never once looked at it and does not know what is on it; it is the only thing she has ever made that she cannot account for to anybody; and she refused the question in January not because she had no answer but because a person who has that in her house and asks a stranger which record is worth having is a person who is asking a stranger to sign for something. **She told two strangers and would not have told one.** The holder refuses all three of the obvious moves — not to see it, not to be told where it is, not to be offered it — and the reason is on the page and is not a favour: a page about a place in a shed on this mole is what this party did to four people, and if she said yes the yard would have a page it cannot check in a town it cannot get to, and if she said no she would have spent a night deciding, and neither is a thing this yard is entitled to put on a woman of fifty-eight before her market is off the boards. **She is the first party in four volumes that has offered her a book to take away, and she is not going to take it, and the reason is that in about four years she will have to be able to say she has not read it — and she read the first four lines at about half past seven that morning and put it back.** A sheet of paper is bought for one penny and the penny is entered: the third money this yard has spent since the eighteenth of December, being a penny on the eighteenth of December past, a penny on the twenty-eighth of January instant and this penny.
6. **236 — the thirty-eighth line. THE BATCH'S DISCOVERY, WHICH IS THE ONE THE WHOLE MOVEMENT WAS BUILT TO CARRY.** The forty-first wipe, bare; the cistern is charged on the Monday and walked on none, the fourth of six. The sheet comes off the shelf: a folded broadside about the size of a board, in that drawer since the eighth of August, printed in this harbor, gone up on the outside of the market wall on the fifteenth of August and off on the sixteenth, and **the only thing this yard has ever had in type.** Thirty-eight lines. Thirty-seven of them are days, the days from the sixteenth of June to the twenty-second of July, and thirty-three of those have a man's name at the end of them and four have nothing. The thirty-eighth line is at the foot, is not a day, was never a day, is the only line in the sheet this yard did not write for itself, and says that **there is a copy of this sheet in about sixty boats on this coast, that a man who has one and finds it changed is to say so to the yard that printed it at the head of this dock, and that any man may go in there and read that line and see where the other ones are.** **THE PARTY DISCOVERS THAT THE LINE WAS NOT A DEFECT AND WAS NEVER A DEFECT, AND THAT THE THING IT WAS AFRAID OF AND THE THING IT WAS PROUD OF ARE THE SAME LINE, AND THAT A MAN WHO BUILT IT IN JULY SAID SO IN A ROOM AND WAS RIGHT** — a compositor of forty-one says nobody asked him for it and gives back what the holder said to him on the fourth of August, that a page that cannot be checked unless somebody can find the other one was the point of it and it was going at the bottom where the man at the top cannot take it off, and he has set it four times since and there is one line in twenty-two years in his own book with no name on it and that one is this yard's. **And in the same breath comes the cost: four days in the middle of July are in that printed sheet, in about sixty boats, since the fifteenth of August, and this yard has read that column out at the head of that dock four times and has never once said out loud that four of the lines in the middle of it have got nobody's name at the end of them.**
7. **237 — the cost of a Tuesday, again, and a different shape.** No rota day. **The wage does not go in and the weeks fallen due stand at seventeen, all seventeen in the same breath.** **THE COST HAS A SHAPE OF ITS OWN AND IT IS NONE OF THE SIX THE LAST BATCH PAID AND NONE OF THE FIVE BEFORE IT: a day of a trade is lost by a person who is not in this yard and not in a street, and the figure is in that person's own book and is entered in the yard's first column because a man in this town can go and ask them, and the reason against the line is that a day this yard's money did not lose is not a figure this yard's money lost.** Two shillings and tenpence, twenty-two hours in two days entered as one day, on Monday the fourth of January, for a man who came into that room on that Monday and paid in advance and gave the name of a town and not the name of a man and wanted the sheet by the Tuesday, and wanted it read out at a funeral on the Thursday of that week, which was the seventh of January, because it was the only place he had where everybody was listening. **The holder will not say sorry to him and says why on the page: in about four years there is a man standing on a mole in another town who says that the yard of the writ on the west basin said sorry to a compositor for a day, and it will be true and it will be about a day that was lost and not one word of it will be about the thirty-eighth line, which is the only thing he actually did.** The compositor says the figure is not nothing, that in twenty-two years there has been one line in that book with no name on it and there are now two, and that he is not asking anybody to keep his book and is asking that it be left where it is and let it stand open. **The shape of sentence is said once in this batch, by the ship's hand, about that day and that funeral, and nobody remarks on it.** The night of the Wednesday is lost and is entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it, and she says she is telling him it happened on the night of the seventeenth because that is when she was asleep and that is the whole of the information this yard has about it.
8. **238 — the third of the four, and the forty of sixty. THE TURN OF THE MOVEMENT, AND IT IS THE TURN THE VOLUME'S OUTLINE NAMES.** The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, the fifth of six, and the sixth is entered as one left. A working day at the face of the second seam. **And at about six on the Friday evening, with the market gone in and about eleven people standing at the head of that dock, a man of about sixty of the second lay says something this yard has not been able to put down since, and he was not asked to say it and this party did not ask him anything and has not asked him anything before or since, and he is not a friend of this party, has not said he is, and is not on a list of anything.** He is a sailmaker and he has a boy of seventeen in one of the sixty boats, and he had four of the yard's sheet in his own kitchen and two of the four are different because they are different weeks of a thing that is still going. He is sixty and can read and has never learned to read a thing like that and went to a man in a room off the fish market and had it read to him for a penny and was refused a second reading for the same penny. **AND THEN HE SAYS IT: a list of names is a list of who can be asked what.** It is not a record;
