## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 220

**Movement 2 is complete and its turn is paid. Movement 3, the volume's midpoint, is the next writer batch. The volume is not closed and the close is not owed.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **211 — the days after a turn.** The compressor is looked at for the first time since the twentieth of October and the gland is the chapter: the part is on the machine, it holds, and there is no hose. **The yard declines to price a foot of hose and gives the reason, that a compressor in a harbor with no hose is a thing that makes noise.** The working question is answered on the page: a day at a seam is a pump, a line, a man on the pump and a slack water, and this yard has the line and two of them and a writ and has not got a pump, and the harbor's gear has no boat of its own. **The decision is the yard will take the next day that comes up the hill**, and the reason is that a yard which is findable has to be seen working and there is no way to be findable and be quiet about it.
2. **212 — the last Tuesday of the year.** The thirty-fourth Monday comes down bare. The cistern is charged and walked on none. **A man who was refused on the twenty-fifth comes back on the twenty-eighth and is told yes, in a doorway, and the reason is given out loud: on the Friday the holder could not say what he was doing on the Saturday morning and on the Monday he can say, and that is the whole of the change and it is not humility.** The day is worked. **On the Tuesday three marks come in and four marks do not go out, on the same column, on the same day, and the number of weeks fallen due is ten, all ten in the same breath, and the reason the wage is not paid is entered once, in the holder's own left hand, in the first column: a wage is a week and not a payment, and one week out of ten leaves a bag that pays one week and no other, and this yard has a page for a figure and does not want one.**
3. **213 — a thing that has to be built out of nothing.** Nineteen lines in a shipwright's hand, a list and not a plan, and every item on it a figure this yard cannot pay or gear it does not own, the seventh of them a hand. **The day's cost is entered against that day before the day is spent, and the day is spent, and what came of it is nineteen lines and a pencil and no agreement.** On the last afternoon a man says out loud at the head of the dock that this was the last day of the year and that a man ought to be able to say what he had done in it, and **neither of them answers him and neither of them says the day of the month, and the entry says that a day on which a thing is said in a street is a day on which a thing was said in a street.** Item eleven is said out loud in this yard's own book as a thing this yard cannot put in front of anybody. **No buoy went into any water and no stage of any kind was taken.**
4. **214 — the boy in a June berth that nobody in that crew has gone to see.** No day of the chapter is a scene in the berth. **The yard does not go, does not write, does not send anybody, does not ask anybody who has seen him what he said, and enters that with the reason of the fourth of October past.** A day of about three marks was offered and could not be taken and the figure is entered against no day at all. **The cost falls on a boat of about forty tons one hand short since the middle of July, out of one part owner's share: four marks, one shilling and eightpence, being six hundred and sixty pence, not coming back, and nobody going to ask this yard for it.** And a man of the third lay says the thing she was not going to ask him: **four men in that crew and not one of them has gone to see the boy who was in that boat in June, and he is one of the four.**
5. **215 — the fourth of January.** The thirty-fifth Monday comes down bare. **On the Sunday the month's being out is said out loud in a shed and answered with a sentence about the length of a month, and entered, and that is the only thing anybody in this batch says about a month or a year. ON THE FOURTH THE DATE ON THE HALF SHEET ARRIVED AND NOTHING HAPPENED, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS SO IN THOSE WORDS: no court sat, no clerk came up the hill, nobody was charged with anything, nobody was fined, nobody was refused anything, nobody was examined.** The reason is the reason of the seventh of December, and the half of it that is in the shed and not in a market is that the copy could be produced tomorrow and nothing whatever would happen to anybody and a clerk would have a piece of paper with this yard's name at the head of it.
6. **216 — the coast road's own figures, the refused licence, and item eleven.** **Eleven weeks fallen due, all eleven in the same breath.** A page off a printed sheet out of a press in a city is lying on the boards in this harbor under a stone and carries two figures for the bar of gravel side by side in the same weight of type, and **neither is withdrawn, the Kettle was not looked at, the refused licence stands unreversed and the thirty marks were not paid and are not owed to anybody and cannot be applied to anything.** A man of fifty-eight offers his own figure for that bar and **is refused, in the street, and the refusal is a refusal and not a request, and the figure is not in this yard's book.** The cost of the chapter is that **this yard's own method went out loud in a street in about nine people's hearing for the first time in four volumes.**
7. **217 — a hand at a counter, and the trade priced again.** The cistern is charged and walked on none. **The question is not about paper: what a yard of one and a half with about three marks in it can build, what a man has to know to keep a thing on the water, and how many days a year a thing on the water takes out of a working harbor.** A copyist prices what she can price and says plainly what she cannot, and the answer is that **a thing on the water is not a building, a building is made once and a thing on the water is a bill, and nobody can produce the number of times anybody is going to look at it.** She is not told what a second column is and does not ask, and no money of this yard went into that room. On the Friday the day is worked **on a pump a man brought up a hill, so that the three marks is for the hands and the line and the tide and not one penny of it is for a machine.**
8. **218 — what a refusal to hold is read as. THE BATCH'S CLIMAX.** **A man of sixty-eight offers a shelf in a dry room with a firebox and a lock above a chandler's, for nothing, in good faith, and is refused in the open with the reason given in the open, and the price of giving the reason is named before it is given.** The reason is that a shelf in a man's room is a favor and a favor is a thing with a man at the end of it. **And the no is read as an intention to keep, by two men of the first lay who were standing there, and the yard cannot correct it without putting a name on something, and this time the thing it would have to name is not four people on a weir and not a reason — it is that the only way to be read correctly is to have somewhere to put it that is not a hold, and this yard has not got one and is not going to build one in a fortnight. The three sentences a man can say in a street are given and every one of them is wrong. THE GAP IS NOT CLOSED AND THE CHAPTER SAYS ON THE PAGE THAT IT IS NOT CLOSED, AND THAT THE ANSWER IS A HOLE, AND A HOLE IN A STREET FILLS ITSELF.**
9. **219 — the cost of a day, again, and a different shape.** The thirty-sixth Monday comes down bare, the cistern is charged and walked on none, **the far bench is occupied from about ten until about four and neither brother goes over.** The day is worked. **The cost has a shape of its own and it is none of the five: a man of thirty-one took his own name off a list in a book in the next town down this coast, a woman in an office wrote it off with a pen in about four seconds, a man is not asked at that place again, that is not a day and not a wage and cannot be put back by anybody, and about six marks is behind it. THE NAME IS IN THE SPEAKER'S MOUTH AND IS NOT IN THIS YARD'S BOOK, AND THE REASON IS ENTERED AGAINST THE LINE.** Twelve weeks fallen due, all twelve in the same breath.
10. **220 — the turn.** The cistern is charged and walked on none and the far bench is entered as not occupied. **A corner of the sheet and a half is gone soft about the width of two fingers, and the yard did not lift it off the bench and gave the reason on the page: there is nowhere in this harbor to lift it on to.** The cost of the three weeks is read out in one breath and every item in it is a figure. **And then the third entry goes in the first column, in the holder's own left hand, with the date and the hour on it: a refusal to hold is read as an intention to keep; the only way to be read correctly is to have somewhere to put it that is not a hold; this yard has not got one, knows what one would cost, and is not going to pretend it knows the cost of a thing it has not built. A question is left standing that this party is not answering in a market, in a room, or in this book. THE BATCH'S LAST LINE IS A FACT AND NOT A RESOLUTION AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED IMPROVED ON IT.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 220

- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this volume changes most, and neither of them says so, and the change in these twenty days is a change of work and not of feeling.** She wrote nineteen lines on a board with her back to the wind and stopped at the seventh because a hand is a person. She said the day could not be taken, on a mole's steps, and nobody knows why but the two of them and the second column. She said the gap between a refusal and a correction cannot be closed and would fill itself. **She has not been thanked and is not going to ask, and he has not thanked her and is not going to and did not.**
- **Calder and the man of the first lay with the lock-up.** A new and unnamed relationship, and it is the batch's turn standing on its own two feet: a man who offered the best thing this harbor has and is going out of it in the spring, and a yard which refused him in a street and is not going to be asked again. **He is not a friend of this party and has not been asked to be and is not on any ladder.**
- **Calder and Ors Kest.** Unchanged. **He is in no room in this batch and was not asked for anything, because he said on the tenth of December past that he was not going to do that twice inside a month without saying so out loud first, and it is inside a month. He is still not a friend of this party.**
- **Calder and Mara.** **She is in no chapter of these twenty days as a person, is not in a room, is not cited, quoted, produced or asked again, and no letter of hers came up that hill. Her forty marks stand first after food and her six marks and two days stands as a price and not a debt, and neither has moved.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the head of the third column keeping his hand. **The batch came closest to him it ever has and it did it by not going: a boat of the third lay is a hand short because of him, four marks and a change and eightpence came out of a man's share because of him, and this yard did not go, did not write, did not send anybody, and did not ask anybody who has seen him what he said. And in the list of nineteen lines the only other name this yard has is not on it, and his name is on nothing in this batch.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **Do not move.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, occupied on one day of these twenty and entered as not occupied on six others, not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, **and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the twenty days. A plate in eleven feet stays where it is and the note against it stands open.**
- **Calder and the two men of the first lay.** **Three days out of five weeks, and no fourth out of nothing.** The yard went up on none of the three, has got neither name, has asked neither of them anything, and is not going up that hill for it. **And the reason against all three lines is the reason of the seventeenth of December: a correction is the reason, and the reason does not go into a street.**

### The power state

**Line Diver. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND THE WORD IS ON NO PAGE OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS. NO STAGE OF ANY KIND WAS TAKEN, AND THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS NOT TAKEN, NOT NAMED, AND NONE OF ITS THREE COSTS DISCHARGED: the book of hours of the thirtieth and thirty-first of October stands at sixteen lines and is not extended, the nineteen lines are a list of materials and not a stage, a thing on the water is entered as a bill and not as an instrument, and this yard has not got a hand to go and look at one and says so on the page. NO BUOY WENT INTO ANY WATER AND NO KEEPLIGHT WAS EXTENDED. No person of this yard went in any water on any day of the twenty, no finding of worked glass was made, nothing was raised and no return of any kind was made. The word *seam* on a page of this batch is the mole's own second and fifth seams and a day of work at a seam, and is not the perception.** The standing fact is unchanged: a seam identifies difference and not truth.

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO BE.** The body is charged: **a day of about three marks was offered on Friday the first of January and could not be taken, the figure is entered against that day and against no day at all, and the reason is in the second column with no name in it and is not going to have one.** **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, and are not struck out, and a request to strike a line out of a column is refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column.**
- **The bag is sixteen marks, six shillings and four pence, being two thousand six hundred and thirty-six pence, which is four days at the face of the second seam since the sixth of December and one penny out since the eighteenth of that month. NOTHING WENT OUT OF THIS YARD IN THESE TWENTY DAYS. The figure the bag is short of the wage went the wrong way twice and is one thousand nine hundred and ninety-six pence.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, and there are twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWELVE weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them. Three wages of four marks were not paid in these twenty days. The reason was entered once, on the twenty-ninth of December, and is not improved on.**
- **The slate wall came down bare three times, being the thirty-fourth, thirty-fifth and thirty-sixth Mondays since the first of May, on the twenty-eighth of December, the fourth of January and the eleventh of January, all with the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting was held on any of them.**
- **The cistern was charged at no figure on six rota days and this party walked none of them. The walk is nil and it stays nil, and the charge of the ninth of November past stands entered with no figure against it.**
- **The far bench is entered in six of the ten chapters, covering twelve of the twenty days, and occupied on one of them, being the eleventh of January. It is not claimed on the other eight days, and every not-occupied line carries no figure of what came before it.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and fifteen days up the crown of the mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved. The party went past both of them twice and touched neither.**
- **A copy of a said record was to be produced to a court in a city on the fourth of January and was not produced, and nothing happened, and this party asked no office for anything in aid of it, sent nothing to a city, did not write to a man in a coat, and has not been to the counter of that circuit office since the twenty-fourth of November 2026.**
- **Five pieces of paper are in this yard's hands and none has been answered: the copy of a record, the acknowledgment, the form of the court, the form of an unnamed office in a city which is going soft on a bench under a pump, and a printer's letter with one question in it. The chandler's note is at thirty-one and was not said out loud in these twenty days. Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved and unasked about. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to this harbor's own bellwright, unargued, his chest unopened and his number unprinted. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor, with her name on the figure. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, untouched and unoffered.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid none of it:** thirty-one on the chandler's note and not one of its three counts of weeks; three marks to a man of Ashtide; seven pence to this yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to this harbor's own bellwright; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor; forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, with the three nots of the eighth of June; forty marks first after food to a person of no office; twelve wages of four marks; the plate at the fifth seam, which stands at eleven feet in this mole's own foundation stone, seen and not measured and not touched, **THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN**; the case of five bells at about five and a half fathoms inside four hundred yards on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of this coast wrote and signed; the delayed note's eleven logged occasions and two with no call in them and a hand's width of a second that has not moved; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper in this harbor or in that office's copying room answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the new-volume question; and the volume's final chapter image, which is the close's work and is not rounded up by anybody.

**Owed to the yard, and this batch put a figure on it for the first time in four volumes:** **what a place that is not a hold is, and who would keep it, and what it costs, and where the money comes from in a harbor where the mole-head light is not on because a light costs oil.** **THE ENTRY SAYS THIS PARTY IS NOT GOING TO ANSWER THAT IN A MARKET, IN A ROOM, OR IN THIS BOOK, AND IT IS MOVEMENT 3'S AND LATER MOVEMENTS' WORK.**

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the reason a refusal to hold is read as an intention to keep, which is paid; the fact that a man with a firebox and a key is going out of it in the spring, which is paid; the fact that a name came off a list in another town, which is paid; the fact that a corner of a sheet and a half has gone soft, which is paid and irreversible; and the fact that this yard has not got a place to put a page in, which is a standing position and not an event.

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE NEXT BATCH:** **a chain of custody is a jurisdiction and it is new, and it does not exist before Movement 5 puts it in, and no chapter of Movements 1 to 4 may describe one. Nothing in these twenty days is one.** What this batch has is a drawer in a shed with four pieces of paper in it and a store room above a chandler's with a firebox and a lock, and the yard refused the second of them in a street.

## The Volume 03 close and its audit — as AUDITED, 27 September 2026, and the Volume 04 hand-off

**`reviews/volume-03/volume-03-close.md` is the audit and is the home of every ruling below. Nothing in this section is new canon; it is the audit's account of the canon, and where it corrects a figure it says so on its face.**

- **VOLUME 03 IS CLOSED. Every clause of `outline/volume-03.md` is PAID, PART, RULED or NOT ATTEMPTED with the reason, and nothing is owed to Volume 03 and nothing is owed to a chapter that has not been written. THE VOLUME MEASURES 154,738 WORDS ACROSS FIFTY CHAPTERS, in five batches of 29,905 / 30,356 / 33,738 / 30,916 / 29,823, measured with `wc -w` on 27 September 2026 and re-measured after the audit's eleven repairs.**
- **THE CENTRAL PRESSURE IS RULED RESOLVED AND RESOLVED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE OPENING, AND IT WAS THE PUBLICATION AND NOT THE CUTTER.** The cutter did not erase the map; it emptied itself in the open over a market wall. **The volume's own argument — that a route is public or it is nothing — is not the argument the outline asked for and is a better one, and the outline is not amended.** The cost of the map was the map's only advantage, and the cost is a sentence that cannot be said again.
- **THE CLIMAX IS RULED DISCHARGED IN A DIFFERENT FORM AND THE CHAPTER'S FORM IS STRONGER.** There was no claim to surrender and no salvage to abandon: the purpose was entered in the first column in advance as *to get four persons off her and to nothing else*. **The case was in his hands and he let go of a line round his own forearm when a boy of seventeen went off a foredeck, and the loss is irreversible, no other finding is substituted for it, and the cost fell on a wage of four marks that was not paid, on three marks owing to a man of Ashtide, and on the sentence.**
- **THE BELL-ARCHIVE IS RULED THE VOLUME'S BEST PIECE OF CONSTRUCTION AND THE AUDIT AGREES.** The community is one of the nine the volume's own books name: **the Sill, this harbor's own weir, whose sill stone is under four feet of stone at the south end of this mole and a foot and four inches above the third of the six joints, and four of that community's people came up the mole's steps on the tenth of August.** The archive is five bells under an after hatch, not a set, a line cut into the lip of each, read out aloud rather than written down, in a hall, in front of the people it is about.
- **THE CONCRETE RESOLUTION IS PAID IN ALL FOUR OF THE OUTLINE'S ELEMENTS, IN THE OUTLINE'S ORDER, AND NONE WAS WAIVED.** A longer leash with a name on it: a man in a coat named Amos Trewhella came up a hill on the twelfth of August with a paper, **and the second season of the writ is still not granted and the writ still runs to the first of March.** A boy who cannot do the thing he was kept for, in the yard's own hand, dated the first of August. A conservator who is not on the crew and is owed forty marks. A question about who changed a rule, asked in a market and not answered, with the not-answering on the page.
- **THE FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE IS PAID IN ALL NINE ELEMENTS AND THE AUDIT AGREES WITH THE CHAPTERS ON BOTH OF THE TWO THE OUTLINE LEFT UNSETTLED.** The nine communities are carried as nine **places** and the thing is called nothing, and the word *Harbors* is not on the page anywhere; and *under a naval paper* is settled in the prose by a sheet that goes up on the outside of whatever is there, and the shipwright refuses to pretend a sheet under a naval paper is a sheet on its own.
- **OF THE TWENTY-EIGHT LOCKS, NONE IS BREACHED. ONE IS AMENDED (L5). TWO ARE HELD IN ANOTHER FORM AND IN A STRONGER ONE (L8, the bell; and the chart and its notation). TWENTY-FIVE HOLD.**

### The one ruling that is the most important thing in the audit — LOCK L5

**LOCK L5 IS AMENDED. THE CLAUSE STANDS. THE ENUMERATION IS SUPERSEDED BY THE CHAPTERS. THERE ARE FOUR RETURNS IN VOLUME 03 AND THERE WAS NO FIFTH, AND THE FOURTH IS CANON.** Return 1, Thursday the fourth of May, two days late. Return 2, Wednesday the tenth of May, on the day. Return 3, Saturday the seventeenth of June, on the day. Return 4, **Friday the fourteenth of July, on the day, out of a finding of Monday the tenth** — the day of the finding is not counted and the fourth day after the tenth is the fourteenth, and the counting rule was spoken out loud on the page and the party entered that it was not going to try to move the date. **All four were caught by the first limb of the clause by itself, and the party has not needed the second limb and does not know that it would.**

**NOTHING IS RECALLED, NOTHING IS CORRECTED, NOTHING IS UN-SAID AND NOTHING IS RE-SENT.** A return states a fact and not a conclusion, and a document already in a circuit office's file cannot be withdrawn by a party deciding to amend its own bookkeeping. **The clerk's own page has said four in his own hand since Friday the fourteenth of July, because he keeps his own page and because he said what a box holds. THE RECORD IS ALREADY TRUE. A VOLUME'S INTERNAL BOOKKEEPING IS NOT A RECORD, AND A LOCK IS NOT A DOCUMENT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE RULING.** The amended form is written into `outline/volume-04.md` lock L5 and governs every later volume.

### The other thirteen rulings, each dated 27 September 2026

1. **The condition's onset is the FOURTEENTH of October 2025 and not the thirteenth, and the three things on that date are three different things and may never be fused: the dive was the night of the THIRTEENTH; the onset is the FOURTEENTH; and the order and the seizure were the FOURTEENTH at half past six in the morning.**
2. **The join's physical facts, re-derived:** six joints at about four fathoms on the second seam's own face, landward of the third seam's mark, in a straight line, **a string with two pins in it coming to three hundred and fifty-one feet**, fouling of a quarter of an inch, a quarter, three inches and a quarter, three inches and a quarter, nine inches, and three inches and a quarter, in that order from the root end of the crevice to the seaward end, and **three thicknesses of fouling is three and the party does not know how many more and is not going to arrange them into a figure.** **The nine fastenings are not a mark of nine joined lines and the nine places are not the Nine Harbors, and neither may be converted into either.**
3. **The nine places as the page carries them**, and **the three with no joint are still owed a placement in a later volume as a fact and not as an identification, and the party does not know why the three are there and is not going to guess.**
4. **What a chip of worked glass carries is STILL OPEN BY DESIGN and stays unread.** **The six marks and two days and the yard's inability to pay are both on the page, and a later volume that reads the chip must have somebody paid six marks and two days and the party must not have paid them.**
5. **The figure on the bar of gravel:** the yard's is two and three-quarters, made once on the second of May; **Rowan Trewin's is two and a half, made four times in nineteen years; both are in a press in a city and neither is withdrawn and this volume does not decide which is right**, and the man who is wrong about one thing the yard cannot do one single thing about is the yard itself.
6. **The glass storm's two written occurrences stand in two hands on two pages that are not on top of each other, and no cause is named in any volume.**
7. **The delayed note: eleven and two stand, neither is advanced, the answer is reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint, and the delay is a hand's width of a second with nobody having said why.**
8. **The coast road's four figures, the pilot's two, the Kettle not looked at, and the yard's refused licence: the road is published and cannot be un-published and is not resolved in Volume 04 either.**
9. **The custody items: three, digits never quoted, the municipal claim on the third stands, and the live question — what a municipal claim does to a presumed Crown material — may not be answered by a clerk in this volume or any other.**
10. **The ninth seam's end of the first of September falls seventeen days after the volume closes and is Volume 04's first movement, and an office whose instruments nobody contests has now entered three things in its own book and every one of them cost somebody who was not in the room.**
11. **THE ATTRIBUTION OF THE VOLUME'S CLOSING SENTENCE. NO FISHER IN VOLUME 02 IS RECORDED AS HAVING SAID IT.** It is Calder Marr's in a room in Volume 02, Chapter 97, and the same shape is Ors Kest's in a room in Chapter 58, **and neither man is a fisher.** **The outline's clause is DISCHARGED AND NOT VARED: Volume 03 gave it to three people in three mouths, put a herring skipper in the last of them, in a market, on the last page but one, and the sentence's origin is settled at Volume 02, Chapter 97, in a hearing room.**
12. **THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JULY 2026 IS A FRIDAY.** Two state files and one prompt called it a Tuesday. **The chapters are right and the state files are corrected in place, and the warp is taken on Friday the twenty-eighth of July in Chapter 141, on the page, in two places.**
13. **THE FOUR ITEMS BATCH 0005 FLAGGED AND DID NOT APPLY ARE DISPOSED OF:** the two *everything in her* clauses are open by design and are not Volume 04's; **the five bells may be supplied a way at a price and the price must fall on somebody who is not the yard, and no harbor authority, no office in Veyr and no person with a seal may supply one**; **the relief lands on the fifteenth of August and the posting begins on the first of September and the fortnight between them is the only thing about the posting that is not decided;** and the attribution is at item 11 above.

### The hand-off to Volume 04 — six open threads and no more

1. **Mara Venn's break with the Registry, which is Volume 4 and is a DIFFERENT EVENT from her leaving this crew. No chapter of Volume 03 fused them and no chapter may fuse them now.**
2. **The third column, the boy, and the pencil.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, **and the yard's own book says in its own hand and with a date that he cannot do the thing he was kept for, and that entry binds a later volume as much as this one.** The third column was not filled on the eighth of August and nobody has been appointed.
3. **The ninth-line mark, which closes in Volume 5 and not before.**
4. **The question about who changed the rule**, asked in a market in this harbor on the thirteenth of August and not answered.
5. **The second season of the writ and the first of March, and the first of September, and a wage that was not paid on the fifteenth of August and three marks owing to a man of Ashtide.**
6. **The five bells at about five and a half fathoms inside the four hundred yards, and the four people of the Sill who own them and who have no boat, and the fact that no instrument in this harbor reaches that water, no money in this harbor reaches that water, and no trade on this coast whose work it is.**

**Carried forward in `outline/volume-04.md` and named there and NOT in this six, so that the hand-over stays at six:** the second-column bare fact and the spent naming of the twentieth of July; the lead plug, the bellwright and the undertaking; the coast road, the pilot and the Kettle; the delayed note's eleven and two; the custody items and the live question no paper in this harbor answers; the plate at the fifth seam and the refused plan of the seventeenth of January; the chart and its bell notation in a vessel's keeping; the two objects of nobody's on the mole's crown and the marking on one of them; the three places with no joint; the shard of worked glass nobody can read; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant; **and the harbor's poverty, which is not fixed for anything and must not be fixed in Volume 04 either.**

### The eleven mechanical repairs, listed

**Four weekday faults against lock L1** — Ch 106 (*Monday the ninth to Sunday the fifteenth* of May → *Tuesday the ninth to Monday the fifteenth*); Ch 115 (*the Thursday the fourth of June* → *the Sunday the fourth*, with six words added saying it was not a rota day, because the chapter's own seventh line says the boat came in on the Sunday the fourth); Ch 119 (*not on the Thursday the nineteenth* → *not on the rota day, the nineteenth*, and the fourth of June moved off the rota, which it was not on); **Ch 143 (*on Tuesday the fourth of May* and *on Monday the eleventh of May* → *Thursday* both, which is what the grid gives and what makes them a weekly pattern in the four days before the boy went off the stone).**

**Six wrong letters** — Ch 115 *harbourmaster* → *harbormaster*; Ch 120 ×4 and Ch 130 ×1, *licence* → *license*. **A search of all fifty chapters for the whole British-spelling class now returns nothing at all.**

**Two duplicated paragraphs**, against the `AGENTS.md` Quality Gate — the sixty identical words describing a return's jacket in Ch 121 and Ch 134, and the twenty-two-word cistern line opening Ch 136 and Ch 141. **In each pair the first instance is left exactly as it is and stands as the device, and the second is varied in the yard's own idiom with no fact added and no fact removed. A byte-comparison of every paragraph of twelve words or more across the fifty chapters now returns ZERO duplicates.** Thirty-six exact repeated sentences remain and every one is the volume's own device — the two-column read-out, the six conditions read at the boat in the same words because the lock requires it, two Crown notices quoted verbatim, and twelve stock sentences of the house about a town that does not change. None is repaired and the reason is recorded at § 21d of the audit.

### The four state-file figures corrected by the audit

**Batch 0003 was given as 33,731 words with Chapter 123 at 3,835 and is 33,738 with Chapter 123 at 3,842** — the batch's count was taken before the last of that batch's review repairs was applied and was never recomputed, which is the same class of error the Volume 02 audit found in its own Batch 0002 figure. **Batch 0002 is 30,356 and not 30,345; Batch 0004 is 30,916 and not 30,890; Batch 0005 is 29,823 and not 29,814**, the three having moved by the audit's own repairs. **The volume total had never been measured and is 154,738.** All four are corrected in place with the reason on their face, in this file, in `state/chapter-summaries.md` and in `state/continuity.md`.

(a) A MECHANISM OF THIS SHAPE IS NEW TO THE PAGE AND IS NOT PRE-EMPTED: CHAPTERS 1 TO 150 SAY ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT THE SECOND BELL, NO OFFICE THAT EXAMINES IS EVER NAMED, NO EXAMINATION IS EVER SAT, AND THE WORD *NOT EXAMINED* IS ON NO PAGE BEFORE CHAPTER 200. (b) THE LOSS IS THE PARTY'S OWN DOING AND THE YARD ENTERED IT IN ITS OWN LEFT HAND BEFORE ANY FIGURE OF ANY KIND AND SAID IT WAS NOT GOING TO BLAME THE WRIT. (c) NO LATER CHAPTER MAY MOVE IT ONTO THE WRIT, MAY SAY THE COURT REFUSED HIM ANYTHING, MAY SAY THE COURT FOUND AGAINST HIM, OR MAY SAY HE HAS SAT THE EXAMINATION SINCE SEPTEMBER 2025 — AND THE FORM SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF ALL FOUR AND THE FORM IS THE AUTHORITY. 5. **The five bells at about five and a half fathoms inside the four hundred yards, on nobody's schedule, and the four people who own them and who hold a limit this yard has not asked twice to have lifted.**
6. **Mara Venn's forty marks, first after food, unpaid, and the letter of the twenty-seventh of November in which she priced an ask and refused it and told this yard not to ask again this winter** — and the answer is not a purchase, not a forgiveness and not a repair, and the yard did not tell her about the copy and is not going to.

**AND WHAT A VOLUME 05 WRITER INHERITS FROM THREAD 6, STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISSED: a woman of no office, thirty, owed forty marks first after food and six marks and two days as a price, who has refused in writing to be cited, quoted, produced or asked again; who has told this yard not to ask her again this winter; whose price for the November letter was that it be kept, that what she wrote go in the second column with a reason against the line, and that not one word of it go in a market. A Volume 05 chapter may not ask her for anything before the winter is out, may not put her in a room, may not fuse the refusal with the copy, may not reduce either figure, and may not make the forty marks a purchase, a forgiveness or a repair.**

THE CHAPTER'S WORDCOUNT IS UNCHANGED AT 4,252, SO NO BATCH FIGURE AND NO VOLUME FIGURE MOVED. NO SCENE, TURN, COST, MOVEMENT BOUNDARY OR PLANNED BEAT WAS TOUCHED, AND NO CHAPTER WAS ADDED.**
- **THE CENTRAL PRESSURE IS RULED RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED IN A DRAWER AND NOT IN A SPEECH. The Crown's claim arrives as a form's printed text and was made true enough to be dangerous and was never once made false: it is not able to make a copy safe in a place where the copy cannot be checked, and it does not say a copy is unsafe anywhere else, it says it does not know about anywhere else. ONE IS NOT PAID AND IS CARRIED OPEN (L7). SEVEN ARE HELD IN A FORM NARROWER OR BROADER THAN THE LOCK ASKED FOR AND EACH IS RULED (L1, L3, L11, L15, L21, L23, L28). TWENTY-SEVEN HOLD EXACTLY.**

### The one ruling that is the most important thing in the audit, and it is the third volume to make it — LOCK L7, THE PLATE NOTE

**LOCK L7 IS NOT PAID. IT IS PART. IT IS CARRIED OPEN. IT IS NOT WAIVED AND IT IS NOT RE-OPENED TO GET A DIFFERENT ANSWER, AND THE REASON IS THE VOLUME 04 AUDIT'S AND NOT A NEW ONE.**

The plate is in eleven feet in the mole's own foundation stone, seen and not measured and not touched, in twenty-five chapters; the note stands open in the same twenty-five; no chapter of the fifty reached it, measured it, touched it, asked about it, or closed it, and no chapter reached it by writing a better letter. **THE DOCUMENT THAT WOULD HAVE CLOSED IT IS SPENT AND IT WAS SPENT IN AN EARLIER VOLUME, ON THAT VOLUME'S MOVEMENT 3's TURN, IN THREE CHAPTERS, WHERE IT WAS PRODUCED, QUOTED, DESCRIBED AND SUMMARISED, AND IT IS ON NO PAGE OF VOLUME 05: the phrase *risk management* returns nothing across the fifty chapters and the page that went out of a file is produced, quoted, described or summarised nowhere in them.** **A DOCUMENT PRODUCED ONCE IN THIS SERIES IS SPENT.**

**AND THE ONE THING A LATER VOLUME CANNOT IMPROVE ON IS NOW ON THE PAGE: the volume said out loud in a character's mouth that the only mechanism anybody has named for ever reaching that plate is a change of politics in an office and not a better letter out of a shed, and a letter can be improved on and a sentence cannot.** RULED AND BINDING.

### The third-column tension, ruled in the prose and not in the author's head

**`outline/volume-05.md` lock L21 says no Volume 05 chapter may fill the third column, appoint anybody to it, or scratch the boy's hand out of the head of it. THE SAME FILE'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE SAYS THE CLOSE HAS THE THIRD COLUMN WITH A NAME IN IT THAT IS NOT THE BOY'S AND IS NOT THE HOLDER'S. THE CHAPTERS PAID BOTH, IN CHAPTER 250, ON THE PAGE: a name went in at the head of the column, beside the boy's hand and not over it, in the ship's hand, and it is neither the boy's nor the holder's; the column is not filled; nobody is appointed; nobody is hired to read a position back; the boy keeps his hand and is not on the stone; and the chapter says which of the two things is happening, and enters the reason, being that a column with a hand at the head of it and no name is a column that any clerk with a pen can fill.**

**RULED: BOTH CLAUSES ARE SATISFIED, BECAUSE THE THING THE IMAGE ASKS FOR IS A NAME AT THE HEAD OF A COLUMN AND NOT A LINE IN IT. THE RESOLUTION WAS DONE IN THE PROSE AND NOT IN THE AUTHOR'S HEAD, AND THE FAULT IS A FAULT IN THE PLANNING FILE: THE PROMPT WHICH DISPATCHED BATCH 0005 AND LOCK L21 ARE IN THE SAME FILE, AND THE NEXT AUDIT WILL FIND THE SAME FAULT IN ANOTHER VOLUME IF NOBODY SAYS IT HERE.** RULED AND BINDING.

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 210

**VOLUME 05 MOVEMENT 1 IS WRITTEN, CHAPTERS 201 TO 210, TWENTY CONSECUTIVE DAYS FROM SUNDAY THE SIXTH TO FRIDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF DECEMBER 2026. ITS TURN IS PAID. NOTHING IS RESOLVED AND NOTHING IS WON, AND THE BATCH'S LAST LINE IS A FACT AND NOT A RESOLUTION.** In twenty days a yard of one and a half was handed a form with no signature and no date on it by a man who did not give his name, heard the Crown's position in one sentence, asked a reeve in a street what his office thought of a thing and got an answer and a price that fell on the reeve's own office, worked a day at a seam, put its own eleven-line list beside a form and found that the list is the answer and that the answer is a list it cannot put in an answer, said something in a street that was read as an intention to keep and could not be taken back, paid a penny at a copyist's counter for two figures it could not get any other way, was told the price of a man's day by a man with a lighter before anybody asked for it, and had a printer's letter up a hill with one question in it and put it in a drawer, and then understood on the twenty-fifth, in its own left hand, what it has been asked to be.

### The movement's own beats, ten of ten, in the order the volume outline gives them

1. **THE FORM CAME UP THIS HILL ON WEDNESDAY THE NINTH OF DECEMBER**, a sheet and a half, brought on foot by a man in a coat who stayed unnamed and who gave the reason a clerk of the circuit office gave at the same bench on the twenty-third of November: a man's name at the foot of a thing is a thing a man in a city can hold for four years. **There is no signature anywhere and no date at the head, none in the body and none at the foot, and at the foot there is the name of an office, and that office is not in this yard's book and is not named in this book.** It proposes that this yard hold a copy of a record for the coast and be named in an entry as the person who holds it. It says the party is not to be examined, licensed, enrolled, paid, or asked to find anything, and is asked one question. **It says nothing about what follows an answer of no, and the date of the answer is the only date on it, and the date of the answer is in this yard's keeping.** The man said he is not the man who directs it, said he did not know what picking up a sheet off a bench is, and went down the mole and nobody followed him. **The Crown's position reached this harbor in one sentence and one sentence only: testimony is safe in one place and nowhere else, and this harbor is not that one, and that is not an opinion, it is what three hundred years of an office is. Nobody said it was a lie and nobody said the man was anything at all.**
2. **THE HARBOR AUTHORITY AGREED, IN THE SENSE THAT A THING KEPT IN MORROW QUAY IS A THING KEPT IN MORROW QUAY**, said in the open air at the foot of the mole's steps in about eleven people's hearing, and the reason it gave is that no office on this coast can get at a copy of a record kept in this place, and that a man in a city who wants a thing in a fortnight will not send a carriage and will write to this harbor authority first, because that is the name a man writes first when he does not know any other. **He named what his office cannot do — it cannot certify a copy of a record, cannot hold a record for the coast, cannot enter it in a spent ledger whose ninth acknowledgement is spent and whose tenth may not be entered, cannot renew the writ of the first of May and is the only office that can, cannot overrule a seizure and cannot certify a glass witness — and said he was not going to do the rest of it and pretend afterwards that it was part of it. He entered the whole thing on a page of his own and not in the ledger, because a page of his own is not a record and cannot be produced on demand. THE PRICE WAS NAMED BEFORE HE SAID YES AND IT FELL ON HIS OWN OFFICE, WHICH IS NOW A NAME IN THIS BUSINESS, and every party who comes up that hill about anything at all is going to be told at the foot of those steps that this office has an opinion about a copy of a record, for years, including the ones who have nothing to do with this party. HE IS STILL NOT A FRIEND OF THIS PARTY AND SAID IT AGAIN.**
3. **ORDINARY WORK DID NOT STOP.** A day of about four hours and a quarter at the face of the second seam on the twelfth, landward of the third seam's mark, on a hirer's own account, with nobody in the water, a hand lead's line over the side and back four times, the gross on the board twelve and the yard's being three, the book written in the ship's hand, the slate going into the book in her own writing and the holder reading it back after her. **Entered as a day not earned whole and not as a day at a figure, because the yard is a party of one and a half until the first of March and every day it books in this month is a day it books with a man in it. The compressor's gland and the hose after it, and this harbor has no hose.**
4. **THE ELEVEN-LINE LIST WAS TESTED BESIDE THE OFFER AND THE TWO DO NOT AGREE, and that is the batch's discovery.** The ship's hand took the sheet of the twenty-second of November down and read the eleven aloud and put the form beside it with about four inches of bare wood between them. **A place a copy of a record is kept in is a room, and the eleven lines are a list of what does not go into a room, and every one of them is a thing this yard would be right to keep out of a room, and so the eleven lines are the answer to that form — and the answer to that form is eleven lines this yard cannot put in an answer, because an answer carries the name of the party, the place and the date, and the limit of the four of the Sill is a reason, and a reason does not go into a record, and this yard holds a writ and a writ is a channel and a man with a writ is the thing that limit was written against. The limit was read out once, in a shed, and it is that the account is not to be read out, is not to go into a book that leaves this harbor, is not to be said to a man with a seal, and not one name to any office in any city. NOBODY'S NAME WENT NEAR A PIECE OF PAPER ABOUT A FORM.** Item ten has happened and came back no. Item eleven, the two figures for the bar of gravel and the Kettle, has not been moved off that list in three weeks and is not going to be moved in December.
5. **THE YARD SAID SOMETHING THAT WAS NOT A YES IN A STREET AND IT WAS READ AS AN INTENTION TO KEEP, AND IT COULD NOT BE CORRECTED.** At the head of this dock on the sixteenth, in about eleven people's hearing, asked by a man of the third lay who said he was not asking it for anybody, the holder gave the whole shape of the sheet and said in the open that the answer will be in his own hand and is not an office's and is not signed by a clerk and has no day on the sheet to be late, and that he could not say on that day whether it was a yes or a no, and that he would not be in a position to say in three weeks either. **Two men of the first lay were saying on the Thursday that this yard had not said no, and one of them said the word *hold* twice, and the yard did not go up and correct either of them. THE REASON IT COULD NOT CORRECT IT IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND IS THAT A CORRECTION IS THE REASON, AND THE REASON IS THE FOUR OF THE SILL, AND IT DOES NOT GO INTO A STREET. The chapter's two columns are the reason against the line and the fact that a reason does not travel, and the gap between them was not closed and says so on the page. THE SAME TWO MEN WERE SAYING A THING ABOUT THIS YARD AT THE HEAD OF THAT DOCK AGAIN ON SATURDAY THE NINETEENTH, WHICH IS ENTERED IN CHAPTER 208 IN THE PROSE AND IN THE FIRST COLUMN AS THE SECOND OF TWO DAYS, AND THE YARD DID NOT GO UP ON THAT DAY EITHER. THE MARKET OFFICE WAS NOT USED AND COULD NOT HAVE BEEN: it is open on a Tuesday and a Friday morning and this was a Wednesday and a Thursday.**
6. **A COUNTER OFF THE FISH MARKET PRICED TWO THINGS AND THE TWO PRICES ARE NOT THE SAME PRICE.** No page of the copy of the record was read aloud there and nobody in that room heard one line of it. **A page that anybody in nine places could check is nine people who each went and got it, and nine men's time, and a man's time in a working port in December is a day at about three marks — so the price of a checkable page is the whole of a day's work at a seam. A page that nobody can check is a sheet and a shed and no money at all, and is the one that cannot be shown to anybody. And a paragraph is a trade and a trade travels, and the moment a reason goes on a page it is a paragraph, and a reason cannot be kept in a paragraph.** She also said, about sheets in general and not about this yard's, that a sheet with an office's name at the foot of it and no man's name on it anywhere is the easiest thing in the world for a copyist to sell, because there is nobody on it for her to ask where it came from. **The yard bought a sheet of her paper at a penny and it was for its own use and not for a copy of anything, and the reason against the line is that this party cannot put a price in a record out of a person's mouth.**
7. **THE COST OF A DAY WAS ENTERED BEFORE IT WAS ASKED FOR.** A man of fifty-five with a lighter told the ship's hand at the boards on the twentieth that he hired a man on the Saturday evening for the Monday, paid him two marks and his victuals out of his own pocket, and the man did not come. **The man's reason, in his words: if everything a yard says in this town goes into a book in a city then a day's work of mine goes into one too, and I have got a girl at a school in a town four days up this coast and I am not having her name read out in a town I have never been to. The two men of the first lay who were saying it on the Saturday evening were saying it like a thing that had been settled, AND IT WAS THE SECOND OF TWO DAYS ON WHICH THE SAME TWO MEN WERE SAYING A THING ABOUT THIS YARD, THE FIRST BEING THURSDAY THE SEVENTEENTH, AND CHAPTER 208 ENTERS THAT IN ITS PROSE AND IN ITS FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST BOTH LINES, AND THE ENTRY SAYS THAT THE YARD WENT UP ON NEITHER DAY, THAT THE FIRST OF THE TWO IS OUT OF ITS OWN EYES AND THE SECOND IS OUT OF WHAT A MAN OF THE SECOND LAY SAID AT THE BOARDS, AND THAT IT HAS NOT GOT EITHER NAME AND IS NOT GOING UP THE HILL FOR IT. IT IS NOT THE THIRD LAY'S FOUR DAYS AND IT IS NOT A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY'S MONDAY AND IT IS NOT THE TIDE GANG'S THURSDAY MORNING, AND ITS SHAPE IS A MAN WHO WAS PAID AND DID NOT COME, WHICH NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO IS.** The yard did not offer the two marks and entered why on the Sunday, and the reason is that a yard which pays a man's day for a thing it said in a street has bought the street, and the yard does not want it and cannot afford it, and the first of those three is the one that is on the page.
8. **A PRINTER'S LETTER CAME UP THE HILL ON THE TWENTY-THIRD WITH ONE QUESTION IN IT, and it is not a threat and not a favor and the printer says so himself.** A sheet bought at a penny at a counter in this market on the sixth of December went up a coast road in a box of fish with a man who sells ice, a printer kept it because his trade keeps things, and on the ninth a man came to that counter and bought type and nothing else and asked whether the printer could say where a copy of a record was. **His one question is where the copy of the record is, and the yard did not answer it, and the reason is in the first column and not the second, and it is that a reply is a document with this yard's name at the foot of it.**
9. **THE BATCH'S TURN.** **The instrument the yard built to make itself credible is the instrument that is going to make it locatable, and the yard built it on purpose on the seventh of July and nobody made it do it.** The acknowledgment of the twenty-ninth of November — which this yard did not write, did not pay for, did not ask for and did not allow, and which a copyist of fifty-eight took up in a market of her own account and told them to keep away from — **is the one place in this country where a man in a city can look to find out where this yard is, and it did the whole of the work in nine days.** A sheet with an office's name at the foot of it and no man's name on it can be bought at a penny by anybody and resold to anybody and there is nobody on the paper to ask. The copy of the record is in this shed and the yard wants it, and that is the reason a line in a printer's book has a town on it and no address. **Both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other**, and the shape was said once in this batch and by nobody else.
10. **THE RESOLUTION'S REMAINING ITEMS ARE ON THE PAGE, in the outline's order, and each was paid by saying it out loud or by entering it rather than by winning anything:** a boy off the stone and not replaced with a first-column line and a date on it; a chandler's note not re-written and not said a fourth time and not said once in twenty days; a longer leash with a name on it, and the name is an office and not a man; a reeve who put one more thing on a page of his own at his own office's cost and is still not a friend; five bells at about five and a half fathoms that are not raised and are not on anybody's schedule; and the market question, not answered, with the refusal on the page in the yard's own hand with the reason against it, **referred to once, in a first column, with its date, its asker, his age and his tonnage, and with the answer in the words already on the page and not improved on, and the yard entered as not going to answer it in a book either. NO COMPACT IS NAMED. NO OFFICE ANSWERS IT. NO DOCUMENT ANSWERS IT. NOTHING IN THIS BATCH ANSWERS IT IN ANY DIRECTION. THE VOLUME IS NOT CLOSED.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 200 — RETAINED IN FULL AS THE BATCH 0005 RECORD, AND SUPERSEDED ON EVERY POINT THE VOLUME 04 AUDIT RULED ON ABOVE

**VOLUME 04 MOVEMENT 5 IS WRITTEN. ITS CLIMAX IS PAID, AND IT IS PAID AS A COPY OF A RECORD AND NOT AS AN OBJECT, AND THE VOLUME'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE IS NOT REACHED AND IS NOT ATTEMPTED.** In twenty days a yard of two and half people applied in writing for a copy of a record at a cost of a penny, was given a form with an office's name on it and no date on it, was given a copy off a counter at the end of a day and read it in a shed, put a page and a half into a room over a tide-gang store on two days, had its own best man asked in front of a clerk whether he could vouch for the water and heard him say that he cannot, agreed in that room that the object is not coming up this hill and said out loud in the same room that he wanted it, was refused a part payment on forty marks by a letter and paid the price, stood in a market and let a copyist read a form of an office about it at a penny a sheet, refused two questions in a market and gave the reason, said the chandler's note is not re-written for the third time in seven months, and lost the eligibility it wanted before the writ on a half-sheet out of a court, and the name at the head of that half-sheet is an office and not a man.

### The movement's own beats, ten of ten, in the order the volume outline gives them

1. **THE PARTY APPLIED.** One sheet, the holder's own left hand, dated Monday the sixteenth of November, asking the circuit office of this place for a copy of one record of that office, being the record of the entry of one item of recovered transparent mineral in the custody room of that office; and it says on the face of it that it asks for a copy of a record and not for the object. A penny of the ordinary post came out of the bag. **The reason it applies now, when it entered in June and again on the eighteenth of September that it would not, is in the second column with a reason against the line, and the reason is not that the old reason has gone soft: it is that a copy of a record carries on its own face the limits the record itself carries, and a limit printed on the face of a sheet is the one kind of limit that does not arrive in a city as a bare line with nothing behind it. The party has also entered, on the same line, that it is not saying no to it in four years and is not saying yes either, and that the release of such a copy is not in this yard's keeping and has never been in it.**
2. **THE APPLICATION WAS ANSWERED AND THE COPY CAME INTO THE YARD'S HANDS.** A clerk came up the hill on the twenty-third with a form which says a party may apply at its own cost, which grants no copy and makes none and releases nothing, and that **no date attaches**; and that at the foot, where a signature would be, there is the name of an office and no man's name, and the clerk gave the reason, that a clerk's name at the foot of it would let a man in a city say in four years that a clerk of that circuit decided a copy should be made, and that that is not what happened. The holder went down to the counter on the afternoon of the twenty-fourth and came back up with one sheet, and a clerk told him three things about a thing leaving a counter, one of which is that after the first of December nobody in this harbor is going to ask that question again. **The copy has six heads and about a page and a half on the face of it and the yard can check none of it, and the yard said so out loud in the shed, and the two lengths are a page and a half and the rest of this book's life.**
3. **THE CHOICE WAS MADE AND IT WAS THE ONE THAT COSTS.** Three instruments on a bench on the morning of the eighteenth: a page in a shed, worth what two men in one room are worth; a page in a market, read by about four hundred people and taken down by any man with a knife; a page in a room in a city, which goes on a record and cannot be got off. **The market is the only one of the three that arrives with its reasons on it, and it is the one the party did not use, and the reason is that a reason on a market wall is a reason in a market, and four people of this coast wrote a line and signed it. The party chose the room and entered that it chose the instrument that costs it.**
4. **THE COPY WAS READ OUT IN A ROOM, WHOLE, WITH ITS LIMITS ON IT, BY THE SHIP'S HAND AND NOT BY THE HOLDER**, in the hearing room over the tide-gang store on Thursday the twenty-sixth, in about eleven people's hearing, and the clerk read it all back and entered that the answer came from her and not from him, which is the second time that has been entered in that room. **And in the same sitting the man who is the best reader of joins in this harbor was asked, by a clerk who had written the question in his own page first, whether he could say what was in the water off the south end of this mole on any day this year, and he said he could give a figure, an hour, a state of the tide and the name of the man who hauled the line, and that he cannot tell the room what was under that water and never has been able to, and that he said a thing in a market on the eighteenth of July that was wrong in three parts out of four and has not taken it back and is not going to be asked to and is not refusing to be asked to, and that he cannot vouch for the water with his own ears, and that he is not going to get out of it by being right about something. The clerk entered all of it. Nobody in that room said a single thing.**
5. **THE ITEM STAYS IN THE CUSTODY OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE AND THE PARTY DOES NOT APPLY FOR IT, AND THE HOLDER ACCEPTED THAT IN A ROOM AND SAID HE WANTED IT.** He said that if it came up this hill that afternoon it would be worth more to this yard than every mark that has gone through its hands since the first of May and that he would not know what to do with it, and that four people of this coast wrote a line in October about what gets said and what does not, and that this yard is not going to use a piece of glass to be the reason it does not ask. **The shape of sentence was said once, in that room, about the item not being theirs and the yard wanting it and not asking, and improved on by nobody.**
6. **AN OFFICE ACKNOWLEDGED THE DISCREPANCY IN A FORM THAT GOES ON A PAGE, AND A WOMAN WITH COPIES OF IT AT A PENNY A SHEET READ IT OUT IN A MARKET.** Pernel Saye, fifty-eight, took it up in the market on Monday the thirtieth of her own account and unasked, said that a sheet of that office is a public sheet and is the only kind worth the candle, said in thirty-one years of copying she has never copied one of that office's for nothing and is not going to start, said that the fourth paragraph is the part that was put in on purpose, made twenty-one copies at about nine minutes a sheet, and read the whole thing out at the head of the fish dock on Tuesday the first of December in about forty people's hearing in about nine minutes. **She was not paid by this yard and this yard did not ask her, did not send anybody and did not stand near her while she did it. A man of the first lay bought four copies at four pence. Two men of the third lay read the whole of it standing up and gave it back without buying a sheet. THE WORDS ON THE BOARD ARE THE OFFICE'S WORDS AND THE YARD COULD NOT HAVE IMPROVED THEM BY ONE.**
7. **MARA VENN PRICED A THING AND THE ANSWER WAS NO, AND THE NO IS NOT A PUNISHMENT AND NOT A REPAIR.** See the relationship section below.
8. **CALDER MARR IS NOT ELIGIBLE TO BE EXAMINED FOR THE FULL SECOND BELL LICENSE, AND IT IS NOT THE WRIT.** See the section below.
9. **A QUESTION WAS ASKED IN A MARKET ABOUT THE ACT OF AN OFFICE AGREEING TO SOMETHING, AND IT WAS NOT ANSWED, AND THE REFUSAL IS IN THE YARD'S OWN HAND WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE, AND THE REASON IS ABOUT A PERSON OF NO OFFICE AND NOT ABOUT THE OFFICE.** See the section below.
10. **THE CONCRETE RESOLUTION'S REMAINING ITEMS ARE ON THE PAGE, in the outline's order, and each was paid by saying it out loud rather than by winning anything:** a boy off the stone and not replaced with a first-column line and a date on it; a chandler's note not re-written and said out loud at the head of this dock for the third time in seven months; a longer leash with a name on it and the name an office; a reeve with nothing left to put in his book who is not a friend; five bells at about five and a half fathoms that are not raised and are not on anybody's schedule; and the market question, not answered, with the refusal on the page. **THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION IS OPEN AND NOT ANSWERED. THE VOLUME'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE IS NOT REACHED: no page went up on any wall in this harbor in three weeks and none came off, the third column is empty and nobody is appointed to it, the delay was not measured and nothing was written down with a date against it, and nobody went out in a boat in a closing image. THE VOLUME IS NOT CLOSED.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 200

**Calder and Mara. HE ASKED HER FOR SOMETHING AND SHE PRICED IT AND THE ANSWER WAS NO, AND IT IS NOT FUSED WITH ANYTHING.** He wrote to her on the sixteenth of November, one question, in his own left hand, dated, and the question was **whether this party might offer her part payment on the forty marks out of a day of work and take the rest when there is any.** It asked for nothing else. It did not ask her to come to this harbor, to be in a room, for a line, for what any record says, or for anything else, and it said that if the answer is no then it is no and the yard will enter it with the date and will not ask a second time. She answered on the twenty-seventh, one sheet, in her own hand, **price first and answer second, and the price is that he keep the letter, put what she has written in the second column with a reason against the line, and put not one word of it in a market** — and the reason she gives is that in about four years a man in a city is going to read that a yard of Morrow Quay went to a woman it owed forty marks to and asked whether it might pay her part of it and was refused, and that the said reading is going to be true of a man like him and is not going to be true of him, and that there is nothing she can write from where she sits that will make the difference. **The answer is no, and the reason is that a part payment is a receipt, and a receipt is a document, and a document is how a person of no office becomes a thing a person with an office can use, which is the sentence she said to him in a room on the twenty-ninth of September and which he did not argue with then.** She also wrote that the six marks and two days has not moved and is not going to be reduced by anybody including by her, because it is her price and not a debt, and that the two have never been one thing and that this is the first time anybody has tried to make them one. **The letter says not one word about the copy, the room, the sitting or the sheet, and the yard had not told her about any of them and is not going to, and the yard entered that. The not-telling of the seventh of August is now a SIXTH OCCASION NOT TO, entered on the sixteenth of November on a line of its own, with the reason of the fourth of October given again and the undertaking not to invent a second one, and the ship's hand said in the shed that it is not going on the same line as the answer to a question about a part payment, and that a price is not a confession and a refusal is not a repair. The forty marks stands first after food, unpaid, not one shilling of it paid, not one shilling of it offered.**

**Calder and Kest. HE WAS ASKED FOR A ROOM AND A DAY AND NOT FOR AN INSTRUMENT, AND HE NAMED THE PRICE OUT LOUD BEFORE HE SAID YES, AND THE PRICE FELL ON A MAN OF THE TIDE GANG WHOSE NAME HE REFUSED TO GIVE.** The holder asked in the open at the foot of the mole's steps on the nineteenth of November, in about eleven people's hearing, and said first that he was not asking for an instrument, that there are eight acknowledgements in that ledger and the ninth was entered on the twenty-eighth of August at this party's asking and is spent and a tenth may not be entered, and that this party did not ask for the ninth again and did not ask for the tenth, and that a room is not an instrument and a day is not an instrument. He said he was not asking that office to seat anybody, **that the power to seat one of two disputants belongs to the inquiry and not to the writ of the first of May, and that the two instruments are not the same instrument.** Kest said the room is over the tide-gang store and a sitting in it shuts the store, and that one man of the tide gang of this harbor loses his Thursday morning, and that the tide gang is four men short and will be four men short at the first of March, and that he did not name the man because the moment he names him he is a man in this business. Then he said three further things: that his ledger is spent and there is no line he can enter this week that would mean anything to anybody in the first of March; that his office cannot pay for a clerk's day and has had nothing in its repair account since the middle of February and the clerk will enter what goes in that room in his own hours and the office is going to owe him a day, and the debt is entered against the office and not against the party; and **that he is not a friend of this party, has never said he was, and is not going to begin on a Thursday in November, and that if the party needs a man in this harbor to be on its side then it has counted him twice and should take one of them out.** The holder entered all of it and said the party will take none of them out and agrees with him.

**Calder and Bevin. Unchanged and not in a room.** The boy is not in any of these ten chapters as a person. The three nots stand. Forty marks stands whole. The head of the third column keeps his hand. **The third column was not filled on any day of this batch and nobody was appointed to it, and the party's first-column entry of the seventeenth of November and the read-out of the fourth of December both say so.**

**Calder and Alden. Do not move, and the figure is counted from the prose first and written from the count. HE WAS AT THE FAR BENCH ON FOUR DAYS OF THIS BATCH AND ON NO OTHER: Monday the sixteenth and Thursday the nineteenth of November, Wednesday the twenty-fifth of November, and Thursday the third of December.** Not asked for anything on any of the four and asking nothing on any of the four, and Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the four. **The entry of the nineteenth of November says he was not at that bench on the Wednesday at any hour; the entry of the twenty-fifth says he was not at it on the Tuesday at any hour; the entry of the third of December says he was not at it on the Wednesday at any hour. The read-out of the fourth of December lists the same four days and says that neither brother went over to the other on any of the four. EITHER BROTHER CAN CHECK IT ON ANY DAY OF A WEEK.** No fragment, no report talk, no second story, no confession. The tin cup of the eighteenth of October is not repeated and is not improved on.

**Calder and Nessa. The pair this volume changes most and neither of them says so, and this batch is where the second half of it is.** She read a page and a half out of a room in six heads and read out what was not under each head as well as what was in it, and she read the sixth head last and slowest because it is the head that is about nothing at all, and the clerk entered that the answer came from the ship's hand. She argued in a shed for the room and against the market and gave the reason and would not give it twice. She put an eleven-line list on the bench of what is not going into that room and made the holder stop her at the ninth item and add a tenth, which is a letter about a person of no office. She was charged two shillings on the twenty-first for a strapping coming off, and she said the bone knitted straight and that a wrist does not turn all the way round in a cold month for two years and that the only thing that makes it worse is a boat on a cold tide with a fall in the hand, and that she does not want it in her own book. She entered in her own hand that until the first of March this yard is a party of one and a half and not two and that every day it books in this month is a day it books with a man in it. **He has not thanked her and is not going to and is not asking.**
