### The eleven days' new-volume question, and the form that has taken the Second Bell

**A QUESTION WAS ASKED IN A MARKET IN THIS HARBOR ON WEDNESDAY THE SECOND OF DECEMBER, IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING, BY A MAN OF THE FIRST LAY WHO IS FIFTY-ONE AND IS MASTER OF A COASTER OF ABOUT A HUNDRED AND NINETY TONS OF HIS OWN, AND IT WAS NOT ANSWERED, AND THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION IS THE SECOND OF THE TWO THINGS HE ASKED AND IT IS THE ONE THIS VOLUME OPENS.** His second question was what an office in this country that has kept records for three hundred years thought it was guarding against at the point at which it decided what it was allowed to lose. He gave the reasoning out loud: that an office that keeps records that long has had to decide what it was allowed to lose; that that is not an accusation but arithmetic; that somebody, in some room, in some year nobody is alive in, decided what this coast was going to be without; and that a town like this one is the last place on the coast anybody can ask, because there is nothing in it worth a clerk's time and everybody in it knows it. **The holder answered that this yard does not know, and that this yard said the same out loud in that market on the thirteenth of August in about forty people's hearing, and that it is not going to say it a second time about the same thing, and that the sheet of the fifteenth of August carries the answer and the reason on its face in about nine words. He then gave out of the yard's own book a second-column line with no name in it, being a bare fact and nothing else, and said he was not going to call a fact an answer in a market. NO OFFICE IN VEYR IS SHOWN A DOCUMENT THAT WOULD ANSWER IT, NO COMPACT IS NAMED, NO MINISTRY IS NAMED, NO OFFICE OR PERSON ANSWERS IT IN A ROOM, AND THE PHRASE *RISK MANAGEMENT* IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH.**

**AND ON FRIDAY THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER A HALF-SHEET CAME UP THIS HILL IN THE ORDINARY POST WITH THE NAME OF A COURT IN A CITY AT THE HEAD OF IT AND THE NAME OF THAT COURT AT THE FOOT AND NO SIGNATURE ANYWHERE, AND IT SAYS FIVE THINGS AND THEY ARE THE WHOLE OF IT.** That the matter of the ASTER GANNET stands before that court and is not closed by a finding, and that a person entered in that matter as an interested party is not examined for the full Second Bell license while the matter stands. That the holder of the said writ is so entered **by the making of a copy of a record, the entry being on the face of that copy, and the entry is dated the twenty-fourth day of November instant** — which is the day the copy came off the counter of the circuit office, in consequence of an application this party made in its own left hand on the sixteenth at a cost of a penny. That the said person was put to the examination once before and did not satisfy it, and that that court has before it no other matter concerning him and knows nothing whatever of his trade. **That this is not a suspension, not a penalty and not a finding against anybody, and that a person who is not examined is not a person who has been refused.** And that the writ of the first of May instant is not before that court, is not a Second Bell license, does not lead to one and renews nothing, that the court has not considered it and takes no notice of it, and that nothing in that paper touches, grants, refuses or deals with the second season of that writ.

**AND THE HOLDER ENTERED IT IN THE FIRST COLUMN IN HIS OWN LEFT HAND AND BEFORE ANY FIGURE OF ANY KIND: that he was put to the said examination in the month of September two years back and did not satisfy it, and that the writ of the first of May instant was granted eight months afterwards, and that he has not gone near that examination since, and that this yard is not going to say in a street in the month of January that the writ did this. THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE IS THAT A WRIT IS A MUNICIPAL INSTRUMENT OF THIS HARBOR AND A FORM OF A COURT IN A CITY IS NOT, AND THAT THE YARD HAS HAD A THING TAKEN OFF IT THIS MONTH THAT IT WANTED BEFORE IT HAD THE WRIT, AND THAT THE YARD WILL NOT BE THE PARTY THAT PUTS THOSE TWO THINGS TOGETHER BECAUSE A YARD THAT IS LOOKING FOR SOMEBODY ELSE TO BLAME IS A YARD THAT HAS BEGUN TO BELIEVE IN A WRIT. THE WHOLE OF THE RELEASE WAS THE PARTY'S OWN DOING, AND THE PARTY IS NOT GOING TO CALL THE COST SOMEBODY ELSE'S.**

**AND THE PAPER ENDS WITH A DATE: a copy of the said record is to be produced to that court on the fourth day of January, and a party which does not produce it is not fined, because a court does not fine a poor man, and the matter simply goes on. THE LONGER LEASH HAS A NAME ON IT AND THE NAME IS AN OFFICE AND NOT A MAN THIS TIME, AND THIS PARTY HAS NOT ASKED ANY OFFICE FOR ANYTHING IN AID OF IT, HAS NOT SENT TO A CITY, HAS NOT WRITTEN TO A MAN IN A COAT WHOSE NAME IS ON NO PAGE OF THIS BOOK, AND HAS NOT BEEN TO THE COUNTER OF THAT CIRCUIT OFFICE SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH.**

### What is owed and what is not, and the one queued phase

**THE VOLUME'S FINAL CHAPTER IMAGE IS NOT REACHED AND WAS NOT ATTEMPTED, AND THE VOLUME IS THEREFORE NOT CLOSED.** Five of its elements are absent from these ten chapters on purpose: no page went up on a market wall where the two naval notices used to be; no person went out in a boat as a closing image; the boy is not on the stone and the third column has no name in it at all and nobody has been appointed to it; the delay is a hand's width of a second and was not measured, not advanced and not written down with a date against it; and the chandler's note is not re-written and no sheet is on any wall. **The one queued phase is `workspace/volume-04/close/PROMPT.md`, which is the volume close and not a batch, and it exists. Nothing else was created: no later batch prompt, no Volume 05 outline prompt, no `.done` marker and no `.retired` marker. `state/phase-ledger.json` was not read as evidence of anything, not edited, and no marker was written to compensate for it; phase status is the controller's alone.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 190 — SUPERSEDED BY THE CHAPTER 200 SECTION AND BY THE VOLUME 04 AUDIT ABOVE, AND RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0004 RECORD

**VOLUME 04 MOVEMENT 4 IS WRITTEN. ITS REVERSAL IS PAID, AND IT IS PAID IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS AND NOT IN A DOCUMENT'S.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half people was told a day was to be named, was served a paper naming it, read its own book out loud in a room for three hours and fifty minutes, put a join on a notice in front of a clerk, could not say what it meant three times, had a market of July read back to it in its own words by a stranger in a flat voice, came out of the room less believed than it went in, entered that against itself in the first column with the reason against the line, cracked a bone above a wrist on a wharf, paid a bonesetter three shillings and sixpence, refused a wharf day of about three marks, did not pay a wage on Tuesday the third of November for the first time this year that the figure went to four weeks, and closed the month forty-two pence lighter than it opened it, and the whole of the forty-two pence is a bonesetter's bill.

### The midpoint, in one paragraph

**THE CREW'S BOOK OF THIS YARD WAS READ OUT IN A ROOM IN MORROW QUAY ON WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF OCTOBER, WHOLE AND UNSHORTENED, FROM THE FIRST OF MAY TO THE LAST PAGE, IN THE ORDER IT IS IN, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN VOICE, FOR THREE HOURS AND FIFTY MINUTES, AND THE CLERK ASKED TWICE FOR A THING TO BE READ A SECOND TIME AND BOTH TIMES IT WAS READ A SECOND TIME.** The two columns were read out. The third column, fourteen lines at the head of a page in the right hand of a boy of twenty-two dated from the second of May, was not read by the holder; the holder gave it up in a sentence in the room and did not take it back, and the clerk read it in a flat voice and said in the room that this office cannot make that boy come and cannot make anybody ask him, and entered that the three nots of the eighth of June stand and that this office is not going to act on them. **THE SECOND COLUMN'S FIVE CHECKLESS LINES WERE READ OUT AS LINES, AND NOT ONE REASON AGAINST ANY OF THEM WENT IN, AND THE CLERK SAID WHY IN HIS OWN TRADE'S WORDS AND NOT AS A FAVOUR: a record has a column and the column is the width of my page, and if I take four words out of a man's paragraph then in about four years a man in a city thinks the man wrote four words, and he did not.** No copy of any record was made in that room and none was given to any party and none was asked for.

### The active pressures going into Volume 04 Movement 5

1. **A SEAM WAS PUT ON A DOCUMENT IN A ROOM AND IT TOLD THE MAN WHO PUT IT THERE ONE THING.** On Thursday the twenty-ninth of October the holder stated that the notice served on this party on the tenth of September has been in two hands at two times, and gave four grounds — the colour of the ink in the first three paragraphs and the sixth against the fourth, the fold of the sheet at that paragraph, the opening and shutting of the paper at the fold, and the depth at which the fourth paragraph begins — and said in the same breath that it does not say which hand is right, or why, or whose the two hands were. **AND THE CLERK OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE THEN SAID THAT HE HAD HIMSELF HAD THAT PAPER SINCE THE TENTH OF SEPTEMBER AND COULD SEE THE TWO INKS AND HAD NOT NEEDED THE HOLDER OF THE WRIT OF THE FIRST OF MAY TO COME UP A HILL AND POINT AT THEM, AND ENTERED THE FACT IN THAT ORDER, THE CLERK FIRST AND THE HOLDER SECOND, AND GAVE HIS REASON, WHICH IS THAT IF THE FACT IS LEFT OUT OF THE RECORD THEN IN ABOUT FOUR YEARS THE ONLY THING IN THE BUNDLE ANYBODY IS PROUD OF IS A THING A MAN OF THIS HARBOR PUT THERE.** He was asked what it means, having written the question in his own page first, and answered *I do not know* three times and would not say it a fourth time in a different way, and the clerk entered all of it. **A SEAM IDENTIFIES DIFFERENCE AND NOT TRUTH AND IT WAS USED THE THIRD TIME IN THIS VOLUME AND IT MADE HIM LESS CREDIBLE AND NOT MORE, WHICH IS WHAT THE VOLUME OUTLINE SAID IT WOULD DO.**
2. **A SENTENCE OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF JULY IS IN A RECORD IN A CITY AND HE DID NOT DENY IT.** The clerk read the entry of the second column of the eighteenth of July out loud in a flat voice, in the holder's own words, and then read the line of the twenty-third of July out of the first column, that the party did not stop him, that it entered the whole of what was said and has not shortened it, and that it was wrong in three parts out of four and has not taken it back. **AND THE HOLDER SAID IN THE ROOM THAT A PAGE IN A BOOK AND A SENTENCE IN A STREET ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT, AND THE CLERK ENTERED THAT AND ENTERED THAT THEY ARE BOTH GOING TO BE IN THE SAME BUNDLE IN ABOUT FOUR YEARS AND THAT HE IS NOT THE MAN WHO DECIDES THAT THEY GO IN SEPARATE ROOMS. AND THE HOLDER SAID HE SAID FIVE THINGS IN THAT MARKET AND THAT FOUR OF THEM ARE IN HIS BOOK AND THAT THE FIFTH HE CANNOT PRODUCE, AND SAID SO IN THE ROOM INSTEAD OF NOT SAYING IT.**
3. **A MAN OF THIS YARD WAS RIGHT ABOUT A THING AND WRONG ABOUT HIMSELF IN THE SAME ROOM, AND THE YARD ENTERED IT IN THE FIRST COLUMN WITH A REASON AGAINST THE LINE ON THE TENTH OF NOVEMBER.** And on Sunday the first of November, at the head of this dock, **Gwil Lasker, thirty-six, of the first lay, a boat of about a hundred and twenty tons, said out loud that he was not saying this yard was wrong and that a man in a city is going to read two lines on one page and take the first off and leave the second on, and gave his name before he was asked for it.** The figure of two and three-quarters on the flood and two and a quarter on the ebb was not withdrawn and is not going to be, the pilot's two and a half was not withdrawn, and neither can check the other and this volume does not decide which is right. **The error he put to his own account in that street is his own and not the holder's: at twenty-two he took a sounding off that bar off a master's own figure at that master's own asking, was a foot and a half out in a slack water, did not tell him, and the said master had it himself inside a month off a man out of a city, and neither of them has said a word about it since.**
4. **THE SECOND COLUMN IS NOW THE MOST DANGEROUS COLUMN IN THIS HARBOR, AND THE PARTY SAYS SO OUT LOUD, ON THE THIRTIETH OF OCTOBER, IN THE SHED.** A party that spent two volumes saying that the second column is the only place a man is allowed to say *I do not know* and mean it came to a room in which saying it went on a page in a city, and the limit four people of this coast wrote themselves and signed — that the account is not read out, is not put in a book that leaves this harbor, is not said to a man with a seal, and not one name to any office in any city — **is not in that record, because a limit is a reason and reasons do not go into a record, and cannot be put there, because this yard holds a writ and a writ is a channel and a man with a writ is the thing that limit was written against.**
5. **THE THIRD COLUMN WAS READ BY A STRANGER AND IS NOT FILLED AND NOBODY IS APPOINTED.** **NOBODY ASKED IN THE ROOM WHO FILLS IT — the clerk read the fourteen lines in a flat voice, said that his office cannot make the boy come and cannot make anybody ask him, entered that, and asked nothing further about it. The *who fills it* argument is in the shed on Wednesday the fourth of November, and she said no twice, gave the reason in her own words, and would not give it again.** The reason is in the first column of the seventeenth of October in the ship's hand. The head of the column keeps the boy's hand. A request to scrape it out is refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column. **A column nobody fills is a column somebody else fills, and the somebody else is a clerk with a pen, and a clerk with a pen is not a bad thing and is not a villain and is the only way a record gets made at all.**
6. **AN INJURY TO A WORKING CREW MEMBER WITH A REAL BILL, AND A BAD DAY, AND BOTH ARE PAID, AND NEITHER IS PAID BY A DIVE.** On Friday the twenty-third of October a copper union on a wharf's discharge let go under pressure and the pump's handle came round through the quarter-turn that is in it and struck **Nessa Pike's** left forearm across the bone about two inches above the wrist at about half past two in the afternoon, and she said before anybody had said anything that it was the bone and not the joint. **Her figure is three shillings and sixpence, charged and paid on the twenty-fourth, and a quarter of a year out of the left side of a shipwright, and both of those are on one line in the first column in her own hand and in his, with the reason that a bone is not a bill and a bill is not a bone and a man who has the two in one line will end up arguing about the wrong one.** A day of work at the second seam on the sixth of November went slower than a day with three on it, and a wharf day of about three marks offered on Sunday the eighth for Tuesday the tenth was refused, and the cost of that refusal is a day not earned and is entered because a day refused is a day not earned.
7. **THE VOLUME'S UNPAID WAGE IS NOW FOUR WEEKS AND THE FIGURE IS IN PENCE.** Tuesday the twenty-seventh of October was paid, the third of November was not paid and no envelope was made, and the tenth of November was paid, and the bag held eight shillings and sixpence against that one, which is one hundred and two pence, so the wage it could not pay was **five hundred and thirty-eight pence** short. **The column runs twenty-three lines and ninety-two marks, twenty-four and ninety-six, twenty-four and ninety-six, twenty-five and a hundred, with the fifth of March the oldest throughout. Eighteen envelopes on a bench, then eighteen, then nineteen.**
8. **THE QUESTION ON THE TABLE IS A DOCUMENT THE PARTY HAS NEVER SEEN, AND IT IS MOVEMENT 5's, AND IT IS NOT OBTAINED HERE.** A copy of a record about an object, with the limits the record itself carries printed on the face of the copy, which would show that a manifest was altered and would not show who altered it, and which the copy itself would say so on its own face, and which a man of the first lay of this harbor cannot check. **The party entered on the tenth of November that it is not applying for one this month, and why, and that it is not saying no to it in four years and is not saying yes either, and that the release of that copy is not in this yard's keeping and has never been in it.** No copy was made, released, printed, quoted, summarized or described in any of these ten chapters.
9. **HE STILL HAS NOT TOLD HER, AND THE NOT-TELLING IS FIVE ENTRIES NOW AND IS NOT PAID.** The decision on the third of October, the not-telling and the reason on the fourth, her line of the seventeenth of October that she was not going to ask him, a fourth occasion in a room on the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and a fifth entry on the tenth of November with the reason again and the undertaking not to invent a second one. **It is not a confession, not a relief, not a price, not a trade, and it is not going to be one in this volume, and the reason has not been improved on in five entries and is not improved on in this one.**
10. **MARA VENN IS NOT IN A ROOM, IS NOT ASKED, IS NOT PAID, IS NOT FORGIVEN, AND DID NOT COME BACK.** On Thursday the fifth of November a man of the first lay, about fifty-five, stood at the wall outside the market office and read the reason on the page of her unsigned finding out loud and asked this yard for her name, and this yard said no in about four minutes and gave the whole of it. **HE SAID OUT LOUD THAT IN JULY THE SAME ANSWER HAD SOUNDED LIKE A YARD BEING CAREFUL AND THAT ON THE FIFTH OF NOVEMBER IT SOUNDS LIKE A WALL, AND THAT HE WOULD RATHER HAVE THE PAGE IN A CITY THAN THE WALL, AND THAT HE WOULD RATHER HAVE IT FROM THIS YARD THAN FROM ANYBODY ELSE, AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO PRETEND HE WOULD RATHER HAVE A YARD THAN A WALL BECAUSE HE HAS BEEN IN FOUR ROOMS IN THIS HARBOR THIS MONTH. AND THE HOLDER AGREED WITH HIM IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING AND ENTERED AGAINST THIS PARTY THAT HE HAS NOT GOT A REASON FOR THAT PREFERENCE WHICH IS WORTH ANYTHING.** Forty marks first after food, unpaid since the fifteenth of October, not one mark of it paid, and a day of work at a seam that brought five marks is not a payment of it and is not going to be entered as one.
11. **THE HARBOR IS POORER ON THE TENTH OF NOVEMBER THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTIETH OF OCTOBER, AND THE WHOLE OF THE DIFFERENCE IS THREE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE.** A mark and eight shillings and sixpence in the bag, which is two hundred and sixty-two pence, against three hundred and four pence on the evening of the twentieth. One herring berth of two out. The north berth out. The light not on. The tide gang four men short. The fire party's hose dead until the spring. ## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 180 — SUPERSEDED BY THE CHAPTER 190 SECTION ABOVE, AND RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0003 RECORD

**VOLUME 04 MOVEMENT 3 IS WRITTEN AND ITS TURN HAS LANDED AND IS SPENT.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half people published a refusal in a letterbox for four pence, sent a man of the first lay down a hill once with the truth, and entered that the second time he says he came is his own account and not the yard's, did not pay a wage for the third Tuesday running, found out that a woman of no office had been cited in a file four hundred yards from its own shed, heard the two words an office uses about its own records out of a copyist's counterfoil at a penny a sheet, was told by that same woman in a doorway on the twelfth of October that the line it had asked her for on the twenty-ninth of September is in her hand in a city anyway and is worth nothing to anybody without a seal, went into a hearing room on the sixteenth and had the truth about a person put into a record in a city in its own eleven words, and closed the month four pence lighter than it opened it with nothing on a market wall and a day of work booked for a Friday it has not reached.**

**THE TURN IS PAID IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS AND IN ITS OWN FORMS, TWICE, AND IT IS SPENT. On Friday the ninth of October a conservator of thirty was handed, at a copying counter in a room off the fish market, a withdrawal counterfoil about four inches by three, in the hand of the circuit office of this harbor, on which the Registry records that it agreed to take leaf 62 out of its own file of the ASTER GANNET on the application of a commissioned officer of the Crown Navy by letter, and that the reason it entered against it is *risk management*, and that the leaf is not to be produced and a copy is held. On Thursday the fifteenth a paper served on this party in a doorway states in a document that the same file is before the inquiry, that one leaf is called for and is not produced, and that the reason of the non-production is on a form of the Registry's own dated the second of September which is not to be produced to this party. THE YARD CAN NOW PROVE ON PAPER THAT A PAGE IS GONE AND CANNOT CHECK WHAT WAS ON IT, AND THE PROOF IS A FORM THAT THE OFFICE SAYS EXISTS AND WILL NOT PRODUCE. ALL THREE RESERVED THINGS ARE SPENT AND MOVEMENTS 4 AND 5 MAY NOT SPEND THEM AGAIN.**

### The active pressures going into Volume 04 Movement 4

1. **THE READING OF THE YARD'S OWN CREW'S BOOK IN A ROOM HAS NEVER HAPPENED AND IS COMING.** A copy of the whole of it has been in a file in a city since the ninth of September and cannot be recalled. It has been produced whole three times — twice in September and once on the sixteenth of October — and not one line of it has been read out of it in any room, and no copy of any record has been made in any room, and on the sixteenth a clerk read a schedule into the record instead. **The party entered in the first column on the twentieth of October that it knows this is coming, is not going to soften a line and is not going to leave one out, and that the week of it is not in this party's keeping and is not going to be.** **IT IS CHAPTERS 181 AND LATER AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT.**
2. **THE SECOND COLUMN HAS FIVE LINES THAT NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR CAN CHECK, AND THE HOLDER CANNOT BRING UP ONE OF THEM.** A line of the fourteenth of August is in his own left hand and he can remember the first four words of it — *a man in a boat* — and not the rest of it, and he entered that on the fourth of October against himself with a reason, the reason itself being what happened to him on the Saturday before. **He entered the same day that he did not know whether the not-reading of that column in a room was a rule or an answer, on the sixteenth of October he did not read it out again, and he entered that he still does not know, and on the twentieth he entered that he is not going to improve on that entry either.**
3. **A PARTY WITH FOUR THINGS AND NOT ONE OF THEM ABLE TO BE PUT IN FRONT OF ANYBODY.** A number off a copying job sheet. A counterfoil in a box under a counter and a fair copy in a woman's own book, both four hundred yards from this shed and neither of them the page. A file on a second floor it has not asked for and is not going to. And a woman it cannot pay. **The shipwright said that out loud in a doorway on the twelfth and it is on the page and it is not going to be improved on in a market.**
4. **ELEVEN WORDS IN A RECORD IN A CITY SAYING THERE IS A WOMAN IN THIS HARBOR THE YARD OF MORROW QUAY WILL NOT NAME**, entered by the holder in his own left hand, read back to him by the clerk of the sitting, and entered again. It cannot be got off a page. **The entry of the eighteenth of September that this party does not put a name on a thing it cannot check is the authority for it and is not improved on, and about four hundred people can read it in a fortnight.**
5. **LEAF 88 EXISTS AND NOBODY HAS SEEN IT AND TWO PEOPLE IN THIS TOWN CAN PROVE IT EXISTS.** A copy of a conservator's own page is to be read with it, and she never wrote it, and an office wrote it, and the copy of her page was made so that it could be. **The yard is not going to be told what is on it and is not going to ask and is not going to guess, and the not-knowing is the whole of what the batch paid for it.**
6. **HE STILL HAS NOT TOLD HER, AND THE NOT-TELLING IS FOUR ENTRIES ACROSS FOUR CHAPTERS AND IS NOT PAID.** A decision to tell her was entered on Saturday the third of October, the day he read his own book from eight in the morning until the light went and could not bring up one line of his own second column, and on Sunday the fourth he entered that he had not told her and the reason, and the reason is that on the third he found out he could not remember one line of his own second column, and a man who has found that out is not a man who is going to be able to tell a woman on a mole's steps that he kept something back from her for six weeks and be believed about it. **On the seventeenth of October she said in the shed that she is not going to ask him and had him enter on one line that she did not ask, with a reason against the line that is about him and not about her.** It is not a confession, not a relief, not a price and not a trade, and it is not going to be one in this volume.
7. **SHE LEFT THE REGISTRY AND SHE DID NOT JOIN THIS CREW AND NEITHER IS A SACRIFICE TO THE OTHER.** A letter of four lines in the ordinary post on the eleventh of October, at a penny out of her own pocket, saying that no form and no sheet and no notation and no hand and no date of hers is to be used to support an account she did not write and has not read, and that she is not resigning anything because there is nothing to resign from. **She is not coming to the market office of this town on a Tuesday or a Friday morning, and on the thirteenth a man came into that room and asked it a question about a form with her hand on it and about nine people in that room could not answer him, and the yard heard about it on the Wednesday and did not tell him where she is.**
8. **THE THIRD COLUMN HAS NOT BEEN FILLED SINCE THE FIRST OF AUGUST AND THE SHIPWRIGHT HAS NINE SENTENCES IN HER HEAD AND HAS SAID OUT LOUD WHY SHE IS NOT WRITING THEM** — that the column is a page where a man wrote down what he said when he was not in the boat, and that if those nine sentences went in it this yard would be holding a page about what a woman said to it in a doorway, and that in about four years there is going to be a page in a city that says what a yard of Morrow Quay knew in October and anybody can read it. **Nobody is appointed to that column, the head of it keeps a boy's hand, forty marks stand whole, and a request to scrape it out is refused in the same words it is refused for a line in any column.**
9. **A REFUSAL, IN A LETTERBOX, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN HAND, FOR FOUR PENCE, and a man of fifty-one who read it in his own wheelhouse and did not know what to do with it for four days, and a man of fifty-one who wrote to a city and would not put his word under a line about water and would not take a shilling for it, and a man of fifty who was sent down this hill once with the truth and nothing else, and who says he came up twice and asked in a doorway on the Saturday as well, which is his account and not the yard's.** Four words in a file in a city say that a yard of Morrow Quay declines to certify a figure and will not be held to it, and the yard cannot get at them, and the refused license from June is carried as a cost and is not re-decided, and about four hundred feet of a woman's warp is on the bottom of this harbor.

12. **A HARBOR THAT IS POORER ON THE TWENTIETH OF OCTOBER THAN IT WAS ON THE FIRST**, and a bag a mark and twelve shillings against a mark and twelve shillings and fourpence, and the whole of the difference being one letter's postage. One herring berth out. The north berth out. The light not on. The tide gang four men short. A hard at Ashtide unanswered. A fire party's hose dead. Nineteen winters in a list in a city. **THE CISTERN BEHIND THE ENGINE HOUSE HAS BEEN CHARGED NINETEEN TIMES SINCE THE THIRD OF AUGUST AND THIS PARTY HAS WALKED NONE OF THE NINETEEN, and the run reads fourteen on the first of October, fifteen on the fifth, sixteen on the eighth, seventeen on the twelfth, eighteen on the fifteenth and nineteen on the nineteenth, and the fifteenth is the one charge of the month this party knows of at second hand, from a man of the third lay at the head of the dock on the seventeenth.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 170 — SUPERSEDED BY THE CHAPTER 190 SECTION ABOVE, AND RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0002 RECORD

**VOLUME 04 MOVEMENT 2 IS WRITTEN AND ITS TURN HAS LANDED.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half people could not pay a wage, worked two days at a seam at three marks and five, told a man of the second lay in a doorway that a day of work could not be done because this harbor has no hose, went into a hearing room at ten in the morning and produced its whole crew's book a second time and read not one line of it aloud, was directed onward to a sitting in the week following the twelfth of October, had a man of the third lay come up a hill in the rain to say where a boy was and is not and was not asked one question, had its refusal of a certification turn into a statement in a city in four days that it had never made, and went into a market office on a Friday morning and was told, in about nine minutes and in eleven people's hearing, that the price of a line with a conservator's name at the foot of it is not money and is an undertaking this yard cannot give, and the answer is still no.**

**THE TURN IS PAID IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS: a refusal to certify is read as a claim, and the only way to be read correctly is to be certified by somebody the yard cannot pay, and it prices the thing in the only currency it has, and says no.**

**And the cost of the fortnight is arithmetic and it closes checkable: a mark and twelve shillings and fourpence in a bag on the eleventh of September and a mark and twelve shillings and fourpence in it on the thirtieth, and in between the two of those figures two days of work at a seam, two wages of four marks paid, two wages of four marks not paid, and the two that were not paid are the week of Tuesday the fifteenth of August and the week of Tuesday the fifth of September, and neither of them has moved and neither is going to be paid this month.**

### The active pressures going into Volume 04 Movement 3

1. **A REFUSAL IS IN A FILE IN A CITY WITH FOUR WORDS IN IT THAT THIS YARD NEVER SAID.** *The yard of Morrow Quay, whose sheet is set in type in this city, gives the bar of that harbor at two and three-quarter fathoms on the flood; declines to certify the figure; and will not be held to it.* **The yard cannot get at the file, will not write to the city, and has entered that a party which has published itself is not a party that gets to be sorry in a street and mean it.** This is the movement's turn and it is on the page.
2. **THE ONLY WAY TO BE READ CORRECTLY IS A NAME, AND THE ONLY PERSON ON THIS COAST WHO CAN PUT A TRADE AT THE FOOT OF A LINE IS NOT ON THIS CREW.** Wil Tranter said it out loud in a doorway on the twenty-seventh: a man with a page cannot act on a refusal, he can act on a name, and there are three people on this coast who can put a trade under a line and this yard has none of them.
3. **A PRICE THAT IS NOT SIX MARKS AND TWO DAYS.** An undertaking, in the yard's own first column, in the holder's own left hand, with a date on it, that this party does not ask her for anything again — not at a figure, not at nothing, not for a line, not for a name, not in a room and not in a shed. **The reason she gave is on the page in her own words: a conservator this party cannot pay is a conservator this party has to keep asking, and asking her to be useful is asking her to be cheap.** The yard could not give it and did not offer it and has entered that it cannot.
4. **HE WENT IN.** On the eighth of September he stood on the steps of the market office for eighty minutes and did not go in. On the twenty-ninth he went in and asked for something, and was refused, and did not thank her and did not say he was sorry, and put the whole of it in the book including the fact that he came in with something to ask for. **He has still not told her that he wrote down the sentence of the seventh of August in the second column on the eighth, six weeks after she told him not to, and the not-telling stands.**
5. **A DIRECTIONS SITTING ON SATURDAY THE SIXTEENTH OF SEPTEMBER, AND A SITTING TO BE APPOINTED FOR THE WEEK FOLLOWING THE TWELFTH OF OCTOBER.** The inquiry is not over. **A copy of the yard's whole crew's book is in a file in a city and has not been read out in any room, and the reading of it in a room is the volume's midpoint and is in Chapters 181 and later. The second column of that book has four or five lines in it that nobody in this harbor can check, and a shipwright said out loud on the crown on Wednesday the thirteenth that if those lines are read out in a room then in about four years they are the only thing in forty-seven weeks that this yard knew and would not say.**
6. **A DAY OF WORK WAS REFUSED IN A DOORWAY BECAUSE THIS HARBOR HAS NO HOSE.** Five marks of compressor's gland on a creditor's page since the nineteenth of May, unpaid, sound, and of no use whatever because the thing after the gland is the hose; the longest thing of hose in this harbor about nine fathoms and it belongs to a man of the second lay. **A man of the second lay booked a day at his own figure for the Friday following and was told at eight in the morning on the Friday that the work could not be done, and the booking was refused and no money changed hands either way, and the yard entered the whole of it with the hour against it.** A poor crew does not get an inquiry's costs waived.
7. **THE WAGE COLUMN HAS MOVED TWICE AND STANDS AT TWENTY LINES AND EIGHTY MARKS**, the fifth of March the oldest, and **FIFTEEN ENVELOPES ARE ON A BENCH AND TWO WEEKS FALLEN DUE THIS YEAR HAVE NO ENVELOPE STANDING AGAINST THEM, being the fifteenth of August and the fifth of September, and the two figures are different figures and neither of them is the other.** The next wage is four marks on Tuesday the third of October, which is three days off at the close of this batch.
8. **THE SECOND COLUMN OF THE YARD'S OWN BOOK HAS ONE NAMED LINE IN IT AGAIN, AND IT IS THE ONLY NAMING VOLUME 04 HAS, AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE AGAIN.** Chapter 164, Sunday the seventeenth of September, on land, in a doorway, with a man of the third lay: the holder cannot always tell which of two things he said in the last minute was the one he had decided to say, and it is a tide-sickness, and it has been got since the fourteenth of October of last year. **THE FOUR LINES ABOVE THE NAMED LINE OF THE TWENTIETH OF JULY ARE STILL FOUR, ARE STILL NAMELESS, AND ARE NOT STRUCK OUT, and the count of four stands in the first column in a ship's hand with no name against it.**
9. **AN ORDINARY MAN CAME UP A HILL IN THE RAIN AND SAID WHERE A BOY WAS AND IS NOT, AND WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION.** A fore berth in June, from about the sixth to about the twenty-first, paid out of the man's own pocket and not out of a wage, and he is not in it and has not been since the twenty-first of June. **The three nots of the eighth of June stand. Nobody wrote to the boy, nobody went to see him, nobody asked anybody who has seen him what he said, and the yard entered that it wanted to say thank you and did not say it, and why.**
10. **THE THIRD COLUMN HAS NOT BEEN FILLED SINCE THE FIRST OF AUGUST** and there is a line in the first column about it, and nobody has been appointed, and a column nobody fills is a column somebody else fills, and **the shipwright has now said out loud, in the first column, that she did not fill it, and why, and that a column kept by a shipwright in a shed on a Sunday is a column about a shipwright.**
11. **THE NINTH SEAM'S MOORING IS IN SERVICE AND IT IS HARBOR GROUND AND IT IS NOT THIS YARD'S.** A man of the first lay asked on the twentieth whether it would take a boat of about ninety tons, and the yard said it would not answer for the mooring, gave him what its own book holds, took nothing, said it was not going to be thanked and had not been, and told him to go and ask the tide gang, **and the tide gang would carry her on a slack water for a day and a half, and a day and a half of the gang was the whole of the price and the tide gang is four men short of what it was.**
12. **THE COAST ROAD'S OWN FIGURE IS SET IN TYPE IN A CITY WITH THE PILOT'S FIGURE BESIDE IT AND NEITHER OF THEM CAN CHECK THE OTHER.** A man of about two hundred tons bought a printed sheet off a stall for a penny on the morning of the twenty-second and read it twice on the boat coming up. **The yard refused to tell him which figure is right, entered that it is not going to decide it in a shed, and did not argue either half of the sentence that is on the sheet. The Kettle was not looked at. The refused license stands. Five miles of that coast has not been looked at and is not going to be this season, and that is on the face of the sheet in the yard's own words.**
13. **THE PRIVATE OFFER OF MONEY IS A SEASON OLD AND IS CARRIED, NOT RE-DECIDED.** Thirty marks in coin, refused in nine sentences in June, on the back of a paper folded into the back of the writ of the first of May, brought out on the twenty-third of September for the only reason that puts a man's hand on it, which is a bag with twelve shillings and fourpence in it. **About four hundred feet of Sella Brigg's own warp came up off the bottom of this harbor on the twenty-eighth of July for twenty-six marks and a day, she was paid by the man of Ashtide, and this yard owes her eight shillings and tenpence, undiminished, unpaid, entered with her name on it at her own asking and not on any wall.** The refusal is a cost and is not a decision.
14. **A REPUBLIC HEAD OF A WALL AND A PRINTED SHEET, AND A PARTY THAT WROTE ON A WALL ON THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF AUGUST THAT A ROAD NOBODY ELSE CAN USE IS NOT A ROAD AND A ROAD EVERYBODY CAN USE IS NOT THIS YARD'S** — and a man with a brush saying *you put it on a wall and told sixty boats where the copies were*, and the yard saying *a printed sheet is the same instrument as a wall with one more step between it and the man who is not going to be able to be brought up in front of it*, entered in the second column and not the first.
15. **A HARBOR THAT IS POORER ON THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER THAN IT WAS ON THE ELEVENTH**, and poorer than it was on the fifteenth of August, by two unpaid wages and a day of work refused for want of a hose and a man of the first lay out of a Monday in August and a refusal that cannot be corrected by anybody but its author. **The cistern is on a rota of a Monday and a Thursday and was charged on eight days in September at no figure and this party walked it on none of the eight.** One herring berth out. The light not on. The tide gang four short. A hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November. Nineteen winters in a list in a city.

In twenty-six days a yard of two and a half people found its own sheet of the fifteenth of August gone off a market wall in one morning in a boat with two naval notices, got the date and the room out of a four-line form that does not mention the writ's second season, sold two days of ordinary harbor work, paid a wage on a Tuesday for the first time in three weeks and did not pay a shilling of a debt to a man of another crew, took a man of fifty-four's figure and put it on a wall beside its own, published a refusal it had received rather than a fact it had established, spent a reeve's last entry on a day of work inside a notice and charged it to a man of the first lay, watched two strangers put a mooring back into service because they had read a date off a wall, stood on the steps of a market office for eighty minutes and did not go in, put a whole crew's book on a table in a hearing room and read nothing out of it, and was served on Sunday the tenth with a notice that hands the harbor authority the power to seat one of two disputants — which is the reporting clause's own second limb, applied to this party, by a form this party did not write and cannot un-write.**

**A DATE AND A ROOM ARE ENTERED IN ADVANCE AND THE DAY IS A DAY IN THE WEEK AFTER THE ELEVENTH OF SEPTEMBER. The yard will be at the sitting, will not be represented, and will answer what is asked and not what it would have chosen, and it has entered that this is a decision and not a virtue and is not going to be thanked for it and is not asking. The third column was not filled on the Sunday night, which is the second day since the second of May that it has not been filled, and nobody has been appointed, and a line in the second column says that the holder does not know whether he is going to read the second column out in a room, with a reason against it and no name in it.**

**A COPY OF THE YARD'S WHOLE CREW'S BOOK IS IN A FILE IN A CITY, and that is the first time in four volumes that a copy of this yard's own record has left this harbor, and not one line of it was read aloud in the room it was produced in, and a man in a coat said out loud at the table that he is not going to open the copy in that room and is going to read it in a city, and the yard cannot stop him and has entered that it does not know what he will be done with it.**

**And the third column of a woman of thirty is empty, and a sentence she told him on the seventh of August not to write down is in the second column tonight with a reason against it and no name in it, and he has not told her he wrote it.**

### The active pressures going into Volume 04 Movement 2

1. **THE INQUIRY HAS A DATE, A ROOM AND A CONSTRUCTION, AND THE CONSTRUCTION IS THE PARTY'S OWN.** Where a finding is disputed the harbor authority may seat one of two disputants and take such finding as is given, without prejudice to any claim. The party built that in April, agreed to it in good faith, printed the clause on a market wall in July in forty copies in about sixty boats, and is now the thing on the table instead of the person reading the table. **This is the volume's central pressure and it is paid.**
2. **THE BOOK IS IN A CITY.** A copy of it, whole, in a file, in another man's hand, and it contains the day a man lost the count of his own basket and the day a case went down, and both were entered by the yard against itself at the time, and the yard cannot un-enter them and did not have to enter them to be hurt by them.

8. **A REPUBLIC HEAD OF A WALL THAT TELLS A MAN WHERE THE COPIES ARE.** The pilot said so out loud on the mole's steps and the yard heard him, did not agree, said so out loud in a market on the sheet's own face, and is not taking it down. **A road nobody else can use is not a road and a road everybody can use is not this yard's, and both halves are on a wall and neither is going away.**

13. **A HARBOR THAT IS POORER ON THE TENTH OF SEPTEMBER THAN IT WAS ON THE FIFTEENTH OF AUGUST** and is not going to be made better: one herring berth out, a day of a man of the first lay lost, a light not on, a cistern on a rota, a tide gang four short, a hard at Ashtide unanswered, nineteen winters in a list in a city, forty marks to a boy, forty marks to a woman, eight shillings and tenpence to each of two women, eight marks and a day of a boat to a bellwright, a chandler's note at thirty-one and not re-written, and a bag with a mark and twelve shillings and fourpence in it.

**VOLUME 03 MOVEMENT 5 IS WRITTEN AND IT WAS THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX AND ITS RESOLUTION.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half people read a Crown notice nailed over its own return on a market wall, watched a working vessel of a community of this coast go on the ground inside the four hundred yards with four people in her, **wrote down the sentence it had published on the fifth of July and repeated on the twenty-sixth and entered the breaking of it and the whole of the cost in its own first column on the seventh of August, in advance, at nine at night — and went past the outer marks on the eighth on its own account with no instrument of any office, with two pots of air bought at the harbor authority's own compressor at this yard's own two-mark rate and a day of another crew's boat at six marks of his own naming, part paid. HE SAVED THE VESSEL'S LIVING CREW AND LOST THE BELL-ARCHIVE, and the two are the same choice and neither of them cancels the other.**

**THE COST WAS PAID AND IT WAS PAID BY SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT THE YARD: A WAGE OF FOUR MARKS WAS NOT PAID ON TUESDAY THE FIFTEENTH OF AUGUST AND THE ENVELOPE WAS NOT MADE, and the money that would have paid it is the money that was spent on a boat, and the yard is four marks short and has entered that in the first column with the hour against it; and three marks is owing to a man of Ashtide for the eighth, with a date on it; and a community's only local copy of its own account of itself is at the bottom of the sea about a mile and a half off this harbor in about five and a half fathoms, and the four people it belongs to are alive and have no boat, and the page that went up on the market wall on the fifteenth says where the bells are and does not pretend anybody is coming for them.**

**Captain Veyra Holt is relieved of the *Vigil* and of the command of this coast from the fifteenth of August and posted from the first of September to the making up of the coast's wreck lists, in a city, at a table. She does not come to this harbor, has not been in it, and appears in no room. The posting came on a paper read in the hearing room over the tide-gang store on Saturday the twelfth of August by a man in a coat of an office in a city whose name the clerk wrote down and this yard has not repeated; **the channel is the writ, was ruled on the fifth of July, was recited on the twenty-sixth and was applied on the twelfth, and the yard entered that the man was let up the stairs BECAUSE of that standing arrangement.** The second season of the writ is not granted, not refused and not dealt with by that paper; the writ runs to the first of March; its ground is not widened; its four names are four. The yard checked the posting against its own entry of the fifth of July and entered that the check holds: it is not a command in this harbor, not an inspection of the harbor authority, not a commission, and puts nobody past the outer marks or the imperial line.**

**Four people of the Sill testified on a mole's steps in about forty people's hearing on the tenth of August, in their own words, with a limit they wrote themselves and signed: a bell-archive is not a thing that is read out, it is a thing that is struck, in a hall, in front of the people it is about, and there is nobody in this town it is about. SOMEBODY BEARS IT: the four bear it, and the holder bears it, and the yard has entered in its own hand and with a date that he wanted it lifted, could not lift it, did not ask twice, and is not going to. A question was asked in a market on Sunday the thirteenth of August in about forty people's hearing — WHO CHANGED THE RULE — and it was not answered, and the not-answering is in the first column in the yard's own hand with the reason against it, and the reason is this yard's decision of the fifth of July not to put a name on a thing it cannot check. A herring skipper of fifty-one with nineteen winters in a naval file said, in the same market, that both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other, and would not say it twice, and made the holder read it back twice, and it is in the book.**

**And on Tuesday the fifteenth of August at about eleven in the morning, in a market, in daylight, a page went up on the market wall of Morrow Quay under a naval paper, on the same nails, on the outside of whatever was there — the *Vigil's* notice of the fourth of August being over the *Sallow Reach's* printed sheet, which was over the sheet of the seventh of June, which was over the yard's tenth thing, and the yard's own fourth return of the twenty-second of July having been under four papers since the twenty-eighth of July and still readable from the side of it in the right wind. IT CARRIES THE PLACE OF EVERY COPY OF IT, THE NINE PLACES AS THIS YARD IS ABLE TO STATE THEM WITH A DATE AGAINST EACH AND THE WORD *HARBORS* NOT ON IT ANYWHERE, AND THE TWO COLUMNS WITH A REASON AGAINST EVERY LINE OF THE SECOND.**

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: NOTHING in a bag, thirty-one on the chandler's note, nothing in a tin, and three marks owing to a man of Ashtide, on Tuesday the fifteenth of August — against nothing in the same bag on Wednesday the twenty-sixth of July.** The chain is **0, 3, 3, 7, 3, 7, 7, 11, 0, 0** across the days money moves. Four days of work at about three or four marks each, the whole of it borrowed from a week that was not doing them. On the eighth of August: the wage, four marks; two pots of the office's air, four marks; the master of the *Sallow Reach*, six marks named out loud, three paid at the mole and three not — **which empties the bag exactly.** Three wage weeks fall in the batch, the first, eighth and fifteenth of August. **The first and the eighth went into envelopes; the fifteenth was NOT PAID.** The column goes **fifteen lines and sixty marks – sixteen lines and sixty-four marks** and stops, the fifth of March the oldest and staying there, and eleven envelopes on a bench and not one of them has been anywhere in twelve weeks. The note is not re-written, its three counts of weeks do not move, five marks of compressor's gland stand on it unpaid and useless, and the tin is empty. **The whole of the money that has come into this yard since the twenty-second of July is fourteen marks and the whole of what went out is eighteen. No office in this harbor has paid this yard a mark since the eighth of May and none is going to.**

### The active pressures going into the Volume 03 close

1. **THE VOLUME IS WRITTEN AND THE CLOSE IS SHORT.** Fifty chapters, five movements, the climax paid, the resolution paid, the new-volume question opened and not answered, the final image on the page. **The close is an audit and a hand-over and must not open a Volume 04 thread by accident.**
2. **LOCK L5 IS STILL FLAGGED AND THE AUDIT MUST RULE ON IT.** It enumerates three returns and says there are three and only three. There are four on the page, the fourth made on Friday the fourteenth of July on the day, out of a finding of Monday the tenth, and Batch 0005 added no fifth.
3. **THE BELL-ARCHIVE IS LOST AND THE OWNERS ARE ALIVE AND POORER.** Five bells at about five and a half fathoms inside the four hundred yards. No instrument in this harbor reaches that water, no money in this harbor reaches that water, and no trade on this coast whose work it is. A later volume may supply a way, at a price, and the price will have to fall on somebody.
4. **THE YARD BROKE ITS OWN PUBLISHED SENTENCE AND ENTERED IT IN ADVANCE, AND THE SENTENCE CANNOT BE SAID AGAIN.** A yard whose saying is worth nothing in any figure it puts on any wall in any year after this one. This is a standing condition and not an event.
5. **A WAGE OF FOUR MARKS IS UNPAID AND THE WAGE COLUMN HAS STOPPED AT SIXTEEN LINES AND SIXTY-FOUR MARKS.** Not the yard's forty marks, which are not going to be paid either way. This one is new, it is a working man's four marks for six days, and anybody can come up the hill and ask.
6. **THREE MARKS ARE OWING TO PERRY OLLETT OF THE *SALLOW REACH*** for the eighth of August, a debt to a man of another crew, in the first column, with a date on it, not in any column of the book.
7. **THE PUBLIC THING IS DONE AND IS NOW ON A WALL UNDER A NAVAL PAPER.** The nine places, the place of every copy, the two columns, the limit, the five bells, the broken sentence. About sixty boats. One copy in a city going to press. **A Crown claim was enforced against a working boat over a market wall, which the volume's reveal discipline allows and which is now on the page.**
8. **THE QUESTION IS ASKED AND NOT ANSWERED,** and the not-answering is on the page in the yard's own hand with the reason against it, and the reason is a rule the yard set itself on the fifth of July.
9. **A BOY WHO CANNOT DO THE THING HE WAS KEPT FOR**, in the yard's own hand with a date on it, on the first of August, and the three nots standing, and the head of the third column keeping his hand, and the final chapter's pencil in Nessa Pike's hand. **He was not paid, resolved, repaired or reduced in this batch and the forty marks stand whole.**
10. **A CONSERVATOR OF NO OFFICE IS NOT ON THE CREW AND IS STILL IN THIS HARBOR,** and is in the market office on Tuesday and Friday mornings because that office is open to anybody, and was asked for nothing by this party, did one thing at nothing **once** and said so in front of nine people, gave six things about the bells and could not give a seventh, and is owed forty marks first after food unpaid since the fifteenth of October. **Her break with the Registry is Volume 4 and is a different event and no chapter of Volume 03 fuses them.**
11. **A REEVE WITH NOTHING LEFT TO PUT IN HIS BOOK,** who said on a mole's steps on the sixth of August that there is nothing in his book that will put a boat of his past the outer marks and nothing in the holder's either, and that this is not a failure of either book, it is the design. Not a friend, not a hero, his ledger spent.
12. **A HARBOR THAT IS WORSE OFF ON THE FIFTEENTH OF AUGUST THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF JULY** and is not going to be made better by anything: one herring berth short, a mooring out of service with an end of it seventeen days off, a third lay that has lost four days and then four more of its moorings in the ordinary way, the tide gang four men short, the fire party's hose dead, the mole-head light not on, no boat of this office's own since the twenty-eighth of April, the hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November, and nineteen winters in a file, in a letter and in a list, and a chart sold for them.
13. **A MAN OF FIFTY-FOUR OUT OF A STORM BELT IS STILL COMING IN THE AUTUMN FOR NOTHING,** with his own figure for a bar of two and a half where this yard's figure is two and three-quarters, and no instrument in this harbor that can call him and none that can stop him, and the yard did not go and look and has entered that it did not.
14. **THE PLANNED ENDING IS UNTOUCHED.** No new antagonist, no new institution, no new final enemy. The ninth-line mark, the Quietening, the Crown Seal, the Office of Returning Memory, the nine final routes, the compartment, the custody items, the lead plug's number, the run under this town, the coast road, the first echo's witness and the plate at the fifth seam are all exactly where Volume 02 left them.

**Calder and Mara are two people who have disagreed in public about whether to publish a dangerous witness, and the disagreement is not repaired and is not settled by him giving her the evidence.** In this batch she was not asked for anything by him at all. **A woman of the second lay asked her a question in the market office on Friday the fourth and she answered at nothing once, said so in front of nine people, said the yard did not ask and would not have got a different figure, and said the not-saying costs her and not the boat.** He learned in Volume 03 that a conservator I cannot pay is a conservator I have to keep asking, and asking her to be useful is asking her to be cheap; **in this batch he kept to the first half and the standing arrangement held, and on the seventh of August she told him not to write down one sentence and he did not write it down, and she told him that if she is ever the one holding the pencil in that yard he can check whether she kept it.** **She is the person holding the pencil in Chapter 150.**

**Calder and Bevin are unchanged and the batch did not put him in a room.** He is in no chapter of it as a person. The three nots are recited in four chapters and none is broken. Forty marks standing whole. **Calder and Kest are at the end and the end is now on the page.** The reeve has spent three times and has nothing left to put in his book, and has said out loud on a mole's steps that there is no instrument in it that will put a boat past the outer marks. **He is not a friend and the volume does not pretend he was right about everything; the holder did not thank him for the second entry, entered that he was not going to use it, and said that in four years a man reading that wall will read it as a reeve's price. The plate was not mentioned, not asked about, and not reached.**

**Calder and Nessa are the pair this batch changed most and neither of them says so.** She won the argument about being quiet in a market. She read back the sentence that broke a published one, in a shed, at ten past nine, and read it back after him. **She did not say the reader thing a fourth time and the reason is on the page. She did not pull the cutoff in nineteen minutes and has entered both what she did and what she would have done at twenty-five. She told him not to write a sentence down and he did not write it down. **Calder and Alden do not move.** The far bench on the twenty-seventh of July, the thirty-first and the first, and the seventh of August; not asked for anything on any of the four days, asking nothing, **and Calder Marr does not go over to him on any of them, and the yard has entered that he did not and that neither brother has said why and neither brother is going to.**

**NO STAGE OF ANY KIND IS TAKEN IN MOVEMENT 5 AND NONE MAY BE.** The Faultreader stage was taken in Movement 4, is spent, and is not taken again. **He read one seam in this batch — mendings under mendings in the *Hearthwake's* garboard, in six feet of water in the dark, on the first call down of the eighth of August — and it identified difference and nothing else, and THIS TIME HE DID NOT SUPPLY THE REST, and the reason is in the second column and the reason is that a man who has been wrong in public in a market once about the word *chain* does not get to be the man who supplies the rest of a sentence about a boat with people in her.** He lost about a second and a half over a shout he could not place, and that second and a half is the price of the volume's climax and it is in the yard's own book in the second column with a reason and **without the word.**

**THE ONE NAMING OF THE CONDITION WAS SPENT IN CHAPTER 137, ON THE TWENTIETH OF JULY, IN THE YARD'S OWN BOOK, IN THE HOLDER'S OWN LEFT HAND, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, WITH A REASON AGAINST THE LINE, AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE AGAIN IN THIS VOLUME OR IN ANY OTHER.** The bare fact is on the page twice in this batch, in the second column, with a reason, and without a name. **The four lines above it are still nameless, are not struck out, and a request to strike a line out of a column is refused. **And he is not repaired and the volume does not let him off.** He goes in the water four times in this batch, inside limits he set himself at the boat and that nobody raised, with the six read aloud in order and the cutoff hers and the word *Enough*, and he comes back with a hand that cannot tell a shout from a deck and with a decision he made by letting go.

- **Two things of nobody's are still living in the open air on the mole's crown above the third seam's mark, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one of them with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and NEITHER OBJECT HAS MOVED IN NINETY DAYS, and the marking on one of them is not identified and is not going to be.** Six joints four fathoms under that same stone, nine fastenings in about seven feet of each, three thicknesses of fouling, a chip of worked glass put into a packing on purpose, and a line of six places three hundred and fifty-one feet long which this party has declined to call a chain.

- **The crew's book has three columns.** The third was filled on the first of August at about four hours' lateness and on the fifteenth at about an hour's, the shortest since the fourth of April, **and was not filled at all on the eighth**, and the entry says why and says that the party does not know who will fill it next and has not appointed anybody.

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 140 — SUPERSEDED BY THE CHAPTER 150 SECTION ABOVE, AND RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0004 RECORD

**VOLUME 03 MOVEMENT 4 IS WRITTEN AND IT WAS THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half men put a hand lead's line into a crevice four fathoms down on the second seam's own face and snagged it on a piece of metal about the length of a hand, and worked it up by hand in a westerly, and came back four days later to the same place with a ring and brought up a lump the size of two fists and a chip of green glass the length of a thumbnail out of the tallow of the lead, **and then made a fourth return on the day, because the clause says every finding of worked glass in four days and the day of the finding is not counted and the fourth day after the tenth of July is the fourteenth.** A conservator of no office who had been in this harbor about a fortnight and whom nobody knew priced herself out loud before she touched anything, proved six things about that joint with a lens and a pair of calipers of her own — two ends cut to each other, packing and fastenings of one age, both over three inches of fouling on the seaward side and none on the landward, the packing pressed in from seaward, nine fastenings in about seven feet with three chisel blows a head and the same three blows on all nine, and a chip of the same worked glass put into the packing on purpose — **and could not give a seventh, and the seventh was who, and her reason is that a body does not leave anything on a thing that a trade can read.** A man in the water put his hand flat on the cut and **read a seam for the first time in his life**: the two cuts in that joint are of different ages, and it came into his hand with no picture and no sound, and it told him there were mendings under mendings and it told him nothing whatever about when or in what order or by whose hand — **and he supplied all three, and said out loud in a market on Tuesday the eighteenth at about half past three, in about eleven people's hearing, that the six joints are a chain, that they were made once in one time by one set of hands from the north end down, and that whatever they are for it is not to keep two boats off the bottom in a blow.** Fouling took it apart in two days: the two thinnest readings are the two at the root end, which is the north end, and he had told eleven people the newest was the first; and a quarter of an inch and three inches and a quarter is not a morning but at least three different days in three different seasons; and there is a joint with nine inches on it, which is the oldest thing in the crevice and is the fifth of the six and the second from the seaward end, and he does not know what that means and said he was not going to say. **It cost a day bought for seventeen and half of it done, a hired diver of another boat who went down because he was told to and is not doing it because of Tuesday, a woman of the second lay who paid twelve marks at the mole for half a day and came up the hill to say the tide was there at seven and at two, and the woman of this yard who is the reason there is a reader and had to read the wrong down and then read a word about her partner's ear down after it.** And on the twentieth of July, in the shed, at a quarter past nine, with a man of the *Grey Widow* awake on a net loft floor and nobody pretending otherwise, **he said the word for it out loud for the first time in seven months and wrote it into the second column of the yard's own book in his own left hand with a name in it, and there is a name in that line and there is no name in any of the four above it, and he broke his own line of the second of June, and the reason against the line is that a man who can lose a quarter of a second out of an ordinary conversation in a shed is a man whose account of a seam under four fathoms is a thing that can be asked about, and the party has decided it can be asked about in this book, on this page, on this date, by anybody who comes up this hill, and the only difference between that and a man with a seal is that it can be argued with.** On the twenty-first the party went into the market office for the first time in five months and read four books out of a press under a stone slab that is unlocked to anybody on a Tuesday and a Friday morning, **and found a builder's day-book of the port of Ashtide with six places in it that are the six joints and a builder's name cut into a stone at the mole head, and a weir-book with a fisher's own storm in it and the third joint a foot and four inches under that weir's own sill stone, and a poor-book with twenty-two children put out of a village and nine of them named and the village not on this coast, and a tide-gang's column of figures that stops — and laid a string on the shed floor and the six joints came to three hundred and fifty-one feet with nothing in the string's way, and there are nine places and six of them stand over a hole in a stone wall and three of them do not, and the party has entered the three and has entered that it does not know why and is not going to guess.** And it declined the word. Nine places is nine places. A line is a line. And the word *chain*, said on the Tuesday by a man who was wrong in three parts of the same sentence, is disowned in the yard's own book. **And on Saturday the twenty-second, in daylight, in a market, the yard nailed its own fourth return up on the market wall over the rival's printed sheet, with no scale on it and no price on it and nowhere on it to write a letter to, and a shilling changed hands at the foot of the dock for the rival's and not for the yard's, and a conservator of no office said out loud in the open air in forty people's hearing that he was a man who had run out of money and a man who had not, and that she was not taking either half back, and her objection went onto the sheet unsigned with the reason, and his answer went on beside it in fifteen words: both, and I will not be able to tell you which was right in October.** And on Sunday the twenty-third at the top of the mole's steps she said, in her own words, before anybody asked her, that a yard that cannot pay her asks her whether she can be useful, that she has been useful four times since the twenty-seventh of January without being asked once or paid once, that six marks and two days is her price and does not come down, and that a trade that says yes to nothing is not a trade — **and then he told her all of it, the day-book and the weir and the poor-book and the nine places and three hundred and fifty-one feet, and she called it the best thing anybody has found out in this harbor in five months and then said it was worth nothing to her, because she is not being paid for it, and a thing a person is given because she is owed money is not a gift and not a trade and not a finding.** And the yard said its own half out loud, in Calder Marr's own words, on a mole's steps: **a conservator I cannot pay is a conservator I have to keep asking, and asking her to be useful is asking her to be cheap, and I have been doing the second thing since the twenty-seventh of January and calling it the first.** And on the twenty-sixth a reeve entered in his own book, at his own cost, that the mole's footing from the third to the twelfth seam is to be examined on the second of August and the third lay closed for the four days of it, **with the repair account of that office empty since the middle of February and the money not coming and the entry made nevertheless, and a man of the third lay said four days out loud in a market and did not ask for anything, and the party asked the reeve on the steps whether any of it was about the plate at the fifth seam and was told, in thirteen words, that it is not and he will not say what it is about.** And at about half past six a man of the third lay said a boat's name out loud in the street — *Hearthwake*, working, with people in her, off the outer marks since before the ninth of July, one of the nine, the tide gang walking past her daily and told nothing — **and the yard wrote it down where anybody can check it, which is a page in a book in a shed on a hill, and did not go, and sent nobody, and asked that man no question about her, and said out loud the fourth thing it entered on its own account on the fifth of July, word for word: the outer marks stand where the writ says they are and the party is not going past them this season and has not tried and is not going to, and that is not nothing and it is not enough and both of those are on the page.**

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: NOTHING in a bag, thirty-one on the chandler's note, and nothing in a tin, on Wednesday the twenty-sixth of July — against FOUR marks in the same bag on Thursday the sixth.** The chain is **4, 2, 6, 2, 7, 1, 4, 0** across the seven days money moves. A pot of air at the yard's own two-mark rate goes out on the seventh and another on the eighteenth. A day at the second seam on a hirer's own account brings four in on the tenth. A day on **Edric Pringle's own account** brings five in on the seventeenth — gross seventeen, the eighth two, the share two, victuals two, two hired hands at three apiece, twelve out of seventeen — **and that is two marks less than the same day of work brought on the twenty-fourth of June, and the two figures are written side by side on the mole's steps in front of everybody without saying which one the yard hoped for.** A day on a hirer's own account, nobody in the water, brings three in on the twenty-first. **Three wage weeks fall in the batch — the eleventh, eighteenth and twenty-fifth of July — and each is four marks out of the bag into an envelope with the week written on it in Calder Marr's own left hand, because there is nobody else in that shed who writes, and the envelopes are in the bench chest and not among the five rolled in oilcloth, and there are nine of them now and not one of them has been anywhere, and the reason is on the page and it is the same reason it has been since the second of May: a wage is not a reason to go to a door.** The column goes **twelve lines and forty-eight marks – thirteen and fifty-two – fourteen and fifty-six**, with the fifth of March the oldest and staying there. The note is not re-written, its three counts of weeks do not move, five marks of compressor's gland stand on it unpaid and useless, and the tin is empty. **The whole of the money that has come into this yard since the twenty-fourth of June is twenty-two marks, and the eight marks that were in the bag on the fifteenth of June went out in June as three weeks of a wage and a pot of air, and this month four weeks of a wage and two pots of air went out, and there is nothing in the bag, and no office in this harbor has paid this yard a mark since the eighth of May and none is going to.** A shilling changed hands at the foot of the dock on the twenty-second for the rival's printed sheet and it is not this yard's income and is not in the bag and will not be.

### The active pressures going into Volume 03 Movement 5 — SUPERSEDED, RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0004 RECORD

1. **THE CLIMAX IS OWED AND IT IS NOW DATED IN THREE PLACES. The *Vigil* moves on the crew while Calder Marr is trying to raise the *Hearthwake*; he saves the vessel's living crew and loses the chance to carry her full bell-archive to the surface; the two are the same choice and neither cancels the other. A boat's name is in a market in this harbor, in a shed book, and the outer marks and the bar of four hundred yards off them and the writ's first of March and a Crown attachment on a market wall are three things a writer can lean on. THIS BATCH DID NOT BEGIN IT, DID NOT PUT THE *VIGIL* IN THE WATER, AND PUT NO PERSON, A BOAT OR A LEAD OF THIS YARD PAST THE OUTER MARKS.**
2. **THE PUBLIC FACT CANNOT BE MADE PRIVATE AGAIN.** The yard's own fourth return is on a market wall with no price on it; a printer in a city was told three lines in advance in the ordinary post and cannot be stopped; a rival says out loud that he will be standing in front of it on Monday with a better sheet. **The only advantage this yard ever had, which was a thing nobody else knew, is gone, and it is gone because the party published it on purpose and because a man of fifty told it that a wall with nobody able to be asked a question about it is a wall worth nothing.**
3. **A FINDING THAT CANNOT BE READ.** There is a chip of worked glass in a packing four fathoms under a mole, put there on purpose by somebody who expected somebody to come, and the party has declared on the page that nobody in this harbor can read it and that the trade which can costs six marks and two days and none of them has six marks. **It is the volume's unsent witness and no chapter of Volume 03 has read it.**

5. **A man who read one seam and got it wrong in a market.** The Faultreader stage is taken and it is spent in the only way the volume's argument allows: **it identified difference and not truth, he supplied the truth from his own head, and the fouling proved him wrong in three parts out of four in front of eleven people and a hired diver of another boat and a woman who paid for the day.** Whether he reads another one, and whether a second one is better, is not owed by this batch.

7. **A conservator who is not on the crew and is not in the Registry's eyes.** She said no in her own words before anybody asked. She took her calipers. 8. **A reeve who has spent twice and a third lay that has lost four days of the best of its season to an examination with no money behind it.** Neither man got what he wanted and the plate is still in eleven feet seen and not measured and not touched, and the plate has been referred to twice in the whole volume, the second time in thirteen words.
9. **A girl of twenty-two's June, forty marks of claim standing whole, a third column this yard intends to keep and cannot yet fill and has now priced at four marks a week, and nine envelopes on a bench and not one of them anywhere.** None of it is paid, reduced, repaired or resolved, and this batch may not and did not.
10. **A cistern that has held since the nineteenth of June and a third lay that is closed four days, and a mole-head light that is not on, and a hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November, and nineteen winters in a naval file, and a harbor that is worse off on the twenty-sixth of July than it was on the sixth and is not going to be made better by anything.**
11. **A man of fifty-four with a different figure for the bar, coming in the autumn for nothing, with no instrument in this harbor that can call him and none that can stop him.** And a question out of a city, three quarters answered, one not, and a sheet going to press in a city in July that will be wrong about one thing this yard cannot do one single thing about.

**Calder and Bevin are unchanged and the batch did not touch him.** He is in no chapter of it. The three nots are recited in four chapters. Forty marks standing whole. A wage going into an envelope. Nine envelopes on a bench.

**Calder and Nessa are at the point where she is right six times in twenty days and the sixth one was a word about his ear that she had to read back.** She wrote the count of four in the first column with no name on it. **Calder and Alden do not move.** The far bench on three days across two chapters, not asked for anything, asking nothing, neither brother going over to him, one first-column line that either brother can check by asking the other.

**What it gained, in one sentence and no more: the perception that two cuts in one joint can be of different ages, and that the difference between a cut made once and a cut made on top of a cut that was there first comes into a hand without a picture and without a sound.** It is not a rank, it was conferred by nobody, it is not named as a stage on the page, and it puts no crew behind a man.
