**VOLUME 03 MOVEMENT 3 IS WRITTEN.** In twenty-one days a yard of two and a half men made a third return on the day, went out on a mole in a north-easterly and could not say in which of two directions a man's voice had come from, and wrote it down in the second column with a reason against it, for the third time in five months, with nobody asking; got its own boat back into the water off a stone crown; worked two days at the second seam and could not afford a third; said out loud on a mole's steps that it could neither produce the harbor authority's chart nor refuse it for anybody, because the chart is not the yard's; read the eleven names of its own public record out loud on a mole in nine people's hearing and would not ask the four it has never reached; watched a reeve sell a chart and pay nineteen winters of a herring skipper's dues for it in a room with a clerk in it, and said nothing, and wrote down that it had said nothing; let a man from Ashtide nail a printed sheet over its own on the market wall, and put the whole of the reason out loud on a mole's steps in nine people: that a slip with eleven names on it had been on that wall since the third of May for a shilling and was the only reason a stranger could print a sheet anybody could write to; heard a woman say in a market that she was going to take her own rope to a man with a compressor; heard a coast office say, for the first time since the first of March, that it does not moor a fleet, and that it has taken three lines out of this harbor's own account of what it cannot moor and put them in a list; answered three quarters of a stranger's question out of its own book and refused, in writing and in public, to make itself able to answer the fourth; asked a man of fifty one question in a room in a boat, exactly as he said he would be asked, and did not write down one stroke of what he said; and declined to put a sheet on a wall it could have put a sheet on.

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: FOUR marks in a bag, thirty-one on the chandler's note, and nothing in a tin, on Thursday the sixth of July — against eight marks in the same bag on Thursday the fifteenth of June.** The chain is **8, 6, 2, 9, 5, 8, 4.** A pot of air at the yard's own two-mark rate goes out on the nineteenth. A day at the second seam on the *Anna Beth's* own account brings seven in on the twenty-fourth, and the yard's seven is three more than the four this yard costed the same day of work to on the mole's steps on the thirty-first of May, because the pot of air went out of the bag on the Friday and the ring, the shackle, the swivel and the four feet of warp all came on the ring and nothing else came off the day. A day at the second seam on a hirer's own account brings three in on the first of July. **Three wage weeks fall in the batch — the twentieth and twenty-seventh of June and the fourth of July — and each is four marks out of the bag into an envelope with the week written on it in Calder Marr's own left hand, because there is nobody else in that shed who writes, and the envelopes are in the bench chest and not among the five rolled in oilcloth, and there are six of them now and not one of them has been anywhere.** The column goes **eight lines and thirty-two marks – nine and thirty-six – ten and forty – eleven and forty-four, with the fifth of March the oldest and staying there.** The note is not re-written, its three counts of weeks do not move, and five marks of compressor's gland stand on it unpaid and useless. **The whole of the money that came into this yard in twenty-one days is ten marks, of which twelve went out as three weeks of a wage and two went out for a pot of air, and no office in this harbor has paid this yard a mark since the eighth of May and none is going to.** A shipwright additionally bought a rival crew's printed sheet for four marks **out of her own hand**, and that four is not the yard's money and is not in any column and is not going to be repaid.

### The power state — SUPERSEDED, RETAINED AS THE BATCH 0003 RECORD

**Unchanged in rank.** Line Diver, with an unstable tide-ear capacity used twice and not used since the eighth of December, and the lift at the end of a childhood call gone and not restorable. **No dive of his own in this batch, no entry of anything, and no Bellwright, Keelwright, Storm-Reader, Chorus Diver or Openhand stage is taken and none may be. THE CONDITION IS NOT NAMED IN THIS BATCH.** **It is on the page as the bare fact twice, in the second column, with a reason against each line, no cause against either, no name in either, and nobody asked — and with a count of four entered against the fourth.** **On Monday the third of July, for the first time in five months, he said it out loud to a person, and a shipwright wrote it in her own hand, and he did not tell her what to write, and she put no name against the line and said why: the day a man of this yard writes that he could not tell which of two sounds it was with his name on it, in about two years there is a page in that book that says what a man of this yard can and cannot hear, and that page will be read by somebody in Veyr who is looking for exactly that.** **THE ONE NAMING VOLUME 03 IS ALLOWED IS THEREFORE NOT SPENT AND IS OWED TO MOVEMENT 4, WHERE THE VOLUME GETS A SEAM WRONG IN FRONT OF PEOPLE WHO TRUSTED HIM. NO CHAPTER OF MOVEMENT 4 MAY TREAT IT AS SPENT AND NO CHAPTER MAY LET IT VANISH SILENTLY: IT IS ON THE PAGE FOUR TIMES, IT HAS A COUNT, AND THE FOURTH OF THOSE IS IN ANOTHER PERSON'S HAND.** What the batch paid is method: a repeat of four casts against a repeat of four casts five weeks earlier that agreed and was entered as a fact and not a proof, six conditions read out in order at a boat with a named tender who is not a diver and a cutoff that is hers, a stated reason entered in the yard's own book with the clerk's absence entered rather than filled in, a third column filled five times with the lateness entered each time and a day-and-a-half lateness entered as the longest and not made into a practice, **and one decision not to write down a figure a yard cannot check, which is the first time in this volume that the yard has had a number in its hand and refused it.**

### The bodies and the dated positions at the end of Chapter 130

- **No air in this harbor except a pot bought on the nineteenth of June, no delivery hose, and a compressor's gland fitted to the yard's own pump since the nineteenth of May, unpaid, on a creditor's page at five marks, and of no use whatever because the thing after the gland is the hose.** The hand lead's line made in the net loft on the second of May is right, was said to be right in about nine words on the twenty-fourth of May, and has been used four times since the second of June — on the second of June, the tenth, the twenty-fourth and the first of July — of which three are in this batch. **Nothing was cast with it on the third of July.**
- **The ninth seam's mooring is out of service and, for the first time since the first of May, HAS AN END ENTERED AGAINST IT: THE FIRST OF SEPTEMBER, entered in the harbor authority's own book on Monday the third of July, by the reeve's own hand, and entered because that office's instruments are not being contested.** It is the first thing that office has entered in five months that a person in this harbor can use. **The notice of the thirty-first of October is not lifted, not narrowed and not altered, and no acknowledgement was entered for a mooring, and no person, boat or lead of this yard went inside the first clause on any day of this batch.** The north berth is out. The third lay is full. **The tide gang is four men short and Petch's stand-off ended on the tenth of May and the mole steps are not going to be cleared in June. The harbor authority's cistern was charged on Monday the nineteenth, Monday the twenty-sixth, Thursday the twenty-ninth, Monday the third and Thursday the sixth — eight times in three weeks, at no figure, by people this office cannot pay, and NOT on Thursday the twenty-second, and the reason is on the page — and it has not gone dry since the nineteenth of June, and the harbor authority has had no boat of its own since the evening of the twenty-eighth of April.** The mole-head light is not on and will not be. The repair account is empty since the middle of February and is not going to be filled. The *Kittiwake* is on the hard with no cradle. The hard at Ashtide is unanswered. Nineteen winters are in a naval file and in four lines of a letter.
- **A wage at four marks a week: the twentieth and twenty-seventh of June and the fourth of July PAID, in the holder's own left hand, into six envelopes on a bench. The column is eleven lines and forty-four marks with the fifth of March the oldest. The forty marks of the claim stand whole.**
- **The bell is on the harbor's own ground in eight and a half feet off the south end**, fouled, a frame cut through the casting on one side, **no tongue on the frame at all and two parts of a chain in a lead plug where the tongue was**, a new rope bought on the eleventh of January, a delay of a hand's width of a second that has not moved, **a going out on the second of May that is done and is spent and was not repeated, and eight marks and a day of a boat owing to that man since the twenty-third of May and unpaid and unargued and not paid in this batch, and the standing sentence said in a street on the third of May standing unreversed.** **ITS GROUND GEAR AND MOORING CARRY, IN A REEVE'S OWN HAND OF THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF DECEMBER, A NOTATION THAT ANY PERSON PROPOSING TO WORK, RECOVER, LIFT OR MOVE THAT BELL IS TO BE GIVEN THE ACCOUNT OF THE HERRING FLEET'S DUES FIRST, AND THAT NOTATION WENT OUT OF THIS HARBOR ON THURSDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF JUNE ON THE CHART, AND THERE IS NO SECOND COPY OF IT BECAUSE THE NOTATION IS ON THE CHART AND THE CHART IS THE PAPER. THE BELL READS NOTHING, SETTLES NOTHING AND SAYS NO WORD, AND IT IS NOT IN A BOAT IN THIS BATCH.**
- **The lead plug. Thumb and a half, a piece of chain, a clean half-inch drilled hole, eleven inches under a bell at eight and a half feet, taken out on the twenty-seventh of February, carried four months, put on a bench on the first of May on purpose, described four times by four men that do not agree, in a chest in a shed with a lock the yard owns, with a boy's writing on the lid saying there is nothing in it that anybody in this harbor can check. IT WAS ASKED IN A ROOM ON SUNDAY THE SECOND OF JULY AND ANSWERED ONCE, AND NO STROKE OF IT IS IN ANY BOOK IN THIS HARBOR, AND THE YARD HAS UNDERTAKEN IN ITS OWN BOOK NOT TO ASK AGAIN, AND THAT UNDERTAKING BINDS THE YARD AND NOT THE OFFICE AND NOT THE MARKET AND NOT THE BOY. THE CHEST WAS NOT OPENED.**
- **The delayed note: eleven logged occasions since the twenty-sixth of October, unchanged. Two occasions logged with no call in them, unchanged. NO OCCASION IS ENTERED IN THIS BATCH**, and on Monday the third of July the mole head's handbell went off the crown at about eleven and a person of this party could not say in which of two directions its answer came, and it was not taken and it was not written down as a figure.
- **Two things of nobody's are living in the open air on the mole's crown above the third seam's mark, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, weighted since the twelfth of June with a fender and forty feet of the harbor authority's own mooring rope lent at nothing and entered at nothing, and the tarpaulins were put back on on the seventeenth of June and neither object has moved since the tenth.** One is a lump of green glass about a hand's length with eleven scallops in about four inches, wetter than it was on the sixth of May, worth nothing to anybody the party has been able to find out about, and the subject of the second return made on the tenth. The other is a shard of about a foot and a half with nine scallops in about three inches and a mark on one face that no person in that boat identified and that this party is not going to identify. **Neither is in any office's book, neither carries a seal, neither has a number anywhere, and neither is connected to the other or to anything else, and the number of scallops is not being counted.**
- **The crew's book has three columns**, the third created on the second of May, filled on the eighteenth and the twenty-sixth of June and the fourth of July with the lateness entered each time, with nobody in the yard who will read a position back, **and a line written at the head of the third column on the second of July with nothing under it.**
- **The coast road, the worked panel in a master's keeping, the conservator's unsigned finding, the run under this town, the compartment, the custody items and the first echo's witness** are all carried forward and all unresolvable inside this movement. **And the coast road's figures are now printed in a market in this harbor and are going to press in a city in July, and the man of fifty-four with a different figure is still coming in the autumn.**
- **The concealment is hidden and the batch closes with it hidden.** Nobody asked the boy and nobody asked the conservator, and the yard's refusal to make itself able to answer a question about a lead line and a slate is on the page and is a refusal about a lead line and a slate.

Chapter 152 is one complete morning in a doorway and one complete evening in a shed.**

**THE READ-OUT IS THE DEVICE AND IT IS USED ONCE IN THIS BATCH**, on Friday the twenty-fifth of August at about eleven in the morning, in about forty people's hearing, at a market wall: the holder reads a **sheet** of his own out twice, gets one of the six builder's figures wrong the second time, corrects himself off the sheet in his hand without going back to the top, and the correction takes about a second and a half and nobody in that market says anything about it, and the yard enters it against itself in the second column with a reason and **without a name of any kind in it.** **The two-column head-of-dock read-out is NOT used anywhere in this batch**, and that is deliberate and is the batch's own rule: the sheet is the instrument, and the yard has spent five months learning the difference between a book a party keeps and a record an office keeps. **AND THE READ-BACK IN THE SHED IS NOT THE READ-OUT, WHICH A REVIEWER PASS HAD TO CORRECT IN THIS FILE AND IN THE OTHER THREE: the ship's hand reading an entry back and the holder reading it back after her, nobody else in the shed, at nine at night, is this yard's standing practice since the second of May and it runs in eight of the ten chapters — 151, 152, 153, 155, 156, 158, 159 and 160 — and Chapter 157 opens with a read-out of the yard's own book in a shed. None of that spends the device.**

**The hearing room is used ONCE, on Saturday the ninth of September. The market wall is published on TWICE, on Wednesday the sixteenth and Friday the twenty-fifth. The two are never the same day, and this is verified twice in the batch.** No day is in a chapter twice and no cost is paid twice.

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page, and a reviewer pass found that it did not: NOTHING in a bag on the morning of Wednesday the sixteenth of August, and A MARK AND TWELVE SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE in it on the evening of Sunday the tenth of September. A mark is a hundred and sixty pence and a shilling is twelve, so a shilling out of one mark leaves a hundred and forty-eight pence and not nineteen of them.** The chain is **nothing · 1 · 1 · 12s 4d · 5m 12s 4d · 1m 12s 4d** across the days money moves: a day at the second seam on a hirer's own account on Monday the twenty-first, gross seventeen and the yard's five, and the wage of four out of it on Tuesday the twenty-second, which leaves one; **seven pence of postage on the letter of Sunday the twentieth, out of the shipwright's own pocket and not out of the bag, because the bag held nothing, and owed by this yard to her and unpaid**; a shilling at the press on Friday the twenty-fifth for forty copies, which leaves twelve shillings and fourpence; a day on the mole's toe inside the first clause on Monday the twenty-eighth, gross seventeen and the yard's five, which makes five marks and twelve shillings and fourpence; **the wage of four out of that on Tuesday the twenty-ninth, which is a line in the yard's own book and not a scene and is read out as a figure on the Friday morning in Chapter 157;** and nothing after that. **The wage column is seventeen lines and sixty-eight marks after the twenty-second of August and eighteen lines and seventy-two marks after the twenty-ninth, with the fifth of March the oldest and staying there. No wage was paid twice, no wage was paid on a day that is not a Tuesday, and the three marks owing to a man of Ashtide have not moved a single mark since the eighth of August.**

**The batch's pressures alternate:** a market wall with nothing on it and a man in a boat at seven in the morning; a form in a doorway and a letter to a city; a day of ordinary work and a Tuesday wage and a debt entered unpaid on purpose; a stranger with a figure of his own and a wall that tells a man where the copies are; a press, a sheet, a public read-out and an error made in public by the man who published it; a reeve's last entry in the open air and a day of a man of the first lay; a mooring two strangers fixed by reading a date off a wall; a man on the steps of a market office for eighty minutes; a whole book on a table and not one line read out of it; and a notice served on a mole's steps that hands an office the party's own clause.

## Volume 03, Batch 0004 summary (Chapters 131–140) — Movement 4, what the glass is joined to. THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT.

**Movement 4 is written and its turn has landed.** In twenty days a yard of two and a half men put a hand lead's line into a crevice four fathoms down on the second seam's own face and snagged it, worked it up by hand in a westerly, and came back four days later with a ring and brought up a lump the size of two fists and a chip of worked glass the length of a thumbnail out of the tallow of a lead; **made a fourth return on the day out of it, because the clause catches every finding of worked glass in four days and the day of the finding is not counted and the fourth day after the tenth of July is the fourteenth**; found a scarph between two ends cut to each other with nine fastenings in about seven feet at a hand's breadth apart, three chisel blows on every head and the same three blows on all nine, a packing that is not stone or oakum or lime or pitch pressed in from the seaward side over three inches of fouling, and a chip of the same worked glass put into the packing on purpose; **had a conservator of no office, in the harbor about a fortnight and unknown to anybody in this yard, prove six things about the join and refuse the seventh, which is who**; watched a man in the water read a seam for the first time in his life and then supply the age, the number and the hand of it out of his own head, and **say it out loud in a market in about eleven people's hearing, and be wrong in three parts out of four, and be disproved by fouling in two days by a bar laid flat and a scraper and a rule and two men's hands**; pay for that in a day bought for seventeen and half of it done, in a hired diver of another boat who went down because he was told to and is not doing it because of Tuesday, in a woman of the second lay who came up the hill to say the tide was there at seven and at two, and in the woman of this yard who is the reason there is a reader; **spend the one naming of the condition on the twentieth of July, in the second column, in his own left hand, with a reason, breaking his own line of the second of June, and the reason is that it can be argued with**; go into the market office for the first time in five months and find a builder's day-book with six places in it that are the six joints, a weir-book with a fisher's own storm in it, a poor-book with twenty-two children, and a tide-gang column that stops, and lay a string on the shed floor and get **three hundred and fifty-one feet and nine places of which six stand over a hole in a stone wall and three do not**; **decline the word, disown the word *chain*, and refuse in the second column to join the account about the sea to the finding about the glass**; **nail its own Crown attachment up on a market wall over a better printed sheet with no scale on it and no price on it, and tell a printer in a city three lines in advance in the ordinary post that it is coming and that he is to print what it says and not what it is about**; hear a woman of no office disagree with the holder in the open air in forty people's hearing and put her objection on the sheet unsigned and his answer beside it in nine words; **hear her say, before anybody asked her, that a yard that cannot pay her asks her whether she can be useful, and take that as the end of her time on this crew**; and be told, on a mole's steps, in his own words, that **a conservator he cannot pay is a conservator he has to keep asking and asking her to be useful is asking her to be cheap**; watch a reeve enter an examination of a mole's footing with no money behind it and close the third lay for four days, and hear the man who pays that price say the number out loud in a market and not ask for anything; **close the month with nothing in a bag and a wage column of fourteen lines and nine envelopes on a bench and not one of them anywhere**; and hear a man of the third lay say a boat's name out loud in the street — *Hearthwake*, working, with people in her, off the outer marks, one of the nine — **and write it down where anybody can check it, which is a page in a book in a shed on a hill, and not go, and not send anybody, and ask him no question, and say out loud that the outer marks stand where the writ says they are and the party is not going past them this season and has not tried and is not going to, and that that is not nothing and it is not enough and both of those are on the page.**

IT IS NOT AVAILABLE AGAIN IN THIS VOLUME OR ANY OTHER, AND THE NEXT BATCH MAY NOT PUT THE WORD IN.**

HE IS IN NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT IN A SHED, A BOAT, A MARKET, A MOLE OR A ROOM, NO DIGIT OF WHAT HE SAID ON THE SECOND OF JULY IS PRINTED IN ANY CHAPTER OF IT, AND THE CHEST WAS NOT OPENED AND WAS NOT BROUGHT DOWN THE HILL. - **AUTHOR-LEVEL DECISION, ON THE PAGE, BINDING — THE JOIN'S PHYSICAL FACTS** are set out in full in `state/continuity.md` § *Batch 0004 as written* § 8. **THE NINE FASTENINGS ARE NOT A MARK OF NINE JOINED LINES, THE NINE PLACES ARE NOT THE NINE HARBORS, AND NOTHING IN THE BATCH IS CALLED ANYTHING.**
- **FLAGGED, NOT APPLIED — the nine places and the three with no joint,** set out in the same § 8. A later volume may place them; this volume may not, and nothing in this batch connects the nine to anything under this town or to a road or to a name.
- **FLAGGED, NOT APPLIED — what the glass carries.** A conservator of no office has said in a market and in a shed that she cannot read it, that the trade which can costs six marks and two days, and that none of them has six marks. **No reading occurs, no echo is entered, and no chapter of this batch certifies anything a thing carries.**

THE CHANNEL IS THE WRIT, RULED ON THE PAGE ON WEDNESDAY THE FIFTH OF JULY, AND APPLIED ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH, AND NO SECOND CHANNEL MAY BE INVENTED.**

## Volume 03, Batch 0003 summary (Chapters 121–130) — Movement 3, the chart and the two men who want it

**Movement 3 is written and its turn has landed.** In twenty-one days a yard of two and a half men made a third return on the day and sent it up a coast in a sealed jacket with a copy for a ledger, and did not go and look at five miles of the coast it has published; said out loud on a mole's steps that it could neither produce the harbor authority's chart nor refuse it for anybody, and that the answer was not its to make; watched a reeve buy an uncontested instrument with nineteen winters of a herring skipper's dues and pay the price in a room with a clerk in it, and entered that it was in the room at the officer's request, produced everything, was asked for nothing, offered nothing and entered nothing; let a man from Ashtide nail a printed sheet over its own on a market wall and said out loud that the yard's own slip of eleven names, on that wall since the third of May for a shilling, was the only reason a stranger could print a sheet anybody could write to; **and said out loud, in a market, in forty people's hearing, that a refusal it had published on the seventh of June is the reason a crew with a compressor will be able to do a job it could have done for four marks on the tenth of June, and that the only reason it could not is that there was a boy who could hold a line and he is on a herring boat now.** It heard a coast office answer a fisher's document at last and put three of this harbor's own lines into a list. It answered three quarters of a stranger's question about a bar of gravel out of its own book and **refused, in writing and in public, to make itself able to answer the fourth, and entered the reason: a figure a yard has asked a man to stand behind is a figure the yard has published, and the day it does that it has made itself the man who takes a road off a chart, in its own hand, on its own wall.** It asked a man of fifty one question in a room in a boat, exactly as he said he would be asked, and **did not write down one stroke of what he said, and undertook in its own book never to ask again, and entered that he did not ask for money.** It declined to put a sheet on a wall it could have put a sheet on, and entered that this is the first thing it has written in four months about a thing it did not do.

**Actual word count: 33,731 words across ten chapters after the Batch 0003 review repairs, and 33,612 before them** (Ch121 3,945 · Ch122 3,175 · Ch123 3,842 · Ch124 3,502 · Ch125 3,193 · Ch126 2,886 · Ch127 3,317 · Ch128 3,262 · Ch129 3,129 · Ch130 3,487), measured with `wc -w` including headings, against the 2,200–3,200 guideline. **Every chapter is above the floor. Four are inside the guideline and six are past it** — Chapter 121 by 745, Chapter 123 by 635, Chapter 124 by 302, Chapter 130 by 287, Chapter 127 by 117 and Chapter 128 by 62 — **and every one of the four that ran ran because a cost could not be dropped: 121 is the third return in full, with the finding, both columns, the line of what it is not, the third bare-fact sound entry and a father at the far bench in the same shed; 123 is one hearing room that has to hold a writ, a crew's book, three returns, a paper and a price, and a chapter long because it is one complete room is a different fault from a chapter long because it is two; 124 is the turn and 130 is the close.** The hearing room is used **once**, on **Wednesday the twenty-first of June**, not a Monday, with a clerk in it, and no market wall on that day. The market wall is used **once**, on **Saturday the twenty-fourth of June**, in daylight, in a market, on no Monday and on no hearing-room day, **and the sheet that goes up on it belongs to another crew.** The batch's pressures alternate: a return and a clock, a market and an institution, a room, a rival, a woman and a wall, an office, a stranger's question, a private room, a reckoning, and a refusal to publish.

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: FOUR marks in a bag, thirty-one on the chandler's note, nothing in a tin, on Thursday the sixth of July — against EIGHT in the same bag on Thursday the fifteenth of June.** The chain is **8, 6, 2, 9, 5, 8, 4** across the seven days money moves. **A pot of air at the yard's own two-mark rate goes out on the nineteenth. A day at the second seam on the *Anna Beth's* own account brings seven in on the twenty-fourth — gross sixteen, nine out of it gone, the yard's seven, which is three more than the four the yard wrote on the mole's steps on the thirty-first of May for the same day of work, the difference being the pot that had gone out of the bag on the Friday and the rope this job did not need. A day at the second seam on a hirer's own account brings three in on the first of July, with nobody in the water.** Three wage weeks fall in the batch — the twentieth and twenty-seventh of June and the fourth of July — and each is four marks out of the bag into an envelope with the week written on it, and the column goes **eight lines and thirty-two marks – nine and thirty-six – ten and forty – eleven and forty-four**, with the fifth of March the oldest and staying there, and **six envelopes on a bench and not one of them anywhere, and the reason is on the page and the reason is that a wage is not a reason to go to a door.** The note is not re-written, its three counts of weeks do not move, five marks of compressor's gland stand on it unpaid and useless. **No money came in from any office in this batch and no money went out to any person except three wages, and a shipwright bought a rival crew's printed sheet for four marks out of her own hand, which is not the yard's money and is not in any column and is not going to be repaid.**

**Four things flagged rather than hidden, and one author-level decision taken on the page.**

- **THE BELLWRIGHT'S ONE QUESTION WAS ASKED, IN A ROOM, ON SUNDAY THE SECOND OF JULY, AND ANSWERED ONCE.** It was put to him in a doorway on the Saturday and not asked in the doorway; it was asked in the cabin of the *Anna Ray* with the door shut, the hatch open, four men present, no office and no seal and no ledger, and the chest not brought down the hill and not opened. **No digit is printed in any chapter of this batch and no figure goes into any column.** His three conditions were agreed in the room and the yard has undertaken in its own book not to ask again, and **that undertaking binds the yard and not the office and not the market and not the boy. NO LATER CHAPTER IN THIS VOLUME MAY ASK HIM AGAIN.** He did not ask for money, said so, and that he did not ask is entered.
- **THE CHANNEL BY WHICH A DISGRACED OFFICER REACHES A MORROW QUAY REEVE IS RULED, ON THE PAGE, WITH A DATE: IT IS THE WRIT.** Chapter 130, in Calder Marr's own left hand, in the yard's own book, on Wednesday the fifth of July. The writ's own last line says the second season is not this office's to give and will arrive out of a city from a man who has never been inside this harbor, and the holder will be told when it arrives and not before. **A man in a coat, of any office, disgraced or not, arrives as a stranger with a paper about that second season, and the yard will read it, will answer it on the day it comes, and will not treat him as a friend or as an enemy.** No new person, office or institution was created to carry it and no later volume may invent a second channel.
- **CAPTAIN HOLT'S POSTING AFTER HER DEFEAT IS EXPLICITLY STILL OPEN AND IS RECORDED AS STILL OPEN IN `state/open-threads.md`.** Her defeat is in Movement 5 and a posting cannot be decided before the thing it follows. **What Chapter 130 forecloses, in the yard's own hand, is what a posting may not be: no posting, appointment, commission, transport or instruction out of any city has put anybody past this harbor line, the outer marks and the bar of four hundred yards off them stand where the writ says they are and are not nearer, and this party is not going past them this season and has not tried and is not going to.**
- **FLAGGED, NOT APPLIED — the first request for the harbor authority's chart is referred to with no date, on purpose.** Chapter 122 says the yard was not in that room, did not hear it, has it from a man who was, **and has been able to establish no date for it and has not invented one.** Chapters 49 and 50 of Volume 01 record the request and the refusal and give no date.
- **FLAGGED, NOT APPLIED — two creditor figures held apart.** The cast list gives Sella Brigg and Edric Pringle each eight shillings and tenpence, and each about four hundred feet of her own warp on the bottom of this harbor. **Chapters 124 and 130 give the eight shillings and tenpence to BOTH women and a warp figure to ONE of them, and the two debts are never in one sentence and the two women are never merged.** An audit should rule whether the February event was one warp with two owners or two warps, and if two, where the second four hundred feet is stated.
- **FLAGGED, NOT APPLIED — an end entered on the ninth seam's mooring, the first of September.** It is a gain and it was entered at no cost to this harbor, which is unusual in this volume, and it is recorded so that a later volume does not mistake it for the notice having been lifted. **The notice of the thirty-first of October is not lifted, not narrowed and not altered, and no acknowledgement was entered, and a municipal mooring is not a person, a boat or a lead.**
- **The batch takes no power stage and does not name the condition.** It is on the page as the bare fact twice, with a reason against each line and a count of four against the fourth, and for the first time in another person's hand, **and the one naming Volume 03 is allowed therefore remains available and is owed to Movement 4.**

## Volume 03, Batch 0002 summary (Chapters 111–120) — Movement 2, weather and the work that cannot be sold

**Movement 2 is written and its turn has landed.** In twenty-two days a yard of two and a half men took a second glass storm and let a lump of glass get wetter rather than put a cloth to it, walked out to a harbor authority's sluice three times for nothing, named three recoveries and funded the smallest of the three out loud, refused a chain on ground a notice closes, priced a woman's own warp in front of her and put her name and a figure on a market wall, told a man of fifty-one out of a storm belt that it does not know who keeps a road and has never been there, agreed to be checked by him in the autumn, **did not put the best man in this harbor on a lead and could not write down the reason why**, entered the three nots about a boy of twenty-two in the first column and let the boy take a season's hand in a market, worked a day at the second seam on a herring boat's own account with a hired man in the water and a tender who is not a diver, **brought up a foot and a half of worked glass of nobody's in a net and put it in a crate in the open air and started a four-day clock**, did not go to the mole's toe on the twelfth of June, **and refused thirty marks in nine sentences on the fourteenth, which cost the town the third recovery.**

**Actual word count: 30,356 words across ten chapters as re-measured by the Volume 03 volume audit, and 30,345 before that audit's eleven mechanical repairs** (Ch111 3,464 · Ch112 3,263 · Ch113 2,522 · Ch114 2,739 · Ch115 3,266 · Ch116 3,107 · Ch117 2,534 · Ch118 3,051 · Ch119 2,937 · Ch120 3,473), measured with `wc -w` including headings, against the 2,200–3,200 guideline. **Every chapter is above the floor. Six are inside the guideline and four are past it — Chapter 112 by 63, Chapter 115 by 59, Chapter 111 by 264 and Chapter 120 by 273 — and all four ran because a cost could not be dropped: 111 is a night of weather with a two-column entry written at ten past two in the morning, and 120 is the batch's climax, which is one shed, one man, one paper, and a refusal that has to be nine sentences long and has to say out loud what the yard would take instead. No cost was dropped.** **The hearing room is used not at all: its slate wall comes down bare at eight on Monday the twenty-ninth of May, the fifth of June and the twelfth of June and on no other day, and there is no sitting on any of the three and the clerk has stopped mentioning it. The market wall is used once, on Wednesday the seventh of June, in daylight, in a market, on no Monday and on no hearing-room day.** The batch's pressures alternate: a storm and a rule that costs, a rota, money, method, discovery from outside, a public wall, an emotional consequence, work and a clock, a municipal recovery, and a refusal in a shed.

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: EIGHT marks in a bag, thirty-one on the chandler's note, nothing in a tin, on Thursday the fifteenth of June — against thirteen in the same bag on Wednesday the twenty-fourth of May.** The chain is **13, 13, 9, 9, 12, 12, 8, 8, 5, 12, 12, 8, 8, 8.** **Three wage weeks fall in the batch — the thirtieth of May, the sixth and the thirteenth of June — and each is four marks out of the bag into an envelope on the bench with the week written on it in Calder Marr's own left hand, because there is nobody else in that shed who writes; the envelopes are in the bench chest and not among the five rolled in oilcloth; none of them is sent anywhere that week and the reason is on the page and the reason is that a wage is not a reason to go to a door.** The column goes **five lines and twenty marks to eight lines and thirty-two marks, the fifth of March the oldest.** A day at the second seam on the pump hirer's own account brings three in; **a day at the second seam on the *Anna Ray's* own account brings seven in, and the pot of air and a hundred fathoms of hemp went out on the Friday, so the whole of that job left the yard four marks and not seven, which is the figure the yard wrote on the mole's steps on the thirty-first of May before anybody knew which of the two numbers was going to be the one.** The note is not re-written, its three counts of weeks do not move, **and a compressor's gland bought on credit in May is fitted to the yard's own pump and is still unpaid and has made no difference, because the thing after the gland is the hose.**

**Four things flagged rather than hidden, and four author-level decisions taken on the page.**

- **A wage that runs to a boy who is off the stone, into an envelope on a bench that is not carried anywhere.** It is consistent with the advance payment of the fifteenth and with the reason Batch 0001 gave for it, it is on the page in three chapters, it does not reduce the forty marks and is not offered as a reduction, and it is carried in `state/continuity.md` § 8 as a proposed canon change flagged rather than applied.
- **The yard's own boat hauled up on the mole's crown above the third seam's mark, and two objects of nobody's living on that crown for five weeks.** That is an application of the second clause and not an amendment of it, and the crown is landward of the third seam's mark and above the ground the first clause closes.
- **A cistern walk and a mooring's gear line on the harbor authority's own page at no figure, in a wharfinger's own hand, against the office's own interest.** The office has now recorded two things it did not pay for and a man who has not been paid for five pay periods. **It is a fact about an office's bookkeeping and it fixes nothing: the light is not on, the repair account is empty, the ninth seam is out of service with no end of it entered, and forty feet of the office's own marline is in the sea.**
- **The man of fifty-one's statement about coming to the mole is placed on Monday the twenty-second, at the top of the mole's steps, at ten in the morning, in the hearing of three men, and entered as a fact the yard learned on a day the yard names.** The card's *in a market on the fifteenth* is on no page and is not written as though a page said it.
- **The February warp and the Friday warp are dated and grounded on the page** — Tuesday the twenty-eighth of February off the mole's face between the first and second seams on a third lay boat's own account, and four feet of warp on a ring at the second seam on Friday the sixteenth of April belonging to a different boat of a different lay — **and the two figures for the bar out of a storm-belt pilot are two and a half and two against the sheet's two and three-quarters and two and a quarter, and the sheet's own figures are unchanged and unresolved and may only be resolved by the man coming back in the autumn.**
- **The batch takes no power stage and does not name the condition.** It is on the page as the bare fact twice, with a reason against it and nobody asking, **and the one naming Volume 03 is allowed therefore remains available and is owed to Movement 4.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 100

**VOLUME 02 IS CLOSED.** Movement 5 is written, the volume's climax is paid, and the volume's resolution is on the page. A wharfinger's fire took about four hundred feet of herring warp off the second lay's wharf and the hose with it; a glass storm came on the twenty-sixth of April and is in the second column with a reason against it and nobody may name a cause for it; a man of thirty-one who had gone down to the ninth seam's mooring without a permit and in a half sea was found alive in five fathoms off the inner shoals at eleven minutes, with a shackle in a hand that would not open, and five men were off that mole of whom not one was on the authority's work and a reeve's barge was committed into a half sea because it was the only boat the harbor authority has; **the cost was a compressor's gland, about ten feet of the yard's own delivery hose, the yard's hand lead's line, a claim window of one date that was worked and logged and raised nothing, two days' work and a pot of air three weeks standing that bought on the seventh of April and is now the whole of the air in this harbor.** The crew earned a **provisional writ with a Crown reporting clause attached to it** in the harbor authority's hearing room on Monday the first of May, **four names on it, the fourth being a hired diver who was asked in person, in a shed, and said he was content to have it**, and the yard took the clause and entered its objection unsummarized and said out loud that the act which made it trustworthy at home is the act that cost it in Veyr, **and that both of those are true and neither cancels the other.**

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: thirteen marks in a bag, twenty-three on the chandler's note, and nothing in a tin, on Wednesday the third of May.** The bag stood at nothing for five days from the afternoon of the twentieth of April, and it is a fortnight of bread on the twentieth that empties it; the tin was opened on the twenty-seventh for a shilling and sixpence of harbor-authority writ fee and emptied on the twenty-eight, **six marks came in on the twenty-eighth from the harbor authority at the yard's own four-mark rate for the claim window, which is the only money this harbor has paid that yard since the first of February, thirty marks came in on the twenty-ninth from four people who each said the cause out loud first and went straight out again — eight to the harbor's bellwright, sixteen to the boy, six onto the note — and the note came down a further four on Sunday the thirtieth out of a hat in a market, straight onto the creditor's page and never into the bag.** **The bellwright's eight marks are PAID and they are not one mark of the yard's own work. All sixteen marks of the boy's wage came out of four men's pockets and not one out of the yard's, and the boy left the fifth of March — the oldest line in the column — in it on purpose, and the column closes four lines deep at sixteen marks, the same figure and the same depth as on the thirty-first of March.** The forty marks of the claim stand whole. **The forty marks to Mara Venn are not paid, the market money did not touch them, and the writ's reporting clause cannot reach her and she says so in a hearing room before anybody is asked.** Eight shillings and tenpence to Sella Brigg stand undiminished and are unpaid, and about four hundred feet of her own warp is on the bottom of the harbor. **The chandler's note is NOT re-written and the yard says so out loud on a market wall, and the three counts of its weeks are twenty-two, thirteen and eleven as last written and none of them has moved since the fourth of January.** Twenty marks of shoal iron remain unsold, and a man of the south lay has offered nineteen for the stack and a shilling for the crown shackle with the saw kerf in it, separately, and the yard has taken neither.

### The active pressures going into Volume 03

1. **A writ with a four-day reporting clock on it, and a first return falling due.** Every finding of worked glass and every raising of material from claimed ground goes to the circuit office of this coast and to the officer of any vessel holding a claim in this harbor, with place, hour, keeper and limits, **and where a finding is disputed the harbor authority may seat one of the two men and take what a person says as it stands.** The writ runs to the first of March next, may be suspended after an inspection for cause by one man with a key and a book, **is not the Second Bell license, is not a charter, and renews nothing**, and its last line says the second season is not the harbor authority's to give and will arrive out of a city from a man who has never been inside this harbor.
2. **The circuit office's fourth request of the sixteenth of March is still unanswered and unrefused**, and the yard's position has changed underneath it: a party with an instrument can now say no inside an instrument.
3. **A lead plug with a number in it in a chest in a shed, described four times by four men who do not agree, in no book.** Two parts of a chain in a lead plug; a clean half-inch drilled hole; a number of which only a two and a bit of another one and a fourth that is not a two are visible; eleven inches under a bell at eight and a half feet. **The number is not written anywhere and the bellwright refused to say what it is, and he is not of this yard.** It is not connected to the plate dug on the mole's toe in February and the two must never be fused.
4. **The notice of the thirty-first stands whole, and a man nearly drowned inside it.** Three lines in the yard's book say he was not lawful there, that the notice did not save him, and that the yard will not say it did and will not say the notice was not worth the paper it is on.
5. **A glass storm, and nobody may name a cause for it.** It came through the water and not off it and it is in all of it.
6. **A bell that needs a boat.** Fouled, **a frame cut through the casting on one side, two parts of a chain in a lead plug where the tongue was, and no tongue on the frame at all** (the bellwright's own statement of the first of May, in the first column as a checkable fact; the standing phrase "a tongue half worn through" is withdrawn by the Volume 02 audit and may not be revived), a new rope bought on the eleventh of January, **eight marks and a day of a boat every four or five years, and the yard has told the four of them now so that there is no argument in four years.** The bellwright has refused on the page to make a repair of the chain in the plug or a finding of it, and has not been asked in a room, and Volume 03 inherits that refusal.
7. **The coast road, published in six hands in six boats, half-believed, and not resolved**, with a question about charts on a market wall and a refusal of the word *network* in public.
8. **Labor.** No air, no gland, no hose, a hand lead's line made badly at night, a bag that stood at nothing for five days, a note that went to thirty-three and is at twenty-three, a harbor authority with no boat of its own and a tide gang four men short and a cistern charged on a rota that a man does not walk, and a mole-head light that is not on.
9. **Neave Tarrant, of the third lay, nine winters, out since the twenty-eighth of February, not found**, and the yard has not gone and has asked nobody anything. **A man of fifty-one with a bad wheel who cannot place a sound and is not put on a lead and does not know why.** The *Sea Wren* at the pile. The hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November. Nineteen winters. The *Kittiwake* on the hard with no cradle.

### The relationship pressure

**Calder and Mara are at the end of five months of refusals and neither of them has broken.** She was asked for a figure for the third time in five months in April and refused identically in principle and newly in detail; he came within four inches of asking her what is in the anchor and did not, and was told by a shipwright that he has asked four people nothing this month. **In the hearing room on the first of May she said, before anybody asked her, that the writ cannot reach her and that she is not of it, and that she has a paper of her own going up the coast on her own account with three clauses about a false seal and a boat and three questions about a chart, and that she is not an assistant and is not going to be one this afternoon.** She holds the forty marks and the sentence of the twenty-second of March. **He did not spend a mark of the market money on her and did not offer and has not been asked to.**

**Calder and Bevin are at their closest and it is a good place and it is a dangerous one.** The boy is owed forty marks and sixteen marks of wage, **has entered a second omission of his own — that he has been to the fishery twice since the twenty-first of March and had his hand open the whole of both times and has not put that down — and called it an omission and entered both omissions in the same breath so that nobody can come in four years and say he hid one and not the other.** His hand is going, the yard said so out loud in a room in front of a clerk of the circuit office, **and he is to be off the stone on the fifteenth of May whatever his own arithmetic says, and the bonesetter's book still says a boat hand in June.** Nobody in that crew asks him one word about it, then or afterwards.

**Calder and Kest are at the end of the volume's own pattern and the reeve has paid six times in his own hand.** The sixth acknowledgement was on the twenty-seventh of April and was the second a party asked for. **The price of the writ is named out loud in a room: the ninth seam's mooring out of service from the first of May with no end of it entered, a tide-gang man stood off to mind a cart, and the statement that the yard is having the best of it.** He committed the office's only boat into a half sea and said what it cost before he did it. **He is not a friend and he is not to be softened, and his last act in this volume was to enter, in his own hand and at the yard's asking, a sentence about the reeve's own greed.**

**Calder and Alden do not move, and the volume closes on the not-moving.** The bench moves under the drip on the twenty-sixth of April and the two of them are in one room for nine hours in a gale and do not speak, and Calder Marr does not go over to him. **No fragment, no report talk, no second story, and no confession.**

### The power state

**Unchanged in rank.** Line Diver with an unstable tide-ear capacity used twice in Volume 01 and not used since. **No dive of his own and no entry of anything in Movement 5, no Bellwright, Keelwright, Storm-Reader, Chorus Diver or Openhand stage is taken and none may be.** What the volume paid is **a rescue and a going out, both of them done entirely by the method the volume built** — a reason entered before anybody is wet, two divers named as not of the party each fixing his own limit at the boat, a named tender who is not a diver and a cutoff he can pull without asking anybody, a pot of air read out on a mole in the yard's own words with the word *once* entered, three columns afterward with a reason against every line of the second and the third one carrying two different times, and four read-backs and a fifth man who was not asked. **The condition is not named in Movement 5 and the word is not used anywhere in Chapters 91–100.** The lead was a burn that came back hours after a rope came off a man's hand, in a leg, in five fathoms of water, and it is in the second column with a reason against it and no name attached to it.

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **No air in this harbor, no compressor gland, no delivery hose, and a hand lead's line being made by one man at night.**
- **The pot of air bought on the seventh of April is the whole of the air and is empty.** The pump is at the harbor authority's work and the yard's reason is in the office's book.
- **The ninth seam's mooring is out of service from the first of May with no end of it entered.** The north berth is out and took a sea on the night of the twenty-eighth with fifty fathoms of warp on it where ninety were to lie, and forty feet of the authority's marline is still in the sea. The third lay is full. **Petch is stood off the wall from the first of May to the tenth** and the mole steps will not be cleared in June. **The tide gang is four men short and the harbor authority's cistern is charged on a rota that a man does not walk, and the office has no boat of its own after the evening of the twenty-eighth until the barge comes back.** The mole-head light is not on and will not be. The *Kittiwake* is on the hard with no cradle. The hard at Ashtide is unanswered. Nineteen winters are disputed and unpaid.
- **A wage at four marks a week:** the first four weeks paid, **the ninth, tenth, eleventh and twelfth paid on Saturday the twenty-ninth of April out of the market, four lines and sixteen marks, and not one mark of the sixteen out of the yard's own work; the fifth to the eighth of March remain in the column and the fifth of March is the oldest line in it.** The column closes four lines deep at sixteen marks. The forty marks of the claim stand whole.
- **The bell is on the harbor's own ground in eight and a half feet off the south end**, fouled, with a frame cut through the casting on one side, **no tongue on the frame at all and two parts of a chain in a lead plug where the tongue was**, a new rope bought on the eleventh of January, **a delay out of the water off the south end that has not moved since the sixth of December, a going out on the second of May at eight marks and a day of a boat bought at a market, and a bellwright who has refused on the page to make either a repair or a finding of the chain in the plug and has not been asked in a room.** The eight marks are paid. There has not been a going out since the twenty-seventh of February before the second of May.
- **The delayed note: eleven logged occasions since the twenty-sixth of October, unchanged. Two occasions logged with no call, unchanged. No occasion is entered in this batch**, and the third column of the book says on the page why a figure taken on a flat calm is not an occasion and that a boy who has counted eleven is not going to make it twelve by writing a number. The answer inside the note remains reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint.
- **The coast road, the worked glass, the conservator's unsigned finding, the sixth hand-copied copy and the plate in a master's keeping** are all carried forward and all unresolvable inside this volume. **The road is published and half-believed and is not explained, is not named as a network, is not connected to anything under the town, and is not resolved.**
- **The concealment is hidden and the volume closes with it hidden.** The Oren mark is in no record, in no office, in no book and not in Kest's chart notation; the one false line on the unverified slate is still false and the slate was not moved; **the boy has not asked and has not been asked, and has entered a second omission of his own, and the holder came within four inches of asking the conservator again and did not; and the conservator with no standing has still never been asked and said in a room, unprompted, that the writ cannot reach her.** It was told once, in Chapter 38, and it is not told again.

## Volume 02 close — as AUDITED, and the Volume 03 handoff

**Audited 26 September 2026 in `reviews/volume-02/volume-02-close.md`.** That file is the volume audit and it supersedes the five batch accounts of themselves which appear below it. Nothing is owed to Volume 02 and nothing is owed to a chapter that has not been written.

**What Volume 02 answered, on the page, in the order the outline's own resolution requires it.** A provisional writ of salvage working, granted by the harbor authority on Monday the first of May, running to the first of March next, with **four names on it and a Crown reporting clause attached** and a four-day clock that has started. **Eight marks and a day of a boat paid to the harbor's bellwright**, out of four hands in a market and not one mark out of the yard's own work. **Sixteen marks of a boy's wage arrears paid out of somebody else's pocket**, four lines, and the fifth of March left in the column on purpose. **The yard's own debt to Mara Venn not paid, not paid out of the market money, and not reachable by the writ**, and she says so in a hearing room before anybody asks. **A Kest payment that cost somebody who is not the yard**: about four hundred feet of a woman's own warp off her own wharf, a mooring out of service with no end of it entered, and a tide-gang man stood off to mind a cart. **The chandler's note not re-written, said out loud on a market wall on the third of May**, with its three counts of weeks unmoved since the fourth of January. **Six hand-copied copies in six hands of six boats, none of them the yard's, and a refusal of the word *network* in public and a question about a man with a pen on the wall in its place.** **A man found alive in five fathoms off the inner shoals, and the notice that closed his ground is not lifted and is not going to be argued.**

**The volume's central pressure is resolved, and resolved in the opposite direction to the opening.** The leash did not shorten: it lengthened, acquired a name and four persons, and now carries a reporting clock and a Crown signature. **The volume's own sentence for it is in Calder Marr's mouth in the hearing room on the first of May and is the better sentence, and the outline is not amended: the yard is the most reliable crew in this harbor and it has cost a hand lead, a hose and a claim window, and the writ we got for it is a leash with our names on it, and both of those are true and neither cancels the other.**

**Two clauses of `outline/volume-02.md` were discharged in a different form, and both are RULED by the audit.** The **climax**: there was no charter to abandon, because the charter had expired on the thirty-first of March, so there was no official route to abandon; it was one man and not a crew; the glass storm is the twenty-sixth of April and the rescue is the twenty-eighth in an easing north-northeast; the paid official route was **interrupted rather than abandoned**; and **no salvage award was ever claimable, because nothing was raised, and a clerk's box cannot hold the difference between a window that was worked and a window that was missed.** The **resolution**: the coast road is published in six boats and the word *network* is used once, by a rival, and refused in public, and what is on the wall is a question about a man with a pen. **Neither clause is an unspent debt and no later phase may read either as one.**

**Six state-file figures with nothing standing behind them were corrected, and two of them are material:** Batch 0002 is **31,300 words and not 30,995**; the bag stood at nothing for **five days and not seventeen**; **the six marks of the claim window's day rate did reach the bag** on the twenty-eighth; **the bell's tongue is not on the frame** and the phrase "a tongue half worn through" is withdrawn; and **no batch review log cited anywhere in the state files has ever existed** — `logs/` holds only `close.log` and `models.log`, fifteen false citations naming Batches 0001, 0002, 0004 and 0005 are withdrawn, and the authority for every Volume 02 review finding is `state/continuity.md` § *Batch 000N review repairs*.

**Ten mechanical repairs were applied in place, in Chapters 62 and 69, all of them the same defect: Edric Pringle is a woman and two chapters called her *he*.** The state files recorded seven wrong pronouns in three places; the true count is **ten, in four places**, and every one is corrected on the page.

**Volume 03 begins here, and inherits by name:** the writ and its four-day reporting clock and the ground it names and the one office that may renew it; the second season as a named absence; the sixth-lay finding, which **does not exist** — the volume's findings are in the second and third lays and no chapter of Volume 02 names a sixth lay; the two Slees, hired on the twenty-eighth of April and not used since; the lead plug in the chest; the glass storm and the ban on naming a cause; the six hand-copied copies in six boats; the question about charts and the refusal of the word *network*; the notice of the thirty-first and the man in five fathoms; **the ninth seam out of service and the eighth-clause plan for the fifth seam still unanswered and still to be reached by a change of politics in an office**; the hard at Ashtide; the coast office's word *capacity* and Elias Voke's statement; the *Sea Wren* at the pile and Noll Tarner; the fourth request of the sixteenth of March; the gland and ten feet of hose the yard owes for air; **the boy off the stone on Monday the fifteenth of May and the bonesetter's June**; the ninth seam's mooring, the north berth, the warp and forty feet of the authority's marline in the sea; the mole-head light and the empty repair account; the cistern on a rota; the fire party's dead hose; and **Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found.** All of it, with twenty-eight locks and the calendar re-derived day by day, is in `outline/volume-03.md`.

## Volume 02, Batch 0005 summary (Chapters 91–100) — Movement 5, the rescue and the writ. **VOLUME 02 IS CLOSED AND AUDITED.**

**Movement 5 is written, the volume's climax is paid, and the volume's resolution is on the page.** In sixteen days the Free Keel yard was asked for a pump and had none, lost four hundred feet of a woman's warp and its own hose to a fire, watched a glass storm come through the water and wrote down what it did in the second column with a reason against it, bought an air pot three weeks standing and read its age out loud on a mole before anybody was wet, put five men off that mole, none of them of the authority's work, and a reeve's barge into a half sea with them, **got a man out of five fathoms in eleven minutes and lost a compressor's gland, ten feet of hose, a hand lead's line and a claim window of one date doing it**, took **thirty marks from four people who each said the cause out loud first** and paid it straight out again, **was granted a provisional writ with a Crown reporting clause and four names on it and said in a room that the act which made it trustworthy at home is the act that costs it in Veyr and that both are true**, looked after a bell for the first time since the twenty-seventh of February, copied a coast road in six hands that are not the yard's, and put a tenth thing on a market wall under a naval paper and said out loud that the chandler's note is not re-written.

**Actual word count: 33,327 words across ten chapters** (Ch91 2,791 · Ch92 2,529 · Ch93 2,972 · Ch94 3,211 · Ch95 3,931 · Ch96 3,435 · Ch97 3,978 · Ch98 3,524 · Ch99 3,136 · Ch100 3,820), measured with `wc -w` including headings after the review repair, against the 2,200–3,200 guideline. **Every chapter is above the floor. Four are inside the guideline and six are past it**, the largest Chapter 97 at about twenty-four per cent over and Chapter 95 at about twenty-three; **every chapter past the guideline is one complete room or one complete day, and three of them carry more than one room on that day — Chapter 92 is the shed and the market, Chapter 98 is the net loft, the mole's steps and the shed, and Chapter 100 is the boards and the dock — which is a shape fact and is now recorded as one instead of being denied.** **The hearing room is used twice, once for the office's own ledger on Thursday the twenty-seventh and once for the one sitting on Monday the first of May, and the market wall is used once, on Wednesday the third of May, and no two of the three are the same day.** The batch's pressures alternate: a fire and a warping, a hand and a market, weather, an office and a paper, the water and a rescue, money and four causes, a sitting, a bell, a going out and six hands, and a wall.

**The money, and it closes checkable on the page: thirteen marks in a bag, twenty-three on the note, nothing in a tin, on Wednesday the third of May.** The full chain is in `state/continuity.md` § *Batch 0005 as written* and in the prose of Chapters 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98, 99 and 100. **The bag stood at nothing for five days from the afternoon of the twentieth of April, the tin was opened once and emptied, and the only money this harbor has paid that yard since the first of February is the six marks of the claim window's day rate, which came in on the twenty-eighth and is still in the bag.** The three counts of the note's weeks are unmoved since the fourth of January and the note is not re-written. **All sixteen marks of wage came out of other men's pockets and not one out of the yard's own work, and the boy left the oldest line in his column in it on purpose.**

**Two things flagged rather than hidden.** **The yard is now the most reliable crew in this harbor and it owns no air, no gland, no hose, a hand lead's line it is making badly, a claim window it worked and raised nothing on, and a lease on a reportable paper.** And **the batch makes no canon change**: the only author-level additions are a discipline — the provisional writ is defined on the page and is not a charter and renews nothing, the yard's practice gains a third column for what the boy said when he was not in the boat, and the counts do not move with the calendar, including the rule that a figure taken on a flat calm is a figure and not an occasion. **Two clauses of `outline/volume-02.md` are discharged in a different form than the outline describes, and both are flagged for the audit in `state/continuity.md` § 9 rather than left for it to find: the climax is one man and not a crew, in an easing wind three days after the glass storm, with nothing raised and therefore no salvage award ever claimable; and the resolution refuses the word *network* in public and puts a question about a man with a pen on the wall instead.** **One inherited defect was recorded for the audit and has now been RULED AND REPAIRED by it: Edric Pringle is a woman, and Chapters 62 and 69 called her *his* — the seven occurrences the state files recorded were in fact ten, in four places, and the audit corrected every one of them mechanically in place. See `reviews/volume-02/volume-02-close.md` Part 2, item 1.**
